Time consuming but pretty good dish.  The chili pods definately add a kick to the dish.  My one suggestion would be to add a couple veggies such as green onions, broccoli and carrots.  I served it with a basmati recipe.  Thanks for the posting.

This dish is absolutely delicious.  It tastes just like or better than the restaurant's.  Very time consuming; frying is always messy.  Next time I will saute chicken, instead of frying.  A very good recipe and worth making!

Holy smokes.....I never thought this could be made at home. This is the best General Tso Chicken I think I have ever had. It is a little messy to make but not dificult at all. I highly recommend you give this recipe a try.......OUTSTANDING!!!!
This was phenomenal!! I didn't have any rice wine, so I just used regular cooking wine and it turned out wonderful.  I did double the sauce as suggested, and that was perfect.
LOVE, love this recipe! It is so easy to make.

Now this was really nice! We dont have General Tso's here in Oz so I dont have anything to compare it with, but I loved the blended flavours. I took Puckheads advise and used chicken breast and it was devine! Definately a recipe that sticks in your head if your looking to do something with chicken. Well done Mean chef!!!!

This was fantastic !  Just as good, if not better, than restaurants. I used chicken tenderloins that I had in the freezer and cut them up into bite size pieces. I cooked this all at once, but if you were to do the 1st stage frying ahead of time, this recipe is a quick, no brainer. Loved it, Loved it, Loved it. But...I expect nothing less from Mean Chef's recipes.

Made this last night.....just as good as the restaurants. Loved it, thanks so much for posting...i used boneless and skinless chicken breast and cut into little chunks..I also used chili powder, just a few sprinkles..... instead of chili pods....worked out fine for me... and was very easy to make....one of my new favorite recipes....thanks again:)

Yummy recipe! I love the sauce. This was very easy to make. I mixed everything up before starting to cook. Then just dipped and fried. The only change I made was to add 1/2 tsp of garlic powder to the sauce. Excellent! I'm definitely making this again.
Thank you so much for sharing.

This is so very good.  I wasn't sure about the cornstarch breading but it was fantastic.  I made this with #38748 Chinese Fried Rice and it was a very satisfying meal for us.  Thank you for this great recipe......Stephanie
144 raves, what went wrong? I tripled the sauce and it was so salty!! I mean way to salty. I think it should have dark brown sugar instead of white sugar. This was thumbs down! YUCK!

This out of all the versions ive tried to make was the absolutely the best one as far as for the breading of the chicken & sauce i  still used another for the sauce recipe as it  was  milder (for KIDS) though but TWO THUMBS WAY UP!!!!! the sauce i used was this 1/2cup cornstarch 1/4cup water 1 1/2 teaspoon of garlic&ginger 3/4 cup sugar 1/2 soy sauce 1/4 cup vinegar&sherry wine one 14 oz can of chicken broth made this the BEST GENERAL TSO"S better by far than the restraunts but if  u  like  it double spicy use   this sauce   but  double  it .... ADULTS  ONLY LOL

Great recipe! I used balsamic vinegar in place of rice vinegar. I found the rice wine in the Asian foods and spices section of the grocery store. I doubled the sauce recipe, and had just enough sauce, so I recommend doing that. It tasted like my favorite Chinese restaurant's General Tso, Chef Peng.
I love this recipe!  I will make it again and again and again!
Made this last night for the first time. This was outstanding! Easy to make. I used boneless chicken breast as opposed to the chicken thighs.

I have never heard of General Tso but my family really enjoyed this dish!  I found it to be a bit salty so next time I will slightly reduce the soy sauce.  I also used chicken breasts and served it over rice noodles and steamed broccoli.  It was even better the next day for lunch.  Thanks for sharing!!

My BF loves General Tso's chicken and orders it every time we order out Chinese.  I had never thought about trying to make it...but I am glad I did.  It was so much easier than I thought it was going to be and the taste was right on the money...according to him.  I did cook the sauce a little too long at the end when it was carmelizing, so make sure you watch it carefully because it really does only take 1-2 minutes TOPS.  Thanks for sharing this yummy recipe!

Trying to make this dish healthier, I cut up boneless skinless chicken breast and cooked in a lightly oiled wok, skipping the breading and deep frying step.

The rest of the recipe was made as called for. I believe the recipe is written incorrectly for step #10 it doesn't say to remove the chicken when adding the sauce. My sauce came out to grainy either because of this failed step or there maybe to much cornstarch in the recipe. Next time I make this I will make sure I remove the chicken, add the sauce for 1-2 minutes, then add the chicken back to coat.
This is absolutely wonderful.  My guys love it.  Thanks for sharing.

This dish is absolutely phenomenal. I cooked it at work but I was worried there wouldn't be enough for everyone cause i couldn't stop picking at it. I had to more than double the chicken cause I was feeding an army so I doubled the egg mixture but there was heaps left over so I won't need to double it next time. I only made 1 1/2 times the sauce but I think doubling it would have been ok. I didn't add the chili's because we are not big chili fans but it was great without it. I will definately be making this one again...probably this weekend. With the presentation and flavour you would think you just spent heaps of money buying it from a Chinese restaurant. 
Thanks for a yummy recipe Kirstin!

I love this recipe. It's way better than buffet or fast food Chinese places. It's fairly simple to make. I've made it with thigh meat and breast meat.  I think the thigh meat is better! and of course I've tweaked the recipe a little. I use 3 egg whites and 1 yolk because I don't like that egg-y taste, and use 1/3 cup all-purpose flour instead of cornstarch for the "batter" which I find leaves almost no remaining batter with 1 1/2 lbs of meat. Like others I double the vinegar and wine, change the sugar to splenda and increased by 1 TBS. Also increased the soy sauce by 1 TBS. I found the chili pods burn too fast, so if on hand I roast ancho peppers and you really smell their aroma in the oil. Then disgard them and contine as the recipe says. I also use red pepper flakes to reach desired spicy-ness. Thanks for posting!!

Fantastic!! Comes out very impressive, just like you would get at a nice restaurant.  I followed the suggestions below and amped up the vinegar and wine, and then doubled the sauce as follows:  4 tsp cornstarch, 6 tbl rice vinegar, 8 tbl rice wine, 6 tbl sugar, and 8 tbl soy sauce.  It was WONDERFUL.  I paired it with Fried Rice #8594.  

Thanks, Kirstin!!

Outstanding!
Like others I doubled the sauce although next time I would make a little less than double. The sauce proved a little too bland even after a little garlic and the chilies so next time I would kick it up a bit.

It is an abomination that I waited this long before trying this out, hence depriving my kids with a sensational dish that they absolutely enjoyed. Followed the recipe faithfully, but I used chicken breasts instead. Thank you so much for sharing.

Outstanding!! I'd rate this higher if I could. It tasted exactly like General Tso's chicken at a Chinese restaurant. The sauce amount was perfect for us. I wouldn't change a thing. I recommend prepping everything before you set out to cook (make the sauce, mix the cornstarch & beaten eggs, cube the chicken, start the rice, etc...). I searched high and low for rice wine and finally found it at Kroger. I think this would be a great entertaining dish along with egg rolls, rice, steamed veggies, almond & fortune cookies! I'm anxious to try making it up through the stage 1 frying, refigerate & when guests come, do the second stage frying. 
Delish recipe...MUST TRY!

I loved this recipe. My husband and i Love chiness food and its so great to be able to make some at home that tastes like all the great resturants and some times better. I used chicken tenderlions insead of thighs because i cut them in 3rds and they were the perfect size. And instead of using chili pods I subsituded red chili flakes. Remember to add just a little becasue they pack some heat. This recipe is the best!!!!!

I got admit. When i first read this recipe i didn't think it looked that great. Without the positive reviews i thought way the hey i will make it. I also has almost all the ingredients on hand so that helped. The only two minor changes i made is i didn't have rice wine so i had a choice between sherry and white wine. I thought sherry sounded more traditional ( ive seen it in other recipes) so thats what i substituted. Also instead of dried chilies i used fresh DeArbol chilies from the garden. Everything else i went by the recipe. I have tried a lot of tso chicken recipes that i found online and a lot of them were horrible. This is the best i have yet made. It doesn't mean though it was perfect. It wasn't good as my favorite general tso place where i live. What changes would i make next time? At least double the sauce ingrediants. There was not nearly enough sauce for me otherwise i would probably leave it as is.

The first couple times I made this, I made it exactly as directed it was really good, but not quite as good as our favorite Chinese place. This time I added 1/2 tsp garlic powder to the sauce and it made all the difference; it was just right. I serve it with fried rice; they go very nicely together. Thanks.
Loved it!!!
Living in Sicily, it is hard to find decent chinese food.  This recipe was great!  Could not find the chili pods, so I used crushed red pepper instead.  Turned out wonderful!

This is amazing.  I usually make it without the first stage frying.  We don't get General Tso's chicken in the UK, but my partner thinks this is better than what he's tried in the States.  Thanks so much!

Fabulous recipe!  My hubbie is a General Tso snob, and he thought it was wonderful.  Wasn't sure how long to cook the chili pods, so I probably did not leave them in long enough [afraid they would burn].  The sauce carmelized beautifully...next time I will double the sauce, not enough for us to eat with our rice.  The sauce makes just enough to stick to the chicken.  
A great recipe!!

Very good recipe! I was hesitant to try it at first but I am glad I did. It is a family favorite! The only thing I did differently was make more suace.Frying of the chiken is my least favorite part of this recipe I have made it 6 times now

A definite keeper! I love the sauce, although it could use a little more spice. The chili pods I put in didn't add any heat to it. Will also remember to use chicken thighs. I used chicken breast, so it was a little tough, but great nonetheless!

not hot enough for me but WONDERFUL flavor. I ended up having to sub merlot for rice wine, but the sauce was to die for. I think next time I will try to cut out some fat by baking the chicken and then stir frying with the sauce. Great stuff. I give 5 stars without a doubt. Better than what you get in the restaurant.

This recipe is Awesome!! No need to order out for General Tso's anymore. Just a couple of minor tweeks. Boneless, Skinless, Chicken Thighs rule!!!  Learned that "Sake" (rice wine) was on the shelf at my local grocery store. Substituted 2 tbsp. chili paste for the chili pods. And, make sure to double the sauce...you won't be sorry. Served with Perfect Short-Grain White Rice by Listening (Japanese, Korean, C Recipe #108409 ..the most awesome rice recipe) and served with Pan-Roasted Broccoli Recipe #155018. Nirvana!!!

Good recipe! Used chicken breast and didn't have dried chili pods, so just used pepper flakes as another reviewer did.  Worked fine. I didn't add all the oil, just a little in the bottom of the pan.  Mine didn't turn out as pretty as Shasha's picture, but it tasted delicious! Thanks for adopting Mean's great recipe!

This is really, really good! I loved the combination of taste from the wine and the vinegar, and the hint of spiciness we get in our mouths! For the rice wine i used Shao Hsing Hua Tiao, which has a lovely smell. I used white chinese rice vinegar and about 6 dried chillies, which was the right amount. Everybody loved it and i'll be making it again and again soon! THANK YOU!

With 171 ratings, you probably don't really need one more, but I have to tell you that this is a most delicious chicken recipe.  I didn't have rice wine, so I used a very good white wine and followed the recipe as directed.  Served it with jasmine rice and a steamed mixture of buttered and seasoned broccoli, carrots and cauliflower.  It has been requested as a repeat in my household.  Thank you, Mean, for sharing the recipe and Kirstin for looking after it in his absence.
Use a gluten-free soy sauce or a gluten-free tamari sacue and this recipe is suitable for a gluten and lactose free diet :)

Time consuming but fabulous! I quadrupled the recipe and used Mexican dried red chilis cut in half, seasoned rice vinegar, and cooking sherry in place of rice wine. Served with broccoli and sushi rice. Rave reviews from everyone. I served it for a party of six and they ate it ALL! If you're making this recipe for more people, after you've done the first and second-stage frying in batches, put the finished chicken on a roasting pan and warm in the oven at 185 degrees. THEN get a huge bowl and add the sauce right before you serve.

General Tso's is one of my DH favorites, so I thought I would give this a try.  His response; "this is the best General Tso's I have ever eaten!"
I substituted chicken breast for the thighs, used about 4 t. of szechwan chili sauce (my store does not carry dried chili pods), used Splenda and used Marsala instead of the rice wine. I felt it was okay for me to rate still since the substitutions are close the original and the integrity of the dish was not lost.  Definitely a keeper!

Wonderfully easy and quick to prepare. My family loved it. The kids were picking on the chicken before I got the sauce on, and raved about how yummy that was.  I will use this tempura chicken to make sweet and sour chicken with sesame. Highly recommend this recipe

My daughter made this for dinner and their were no leftovers.  While it's time consuming it is worth it.  We ended up using extra rice vinegar since we had no rice wine and we used red pepper flakes for the dried chili pods(the girls don't like really hot food).

Wow!  This was as good, if not better than from the restaurant.  I followed the recipe exactly.  It was quite mild, but I have little kids, so that worked for us.  I more than doubled the recipe and after our family of 5 got through, there were no leftovers.  YUM!  If you like it spicy, you might want to add a few more peppers.
This was great! I used the wrong kind of peppers, but I won't let my mistake stand in the way of this awesome chicken! It looked like something we had ordered out. :D
Double or tripe the sauce. Otherwise don't change a thing.

This should probably be two stars, but since I've only made it once, I'm giving it three.  I had high expectations reading the reviews, and while the chicken itself was done just right, the sauce was definitely substandard from what you'd get in a restaurant.  I made it exactly according to the recipe, except I added 3 more chili pods.  I still didn't get any heat from them, and the flavor was basically sweet soy sauce.  It wasn't bad at all, but it wasn't General Tso's as I know it and love it.  I'll be trying a different recipe next time, but thanks for posting.  It was fun to give it a try!

Fabulous.  I didn't have rice wine, so I replaced it with gin.  I also used only egg whites instead of whole eggs.  It turned out just wonderfully, and I got the green light from DH to make this the only General's recipe I make from now on!  Thanks!

General Tso's chicken is the only thing my wife and I get when we go out for chinese and we are very particular about it.  In fact, we've only found one place that makes it very well.  The rest range from so-so to gross.

I have tried making at least 6 different generals recipes and we just can't find one we like.  I used sherry like one of the reviewers mentioned in place of the rice wine but followed the recipe to the letter for the rest.  The sauce came out rather bland and got worse the more you ate.  Still looking...
Very Good!
i made this for my anniversary of 24 years my husband loved it.
This was absolutely fabulous!  We've never tried a General Tso's recipe before and now we won't ever need to look for another recipe.  A definite 'make again'.

Very good and yummy. really love it. my husband really loves the unique sweet and sour taste from it. 
really like it. will make it again. thanks for the recipe.

I love the fact that the first stage of frying the chicken can be done in advance as that part can be a bit time consuming, but the dish is SOOO delicious that I'd like to make it often. After the sauce is made and first stage frying is done, it is really easy to throw this recipe together for a quick weeknight meal that everyone will love! I did 1.5 X the chicken (used boneless, skinless thighs) but tripled the sauce and there was not too much sauce. Thanks for the nice detailed instructions Kristin as it made my first try at Chinese so simple! I will be making this often.
Thank you for this recipe.  My husband loved it and it was so easy.
I can't believe I didn't rate this recipe. This will be my 4th time making it. Perfectly delicious!!! If I could give it 10 stars I would. Thanks for sharing.

This was really delish!!! I used chicken breasts and tripled the sauce...hmmmm! I added a tsp of garlic to the sauce and used a tablespoon of red pepper flakes instead of the chili pods. Incredible recipe...the kids want it once a week!!!
Good recipe!!  The sauce for the chicken is a little strong.  I watered it down a bit.  Other than that it is much better than any other General Tso's I've had in Chinese restaurants.
my husband loved this recipe!

My picky DS loved this!  I was too tired to drag out my whole dried peppers, so I just used the pepper flakes.  Also I used boneless, skinless chicken breasts.  The only thing I would do different next time is double or even triple the sauce.  Also, I did not have rice wine, so I subbed water with just a tidge of lemon juice.  Thanks for sharing this!
Excellent.  But, I tripled the sauce and added two teaspoons chopped ginger.  Not as spicy as I had thought, added a little jalapeno juice this time, will add a serrano pepper or two next time.
Takes time but very good. I'd double the sauce next time.

So many reviews already, but might as well make it one more.  YUMMMMM!!!  I used chile bean paste instead of chili pods, and took the advice of others and doubled the sauce and added green onions.  I only fried once, so my chicken wasn't as crispy...sadly.  Next time I'll do the two-step frying.  I'd probably give this 6 stars if it had turned out crispy!
Substituted New Mexican red chiles (Bueno's), and boneless chicken breasts.  GREAT!.  Thanks for posting.
I've been trying to find a recipe for General Tso's chicken that we all like. Up until now, the others we've tried have all been so so. However, this absolutely rocked. My kids loved it!
Hmmm...made this for dinner last night.It was yummy!!I this is a really simple dish to make. I added in some roasted cashew nuts as well. This dish is definitely a keeper!! Thanxs for the recipe!!

This gets a triple 5 stars rating from my entire family.  It's to die for!  I added some grated gingerroot on the sauce. Decreased the sugar (personal preference)  and cooked the batter just using 1 large egg.  Will make it again VERY SOOON!

Loooooooove it!    I used 2 eggs instead of 3 and just 1 chili pod. DOUBLED the sauce mix for more glaze but just used 5T sugar. Peeeerfection! Will make this again on Sunday when my sister comes with her boyfriend!
Simply the best!

A thousand thanks for this recipe, Kirsten!  It's in my top five recipes!  I used 1 1/2 rounded tsp. chili paste instead of the pods and chicken breast instead of thighs.  I doubled the sauce like others suggested.  My husband thought it was a little sweet (I adjusted it for him, as per usual), but I loved it!!!!
Whoa!!! AAA+ 5 star all the way!!  Easy and tasty, doubled the sauce like others suggested.  A keeper!

This came out great!  My only regret is that I meant to double the sauce and forgot so it didn't cover the rice & steamed broccoli.  But the chicken came out fantastic!  I will definitely make again. Thanks for the recipe!

although this doesn't taste exactly like the general tso's i'v tried...it was really good! i doubled the sauce which i regretted because it almost tasted a little salty. and my kids mentioned they didn't want extra sauce on their chicken. so next time i'll listen to the chef's direction and not double. my husband enjoyed this so much that he emailed me while at work to say how "really good" the lunch was. he never does that plus he's so darn picky! so i'll put this in his favorites file. next time tho i'll add a little more sugar or brown sugar to make it a little sweeter since that's what i'm used to. thank you for sharing a wonderful recipe!

Excellent chicken dish!  From the first mouthful I was hooked!  This is one of the tastiest dishes I have had in a long time.  I doubled the recipe to have enough for leftovers, and it came out great!  Chicken was very tender and the flavors were perfect. I will be making again and again here!  Thanks for sharing your recipe with us Kirstin!  Becky

EXCELLENT!!!  I give this 5+ stars and my son gives it 5 stars, so that means 10+ stars for this one :)  We truly enjoyed this recipe.  The flavor was great and the meat was nice and tender.  We used chicken thighs and breast and doubled the recipe and sauce.  We had enough left over for one lunch, so I would have to say it only serves 2 if you don't eat like a bird! I will be passing this one along to family and friends and will be making often.  We LOVED it!!!  Thanks for adopting Mean's recipe and sharing it with us Kirstin!

Very good.  I didn't have rice wine so I used cooking Sherry and the flavor was still wonderful.  The dried chili pods didn't add nearly enough spice for me so I added crushed red pepper flakes too.  Will definitely make this again!  My 2 year old loved it too.  She said, "Mmm...de-wish-ous!"
Good Stuff ! I also added the crushed red flakes. The rice does'nt get enough sauce in it though.Doubling or maybe tripling the sauce is the way to go.  Thanks

We loved this in our house! I also used boneless chicken breast and red pepper flakes and it was still delicious.  I also doubled the sauce and honestly could have tripled it because it was delicious with rice.  

I thought this would be really time consuming but it honestly was very easy.  I did the first fry in advance and then when the rice was close to done I did the second fry.

The only tricky thing was making sure the chicken was actually done cooking on the first fry.

I will make this again and again because it was amazing.  There are no good chinese restaurants here so this was a really welcome meal for us!

Yummy recipe! My husband said "Let's have this again!" as he went for THIRDS. I used boneless chicken breast too, yum. For the chili peppers, I used dried Santaka Chili Pods (Japones) - the long skinny red ones. They worked great. I also used sherry b/c I didn't have rice wine (where do you get this?) and I doubled the sauce recipe. It could have used even more sauce - I love the sauce. Be sure to let the sauce cook after you add it b/c it's the carmelizing sugar that gives the General Tso it's yummy texture. And I followed another poster's idea and added some green onions. I recommend having everything arranged before starting to cook - mix up the cornstarch/eggs and also the sauce. Then the cooking goes much faster. We're definitely having this again. UPDATE: I find that if I cook the sauce in with the chicken, the chicken loses its nice crunch. Now I take the chicken out when it's cooked, then put in the sauce and get it nice and thick with the carmelized sugar, and then pour it over for serving.

What a pity...we can't give occasional 10 stars to recipes! This is very good, with a flavorful sauce. It is not too hot (if you want it hot, chop up some of the chili pods). I suggest using Chinese rice wine (I use Shao Xing brand). The only problem I had was not the recipe's fault--my glass-top stove is just terrible for stir-frying over, so it didn't really crisp up like it should have. Next time I may take DH up on his offer to stir-fry outdoors over his portable gas stove!

Loved it!  What can I say that hasnt already been said?  This dish is easy to prepare and has great flavor.  We chopped up one of the chili pods (used Thai dragon chilis) and left the other 4 intact to give the dish some heat.  I will definitely double the sauce next time.  Thanks for this keeper.
This was a great recipe.  I used chicken breast but was delicious!  Served with Perfect rice  Recipe # 53520 and  Oven Roasted broccoli Recipe # 206184.  Great Meal!

This turned out great!  Using some of the reviews I did change things up a bit.  I couldn't find chili pods so I used 1 tablespoon of crushed red pepper flakes in the sauce.  I also tripled the sauce recipe using 5 tablespoons of cornstarch. I will follow the review next time and use only 4 because the sauce did get extremely thick.  Husband, daughter, niece and I all loved this.  
Thanks for a keeper!

This chicken is awesome. I have fixed it many times in the last few months. My husband (the pickiest man in the world) asks for it all the time. It does take a while to fix, so sometimes I wish he wouldn't ask for it, but once it is on the table, the taste is worth it! I have only used chicken tenderloins and it turns out great. I also use white wine for the rice wine, and most of the time i will double or triple the recipe, but I sometimes cut back on the sugar when I do that, once my husband mentioned it was too sweet. But, nonetheless a WONDERFUL recipe!!

Wow!  So good!  This is my husband's favorite, he's addicted.  I followed the recipe almost exactly, but I did add more spice and a little bit more soy sauce to it.  I added a couple of dashes of powdered cayenne pepper.  We loved it that way, a little kick is always good in my family.  My husband doesn't like sweet meat too much, so I added about another Tbsp of soy sauce to the mix.  This is a keeper, thank you for the recipe.

I must be a terrible cook because this didn't work out for me :(  What I did differently was use red pepper flakes in place of the chili pods, use Tio Pepe sherry in place of the rice wine (couldn't find it anywhere) and I also added a dab of minced garlic and ginger; otherwise I followed the recipe exactly.  I fried in a typical frying pan because I do not have a wok, so that could be the partial cause of my problems.  The sauce didn't taste anything  like General Tso's to me, the sherry taste came through VERY strongly.  I used two tablespoons of sherry (since the recipe states 2 tablespoons of rice wine) but perhaps I should have reduced it.  I don't know ANYTHING about sherry so perhaps I got a bad brand or used the wrong type of sherry or something (it was an extra dry sherry).  Also, the sauce almost seemed kind of gritty and definitely didn't have the right texture.  I am assuming this is because I used a frying pan...It was a little difficult to swirl all the chicken around in the sauce.  I'm DYING to be able to enjoy this recipe since I'm sure it's a good one with so many wonderful reviews.  I'd be so appreciative if there was someone that could Z-mail me some tips that may fix my problems so that I can enjoy this recipe with the rest of you!
Great recipe! I made this and served with white rice and "Broccoli Parmesan" #17402. No need to go to the buffet anymore!
Yummy! We love this one!  So much cheaper than going out and easy to make.
i didn't particularly like the twice-fried aspect of this.  and the cornstarch mixture didn't stick well.  but the flavor was excellent.
Mean Guy makes a mean General Tso's Chicken, that's for sure!  We loved it with our Chinese dinner!

My husband and I made this together last night. I am only giving a four star rating because we didn't use the sauce. We had never attempted General Tso's before and it really wasn't hard to do. We omitted the chili pods b/c we just didn't have any and used red pepper flake. We deep fried the chicken and we used a bottled General Tso's Stir Fry sauce I bought at Target (Archer Farms Brand...Also the best Teriyaki) we added chili oil to the final product it was awesome! Served with Fried rice and Spring Rolls. Perfect at home Chinese meal.

Just got done eating this delish dish! A most excellent recipe and pretty easy to make too. I made it exactly as described, but next time I may skip the part of the egg and cornstarch just to lower the fat content a bit. The flavor of the sauce was awesome, so I will completely keep that part. I will definitely make this again and again.
Very good. Instead of frying the chicken, I grilled it with dried peppers. Then pan fried it with the sauce.

I was a little disappointed.  I had a hard time getting the batter to stay on the chicken pieces during the first fry.  The taste of the sauce was good, but because of the chicken, I was overall disappointed.  Will try again...maybe I cooked too much chicken at a time.  If anyone has any suggestions, please share.

Wow -- this absolutely rocks!  I made this for dinner the other night, and was hoping it wouldn't be awful (I have had mixed luck with some recipes on zaar, even ones with great ratings).  But this is SO GOOD!!  I upped the chicken a bit, tripled the sauce and served it with fried rice.  And it's SO EASY!!  Next time I might reduce the chilis just a tad but not too much.  Thank you Kirstin!!

I'm giving it 5 stars as it wouldn't be fair to knock it down since I didn't follow the recipe. The thing I've always disliked about GT chicken is the thick batter so tonight I oven baked the flour dredged thigh pieces and then pan cooked them with the sauce.  Wow what a difference. It was lightly crispy without all the empty calories.  The sauce made it though.  Thanks!

VERY GOOD! My family devoured this. :) I did not use peanut oil, I didn't have any & I did not put in the red pepper, because my kids don't like spicy food. I used vegetable oil & it came out just great. I can't wait to make it again! Thank you for posting ;)

I love your recipe, and it comes out sooooooo good.   Although Peanut Oil is more expensive than other oils, it is ESSENTIAL for getting the temperature hot enough to stir fry the recipe correctly.  Peanut oil has a much higher boiling point than other vegetable oils, and allows you to get the wok much hotter without scorching, for stir frying and making wonderful dishes such as General Tso's Chicken.  Thanks for the recipe.  It's a winner!

This is a great dish.  I think a few small changes make it even a little better:
1.  add some garlic to taste- 1/2 tsp or so to the sauce
2.  add some ginger to taste- a couple of dashes
3.  triple the sauce to have enough to drizzle on rice as well.  Double is plenty to cover the chix, but triple for a little extra oomph.
4.  split the 2nd fry up like the first one, they will get brown faster and crispier.
Delish!  thanks mean guy!

Awesome. buffet quality. I doubled the sauce and added 1/4 tsp of ground ginger and 1/2 garlic powder. though i think added fresh minced ginger and garlic to the dried chili pods would be even better. been wanting to try this one for a long time and glad i did

This was excellent!  Next time I will double the sauce as some of the other reviewers mentioned...and add garlic.  I served it with Chinese Fried Rice #38748 and the meal was a huge success!!!  Thank you!
Made it for my son and he loved it. Followed directions as written. Very easy to prepare. Thanks!!!

Yum Yum Yum... I made this for the first time a couple of weeks ago and have made it 3 times since.

The only difficult part is finding a store that carries Mirin.

I made a big error making this one, but even with my goof up it still ended up tasting good.  I forgot to brown up my chicken and just put my liquid mixture into the pan without chicken being in there...well it turned into a big huge jello-ish ball lol  I have no clue what happend but nothing I did would thin it down..I tried some more wine, water, chicken stock lol  it just got bigger and bigger...so strange!  So I threw my chicken on top of my blob and just mixed it all in...and it still turned out good!  I'll definitely make this one again.
Never had before, but will make again!
Made this tonight and my family looooved it!!! This will be on the top of my favorites list along with the bourbon chicken recipie that everyone loves!

WOW!  This was absolutely awesome.  I did not have all of the ingredients so I did the following.  In place of rice vinegar I used white vinegar, I replaced the rice wine with white cooking wine and I fried them in canola oil instead of peanut oil.  My husband said it was wonderful and we ate every last bit of it.  Thanks!

Very yummy!! Although, next time I'd use a half the sugar, it was very sweet. Added a lots of chopped green onions at the end and it gave it nice freshness and color. I also used chicken breast.  So much better than take out because the take out stuff usually has too much fatty blobby bits in it. I'll make this again experimenting with other meats, or without frying. Thanks!
Delicious!! Beats any take out general tso's.  Added some fresh garlic and ginger and the flavor was amazing.  Definitely a keeper!

Excellent recipe!  This is my sons birthday dinner request.  I made the chicken a night ahead and did a test batch for the sauce.  Very yummy.  I will be adding ginger root, garlic and wee pinch of cayenne for heat to my finished product tomorrow for added flavor.  But very good stuff!
Very good recipe, I always double the sauce to make sure that I have plenty.  My family really enjoys this, thanks for the great recipe.

Made this a week ago and per my hubby's request we are having it again.  Used Sriracha hot sauce instead of dried chili's.   A delicious recipe.  Doubled the sauce and added a bunch of fresh veggies.  Thank you!!
Great recipe. Only difference was I used chicken breasts and added in some onions I needed to use up. We will be making this again!

My hubby raved over this one.  The flavor is better than what you would get at a restaurant.  The sauce is suppose to be thick so I didn't change the recipe.  The pepper pods added a nice "crunch" so the texture of the whole meal was great. This is a keeper.

I dont even have words for this recipe it was so good and perfect. I later had some at a restaurant and was quite disapointed. VERY GOOD, even if a little labour intensive. Worth every secong of prep time.

We loved it!
Outstanding! - we like it spicy hot and added double or more pepper pods.  Not too sweet like the restaurant versions.  Easy to do .. this is a winner.

This recipe is a winner!  My husband and I moved to a small midwest town with absolutely no chinese food.  We've been craving this dish and decided we'd have to learn how to make it ourselves.  Our first attempt at another recipe was not so great.  This recipe hit it out of the park!!  I think this is better than the best chinese food restaurant I ever ordered this at.  By mistake we didn't fry the chicken two times.  After frying we just put the sauce in a a pan, reduced it a little and then tossed the chicken in to coat.  Also, I used Mirin for the rice wine.  I found it in the asian section next to the rice vinegar.  I think it's the same as rice wine but not sure.  Regardless, it turned out delicious!  We also used the hit peppers but didn't get any heat.  I think I might just add a little siracha to the sauce next time since I like everything a little spicy.

Very good, only issue I had was that the sauce carmelized and clumped leaving most the chicken w/out any sauce.  Will totally remove from heat next time and allow the sauce to slowly carmelize and coat the chicken.

I used tofu instead of chicken and subbed 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper for the chilis. The cornstarch didn't stick too well to the tofu, but it still came out a nice golden brown. Very strong tofu taste though, I should have marinaded it in the sauce first. The sauce was great, even if the rest of my dish wasn't.

I have to say I made this General Tso chicken and the chicken itself came out crispy and good however the sauce for this chicken was way to salty!!! And I am the type of person that has to have salt on everything but this sauce was soooo salty I could not eat it! The sauce needs to be less salty and a little sweeter! Sorry for the bad review but people need to know that the sauce needs to be changed a little bit. Maybe use less soy sauce or use the low sodium soy sauce???

I had read all the reviews before making this and listened to doubling of the sauce and I am so glad I did.  This was the most delicious General Tso I have had..it was the perfect blend of flavors. Not too sweet but sweet enough, spicy hot but not overly and not salty at all. I didn't find a problem with any of it.  I followed the recipe but as I said I doubled the sauce, I did add in some spring onions, a little garlic and fresh ginger and sprinkled some toasted sesame over the cooked dish. Another 5 stars.  This was mouth watering excellent.  We certainly didn't need it, but we did wish for more sauce.  Also, I found this much easier to make than I had expected.  This will definitely be made again.  And again, and again, and again.

Hey, this is good stuff!  I didn't have rice wine so I used sherry and it worked great.  I also didn't bread my chicken to save on calories.  Subed crushed red pepper flakes. Yum. I have a secret love of WalMart's generals chicken and decided to give it a try at home. Excellent results. A big enough hit that it has entered into the normal circuit. For those of you who found this salty, try low sodium soy sauce.  For the person who used mirin  it's just sweetened  sake.  If you love General Tso's Chicken you have got to try this recipe. Oh, this is soooo good.  My family really loved it!  Thanks for posting!

Wow, this is a fantastic recipe! General Tso's is my son's favorite meal and I gave up on finding a recipe as good as we can get down the street. I tripled it and still didn't have leftovers. FANTASTIC!! Does anyone read the 3, 2 or 1 star reviews? This is where the helpful information is. Okay so the truth is that the breading isn't anything like the Chinese Restaurant because it's so thin, it's just enough to brown it and that's all. Notice no salt, pepper, garlic, or anything in the breading - that means it also adds no flavor. Now, the sauce calls for cornstarch so you really should thicken it and reduce the starch BEFORE you put it on the chicken so you cook off the starchy taste and allow it to thicken up a little so it just coats the chicken, not soaks up the little breading that is there. Also, the sauce, where is the pressed garlic or fresh ground ginger? I'm sure there is one or the other of those in every General Tso's Chicken I've ever ordered. So if you read this, maybe let me know because I only read all the rave reviews which didn't help me at all. Don't get me wrong, it's not a bad recipe as is! It's just not anything like the General Tso Chicken that actually crunches a little under the thick sweet spicy sauce that clings to the tasty breading.

This was really delicious!  The best and easiest Szechuan I have come across!  I tripled th sauce because I had several baby zucchini's that I cut into chunks and sauteed in advance with the red pepper.  I removed them from the pan and then added the chicken, cooking until brown and almost done.  I removed the chicken from the pan and set aside to ensure that it stays tender.  I added the garlic along with 2 chopped Serrano peppers to the pan and sauteed a few minutes until browned.  I added the remaining ingredients and simmered for a few minutes.  I added about a tsp of cornstarch to 1/4 cup of water, mixed and put that in to thicken the sauce.  Last, I added the chicken and veggies back to the pan and simmered a few minutes to reheat and finish cooking the chicken.  I loved what the cornstarch did to the chicken when cooking it.  I did not have carrots or green onions... you could add anything you wanted to this and it would be good.  I was out of rice wine vinegar, so I used white wine vinegar and it worked out fine.  The only thing that would be a nice addition to the sauce is a little ginger.  Thank you Mirj... this is a true keeper!!

Definite winner! Put some brown rice in the cooker first and then diced the chicken and garlic. While they were cooking, I chopped my veggies and measured out the other ingredients (just put everything into one big bowl as I finished with it). By the time I finished with that, the chicken was nicely browned so it was time pour in my big bowl of stuff and the whole thing was ready just as the rice finished cooking!A healthy and delicious dinner was ready in 20 minutes! I usually don't like the texture of meat when you coat it with cornstarch, so I just made a slurry with chicken broth and added it right before I added the scallions. I also threw in some mushrooms that I needed to use up and some sriracha sauce for a bit of heat. Right before serving, I sprinkled in some crushed dry roasted peanuts and some slices of lime on the side. Guess that didn't make it a real szechuan, more Thai...but it was delicious. Thanks for sharing, Mirj!

This recipe is a do again it was easy with a great taste. I did double the sauce may even triple it next time. I didn't like the cornstarch on the chicken.Next time I am going to cook the chicken and make a slurry of the cornstarch and chicken broth. I also added crushed red pepper for a little heat ,mixed up the peppers usinng a little red and a little green and added straw mushrooms and some broccoli. Yum... Yum ... will do it again , Thanks for sharing Mirj.

This was deeeeeelicious!! The whole family loved it! I'm not a zucchini fan, but julienning them and mixing them in this sauce helps disguise them for me. I will definitely be making this again!! Thank you!
Mirj, my husband and daughter loved this! The flavors were great and just right! Thanks for a lovely dinner!
Thanks, Mirj, for a great recipe.  Left it in the oven until it was really crispy.  The family really enjoyed it.  Also, left it in the marinade for about 6 hours.

Mirj, when I stumbled onto this recipe I wondered... "could it be similar to my beloved MarFar chicken?" And it is! This was so tasty! And best of all, I don't have to get the ingredients at a specialty store. Thank you so much for an easy, wonderful alternative! This one is going into regular rotation.

There are those of us who know better than to mess with Mirj's recipes..and then there are those of us who are FEARLESS...LOL.  I made this up with chicken breasts and they were delicious, so I tried with salmon steaks and they were even more delicious.  Thankyou Mirj for a keeper, easy to make, the ingredients are easy to come by and it tastes damn good.

this stirfry made a delicious supper, served it over brown rice.
I had to use a green pepper and I had some asparagus I needed to use up, other than that followed the recipe as it instructed. It was a lovely combination of flavours, especially the ginger and we liked the idea that it made it's own juice and didn't need to be thickened.  thanks for posting Mirj, I will be making it again!

I had my doubts about this one.  First, it just sounded a bit odd, plus I'm not a big fan of red peppers or celery, but I really liked the way these flavors went together.  I left out the cayenne pepper.  My husband added teriaki sauce to his (maybe not kosher, but we're not Jewish).

Nice different side dish, quite a conversation piece. Some liked it, some didn't. But on the whole most did and it was a change from the usual cucumber relish type of dish. I used the chili powder, didn't want to buy a whole bottle of chili bean sauce to use 1/4 teaspoon, but can use up the black beans in another recipe.  Liked the taste of the sesame oil, it added a nice nutty taste.
This added a good change to our Easter dinner, thanks for sharing.

i never would have thought of cooking cucumbers, but we really enjoyed this different way of serving them. this cooked up quickly, loved the asian flair. i just cut them in halves, very easy and tasty.
Wow! I had also never fried (or even cooked) cucumbers before.  It is a hit with the whole family.  The sesame oil really added a nice taste to the dish.

This recipe was kind of bland by itself, but when added on top of homemade cheesy mashed potatoes, it was wonderful! I used the chili powder and only half of the sesame sauce that it called for and enjoyed it as a topping.

I've had this on my list since it was posted and finally got a chance to make it. It's a very simple recipe to put together. The pork came out very tender and the sauce goes well with the broccoli. I tasted it while it was cooking and thought it might need a little more kick, so I added the hoisin sauce and also about 1 to 1.5 tsp of five-spice. Worked out well. This is great served over rice. I'm sure I'll be making it again. Thanks for posting Jelisa

J!  This is sooo good!  Even my 8 year old loved it! This was one of my picks for last weeks ABC chef game.  It's so easy to prepare, and cooks so quickly, great for a quick evening meal.  I added a couple TBSP of hoisin, and about 1/2 tsp fresh ginger, at the same time that I added the chicken back to the pan.  The sauce is delicious, and there is plenty of it. Had it served over Basmati rice.  I wold have added some extra spice as Mark suggested, but I was serving to the kids, so I held back.  Thumbs up from all of us!

This was easy to make. I was hesitant about letting a cornstarch-based sauce simmer without stirring, but it worked just fine.  If I make it again, I'll marinate the pork chunks in the sauce before adding cornstarch (the broccoli was fantastic, but the pork a little bland).  Besides other seasoning suggestions, maybe a few drops of sesame oil?

This worked well for ease of preparation but the taste was quite bland and 2 Tablespoons of sesame seeds was, in my opinion, way too much.  One teaspoon would have been adequate.  The next time I make this, I would definitely add more soy sauce (about 1 T.) and maybe some hoisin or oyster sauce to boost the flavor.

This was a big hit with my family.  The sauce was delicious, I doubled the amount of sauce and added extra broccoli and served it over rice noodles.  I also added a little extra soy sauce.  This is high on our list of favorites.  Thank you so much for posting it.

This was very good.  I used frozen broccoli that I already had on hand, but will be sure to get some fresh for next time I make it.  I did add extra soy sauce, a little hoisin and ginger, as well as a few pinches of Szechuan seasoning blend for some kick.  I'd like to try making this with chicken also.   The kids liked it; even picky DD#2 pronounced it "excellent."  Thanks!

Wow!!! This was probably one of the most authentic tasting oriental recipes I have made!
My pork tenderloin had been marinating in roasted garlic teriyaki sauce before I sliced it. I doubled the sauce as I wanted to up my veggie amounts. I used the full pound of broccoli, and 2 stalks of celery cut on the bias, 1 medium onion wedged, 1/2 red pepper diced, an 8 oz pkg of sliced mushrooms and a hand full of pea pods. I did add some additional garlic and ginger as I was stir frying the meat per the recommendation of other reviewers. And I ran out of regular soy sauce so I used mushroom and generous splashes of oyster sauce and sesame oil. Fantastic base recipe to play with, I am thrilled with the results!
This recipe is a great starting point.  Added Hoisin Sauce and Ginger plus mixed vegetables. Thanks for posting the recipe and Thank you to Recipezaar.com

At the risk of sound like all the other reviews - WOW! A very easy dish to make. Pork was very tender and I undercooked the broccoli as we prefer a crisper taste.  Will make this again and again.  Thanks for sharing such a great recipe!

For us, this was just OK. I wanted to stay true to the recipe, so I followed it exactly and came up with a bland, mushy broccoli dish. The pork was very tender, and the method was simple. I think that if I make this again, I will try some of the other reviewer's suggestions to add some extra flavor and spice.

This was a real winner in my house! Even my picky teenager liked it. The only change I made was adding a bag of frozen Chinese stir fry vegetables. I will defiantly be making this again! Thank you Jelisa for a wonderful recipe.

I liked this very much.  I did, however, change the cooking method a bit.  I added thesoy sauce, ginger and garlic to the cut up chicken and maranaded it for a couple of hours.  I then cooked the chicken with the green onion, removed it and cooked the broccoli using water (no broth on hand). I thickened this up with a bit of cornstarch and water, replaced the chicken and enjoyed all over rice.  Thanks J e l i s a
very ordinary, average

Everyone's suggestions very helpful.  I did others suggested, marinaded in ginger, garlic, five spice powder (<1 tsp) and soy sauce, but one change I made that added to flavor, was to grate the ginger.  It brought out more flavor. Would make again!  Not too bad if watching your calories, too!
My family really liked this recipe.  I added fresh ginger when sauteing the pork and water chestnuts for crunch, but otherwise made no changes. Thank you for sharing the recipe!
This turned out great and was so easy!  The sauce was thin so I used corn starch to thicken it.  Served it over plain white rice and added stir fry vegetables.

Easy to make and very good.  The flavors are excellent and light.  This recipe is now on our 'comfort food' list.  Next time I might double the soy sauce.  I cooked on low for about 7 hours and served over rice.

I have made several spicy orange ginger recipes over the years. This recipe is one of the BEST!! There is no batter, no sticky sauce, just lean meat with lots of flavour. It is a new family favorite!!!We added a little extra chili peppers. THANKS-GREAT !

I would give this more than 5 stars - It was wonderful. I cut the chicken back to 12 oz but made the full sauce. I used 2 1/2 tbsp of sweet chili sauce and cut out the extra sugar..  It is such an easy recipe to propare because you can get everything ready ahead of time and then it only takes a few minutes to cook.  Thangs Paja this is a keeper.
This was excellent!!
This is great my 2 year old ate it too not too hot... Husband said it was a good one
This is great
This was wonderful.  Great contrasts in flavours and textures.  Very fresh-tasting.  I didn't stray from the recipe at all and it worked perfectly.  Thanks.

This is great.  I made only 2 slight changes, instead of sesame oil and chili, I used sesame chili oil. And I also substituted brown rice for the white.  I've only made this once, but will be sure to not lose this one.  In fact I've marked it five stars and a capital GREAT!

Wow!  This was awesome...  
The preparation is spread over a couple of days, but it's not too complicated and it's definitively worth all the work.  We used mallard legs and showeler breast meat to make the soup, and it turned out better than I could have imagined.  Instead of a duck carcass we used chicken (leftover from before), and we did not have any star anise...  Who knows how this changes the overall result?  Will find out soon because we will make this again for sure.  Thanks for posting this!

I finally found a recipe to use the star anise xmas gift. Loved the marinade and will definitely use that again. I subbed sherry for the mirin otherwise followed all the instructions and loved it!! Saving this recipe into the make again file.

This was a fantastic recipe. I didn't use the star anise, but that didn't seem to hurt it at all. What flavor! What textures! And not too fatty or gamy. Thank you for sharing. I have always shied away from duck soup but now it will be one of my favorites.

Can't WAIT to make this true!
And am SURE Ian would be proud his original inspired you to do! :)
The sauce is highly flavorful and delicious.  We really loved it.  I added some scallions (cut into about 1/2" pieces) with the other veggies.

This is a tasty dish and easy to prepare.  I will probably leave out the cornstarch next time as I prefer the sauce to be more on the 'runny' side, but that is just a personal preference. You could vary it with other vegetables too, such as baby corn, fresh asparagus, bell peppers and water chestnuts.  I will make this again. Thanks for sharing.

Very easy and pretty dish when prepared.  I also put in the green onions suggested and was glad I did, for a little extra taste.  I might cut down on the seasame oil, a little goes a long way.  A very nice dinner!
Thought I would try a different cashew chicken...this was a great recipe...very easy and the sauce was perfect.  thanks, I am sure I will be making this often.
Soooo Yummy!  I just made it plain Jane and it was amazing, I can't wait till next time, when I jazz it up a bit!  Thanks!

Made this just like recommended and addes peas and carrots.  It was delicious; just like you get at a restaurant.  Very quick and easy too!  I used leftover herbed pork roast, and will keep this recipe for my roast leftovers from now on.  Thank you!
Added peas, topped with cilantro when serving. Yum! Family loved it.
Perfect for the recipe#20445 I made for tonight.  Delicous!  I did add about 1 to 2 tablespoons of water to the sauce as I found it a little strong, but the taste was right-on! Pam
Have to agee with the previous reviewer, had a bit of a strong flavor from the vinegar - added 2 tablespoons of water and tasted much better!  Thanks for posting - will make again.

Oh gosh Evelyn this is wonderful fried rice, all the flavors blend together wonderful, I used a can of small salad shrimp in place of fresh shrimp, and increased the fresh garlic, this is delicious, thanks for sharing!...Kitten:)

Kate will be pleased at yet another cross-cultural triumph - A Greek cook posts an Asian recipe prepared in Iceland by a transplanted American! I used all my creative power to make this happen, Ev.
