I found that it is faster and easier if you put them on a roaster pan and bake in the oven at 400-425 for about  10-15 minutes (matters the size of the meatball). All the grease then goes to the bottom of the pan making it a little healthier.

This is a fabulous recipe! I made it as written and it is flawless. I have also baked these meatballs and they are still wonderful.  I like them just as they are but have added different spices depending on what I will use them for. Oh.. and I ALWAYS make double and freeze half. Be sure to freeze on a cookie sheet and THEN put them in a freezer bag! Thank you, Karen, for sharing your mom's genius!

If a meatball could be a perfect 10, then your recipe fit the bill!  Phenomenal!!!  Comfort food!  I have made your Mama's spaghetti sauce before, so I know that these meatballs will be a wonderful addition to a incredible sauce!!!  I baked them at 375 for 15 minutes and I was pleasantly suprised that there was no grease or meat foam that can appear with meatballs or meatloaf.  I use a blend of ground beef and pork that I got from my butcher.   I couldn't resist and cut into one just out of the oven.  They were mouth watering yummy!  This will be "my go to" recipe from now on!  My congrats and thanks to your Mama for sharing such a recipe!!!

These meat-a-balls are just plain AWESOME!!!  Beyond the taste and texture, I cannot tell you how absolutely ITALIAN my kitchen smelled while these balls were baking.  Mmmmm, Mmmmmm, Mmmm.  I can't wait to try them today after they've had a chance to rest and soak up some of the sauce.  Thank you for sharing your mom's recipe.
If I could give this recipe a 10 I would! These are absolutely the best meatballs I have ever had!!

These are the best melt in your mouth meatballs you will ever taste.  I made according to directions- used 1/2 cup of parm- if given a choice I'm always going with the max on cheese, but only 1 teaspoon of salt.  I figured since I added the max on cheese the salt could be lessened.  It worked perfect.  I was careful not to mix the meat too much or form the balls too hard, so they were very tender.   I made these and added to Mama's Don't Skip a Step Sauce- What a great meal for company.  It was such a hit.
These are the best!  I baked instead of frying!  I ate so many before i put them in my spaghetti, i just can not get enough of them. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.  =)

these were so good and not difficult at all. Very flavorful without that sausage heartburn later in the day. I served these as meatball sandwiches a few days later and they were as good as the spaghetti and meatballs dinner the day I made them. I still have some frozen in my freezer. Can't wait to eat those!! Absolutely will replace my other meatball recipe!!

Very good meatballs.  I used twice the garlic powder and a little more fresh ground pepper, and then made 80 small meatballs that I baked at 350 for 15 minutes, then let them sit in the turned off but still  hot oven another 5 minutes.  Delicious!
I have a house of hungry meat eating men and they loved your recipe. Thank you for this one.

I just made these this morning for dinner tonight with my extended Italian family.  From my taste test these are really good.  However, there does seem to be something missing from the recipe.  Usually there is some milk or water added to the meat mixture for moisture because the egg just doesn't add enough and I needed to add milk to mine because with bread in 1 inch chunks, I couldn't get the bread to completely mix into the mixture without being obvious.  Even with adding the milk to the mixture after the fact, you can still see the bread.  My Italian Mom has been making meatballs for the last 40+ years and she uses breadcrumbs so when my family comes over for dinner tonight hopefully no one notices the bread!  Since I can't replicate my Mom's recipe I decided to try this one, but next time I will soak the bread pieces in milk as other recipes for meatball using bread chunks do.  I made this with the matching sauce recipe and it is great!  I would have given it 5 stars except for the issue above.

I have made these multiple times and have to say they are FANTASTIC. Everyone loved loved loved them and kept talking about them for days. Next time I went to make spaghetti I was asked if I was making meatballs and I got the puppy dog eyes begging for them. I said sure, afterall, all I did for this recipe is measure and fry. My 4 and 5 year olds to most everything else!

In the words of Rachael Ray "YUM-O!) These are amazing! I drizzle olive oil on a sheet pan and then drizzle it over the meatballs. Bake until browned and they are PERFECT! I make one batch and then divide it into thirds. Keep one third for that night (or the next) and then freeze the other two! Works perfectly! Great time-saver!

These were great! I halved the recipe since there is only two of us and we still had plenty of leftovers. The only change I made was to use 1/4 c. italian breadcrumbs instead of the bread since I didn't have any stale bread around.  I baked at 375 for about 20 min.

I always hesitate rating a recipe I've changed, but these were so fantastic I just had to have my say too!  We have lactose intolerance issues in the house, so I omitted the cheese replacing the binding action of it with an additional egg and using the full amount of bread.  Discovering no parsley left in the jar, I doubled all the other seasonings (except salt) using Homemade Italian Seasoning #17718 and to ensure the best flavor, I fried them... these were scrumptious!  I'll be back ;)

Wow! These are easily the best meatballs I have ever tasted!! I can't believe that I actually cooked them myself! I used 4 white rolls that I had left over and 3 slices of whole wheat bread (broken up). I, too, fried them in the pan with extra virgin olive oil and it was just so easy! I made this as a spur of the moment late dinner and it was a wonderful surprise for my husband and daughter. They both devoured it! Thank you for sharing this amazing recipe! I will save it to use over and over!!!
Yum!

Bravo Karen! Another fantastic recipe. I made these meatballs straight from the recipe and they turned out exactly as I expected, PERFECT!
These are the bomb. Thanks again for another superb recipe

I just tried one that came out of the oven.... Fantastic!  Can't wait to try them with a spaghetti or swedish sauce.  I baked them on a cooling rack set inside a baking sheet at 450 F for about 15 minutes or until the internal temp reached 160 F.  Thanks for posting!

These were the best and most easy meatballs I have ever made! When you think of making meatballs it sounds like a lot of stuff and work, these took me about 20 minutes to make a bunch of them. I made extra to put in the freezer. Its very affordable and you can use them in your pasta, as a snack, or in meatball sands! The possibilities are endless with these. I made these for my family dinner night and everyone loved them and asked if I would make more for them to take! I wouldn't change anything about this recipe!

YUM!! My kids gobbled them up, which is more than 5 stars in my book!!! They were so easy to put together, and just full of flavor! I baked mine instead of frying them, that is just a personal choice. Loved, loved, loved these! Thank you for sharing your wonderful recipe!
Yummy, this is a great recipe and will be used very much in my household!
These are deeelish!!  Thanks so much for sharing!  I made the fresh tomato sauce on here and was really pleased with the outcome.  :o)

Mama Iuliucci...will you adopt me?!  These "meat-a-balls" are delicioso!  I have made these using both methods of frying and baking.  I prefer them fried, but seems baking is easier for my busy household these days (& honestly no one in my family can tell a difference after they've been added to the sauce.)  Thank you!

This is the best meatball recipe i've ever tried. The dont miss a step spaghetti sauce goes with it brilliantly. Loved by every single person whos ever eaten it with our family. My 3 year old son and my 28 year old husband would eat it ever day if they could. Top marks for a top dish!
YUMMY....Absolutely delicious !!!!

This recipe is truly wonderful, the best and so Easy!  I subsituted 1 LB ground bison, 1 lb of lean ground beef, and panko bread crumbs because that is what I had on hand.  I also baked mine.  I use only this recipe now for meatballs!
Fabulous recipe! Really! Next time I'll try it with a "meatloaf mix" instead of all ground beef to see if that adds anything; but as written, it's practically perfect - thanks!

These are great meatballs.  I usually divide the recipe in half for the two of us, keeping the salt at one teaspoon.  I use four slices of pepperridge farm white bread and process the bread, add the seasonings and mix, then add the egg and a little bit of milk to it.  They are very tender and tasty.

This recipe is great! I have recently gone back to a Non-Meat diet (I'm not a full vegan, love ice cream too much ha ha) so I used my Gimme Lean Veggie Ground Beef style and followed the recipe, light frying then simmered in sauce. They came out wonderful! So tasty, I could hardly tell a difference at all. Thank you so much for sharing.

DIVINE! Used the fill 2 t. of salt. Used my own "italian seasoning" which was basil, oregano, rosemary, and thyme. Quadrupled the garlic powder and used organic, grass fed, free range, hormone free beef. THE BEST MEATBALLS EVER! Baked at 350 for 30 minutes and the plopped them into my homemade sauce. They were moist and incredibly flavorful. Perfectly seasoned!! Thanks for making my first meatball endeavor amazing!

WOW!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  Thank You for sharing.  I have used this recipe twice as a gift-meal for families who needed help.  And the reviews have been amazing.  Not to mention how happy my family is after serving them this dinner.  The only problem is we never have enough.  It takes 10 minutes to throw it together and is so easy.  Not many recipes say mix all ingredients together and cook.  I love it and can't thank you enough.  I like to fry the meatballs and then put them in the crock pot with my sauce where they can stay warm until we are ready for dinner.  Meaning you can make this ahead of time and come home to it ready to go.  Thanks soo much

Oh my.... I've had this recipe saved in my cookbook for ages and never got around to making it. Well, tonight I did. These are amazing! I doubled the garlic, used panko instead of breadcrumbs, and baked them. Other than that I stuck pretty close to the recipe and nearly fainted when I took the first bite! If there were 6 stars this recipe would get it.

So good! I only used 4 slices of whole wheat bread. The mixture wasn't too wet. I also used 1 pound of Italian sausage and one pound of ground turkey breast. Just what I had on hand. These were probably the best I have made. I didn't fry in oil. I didn't need to. The Italian pork sausage had enough fat so I didn't need the oil. Oh, I also added onion powder. Good recipe.

A very tender and tasty meatball. I baked instead of fry (450 for about 15-20 min) to cut down on calories.  I think I will try frying them next time just in all fairness of the recipe, but baking came out great too..  I was on the heavier side off all the spices and it was perfect. I froze the rest so I can use them at will! I'm very happy!

I LOVE THESE MEATBALLS!!! very delicious, excellent taste, the texture is just right and combined with My Mama Iuliucci's "Don't Skip a Step" Spaghetti Sauce ITS A MEAL WORTH 5 stars! when making these meatballs i usually lightly toast the bread, just personal preference. sometimes i use a little less parm. cheese but thats just personal taste. THESE ARE THE BEST! EXCELLENT MEATBALLS wether they be used as appetizers for the football game, or put into your favorite spaghetti sauce for an excellent meal. (im planning on making this with Mama Iuliucci's "Don't Skip a Step" Spaghetti Sauce for my parents 21st anniversary)THANK YOU KAREN FOR POSTING THESE I PLAN ON MAKING THESE FOR A VERY VERY LONG TIME!
Really good and really easy to make!
These were really good! Thanks!

Easy, and ingredients I have in my pantry every day.  Oh, and did I mention they are delicious?  Next time I'll make the sauce you recommended, because my jarred sauce didn't cut it.  I put them in the crock pot and simmered them and they got so tender.  Thanks for sharing, Karen.
It was super! My family loved it so much! I have to do more of it!

My new go to meatball recipe! I used 1lb. 80/20 ground beef and 1lb. ground pork. I also didn't have any old bread so I used one cup of plain bread crumbs. After scooping them with a medium cookie scoop, I broiled them in a broiler pan on low for 15 mins turning them after about 10 mins. They came out perfect! To make them extra moist and flavorful use 1/4 cup grated parmesan and 1/4 cup shredded parmesan and/or romano. Ah-mazing!

I am not a fan of meat balls - usually heavy and boring so I prefer a meat sauce. But my son is coming for a viist and HE likes them so thought I'd try these based on the reviews. I was shocked at the amount of bread it called for and bought a loaf of wonderful, fresh, Chicago Italian for the nice crust and went to town with it, I  treated everything delicately and made sure the herbs and spices were distributed evenly. I browned the meatballs a bit but finished them in the oven - so had the fond for my sauce but less aggravation - for me anyway. These meatballs are exquisite! Light, flavorful, good just as is or with a sauce of any type. It made a lot which was good as I kept finding myself swiping one from the container till I finally froze them except for those that I put in the sauce for my son. I HIGHLY recommend these. Well worth the effort!
Easy and delicious. Makes a lot! Thanks for posting.
Made these for meatball sub sandwiches and they were delish! Thanks for the recipe!

I tried this recipe yesterday along with Mama Iuliucci's spaghetti sauce recipe. They both tasted wonderful! I have tried making many other spaghetti sauce recipes and have not liked any of them. This is the best meatballs and sauce!

This is really good meat ball recipe. I have made it twice and I just love them.I have used greound sirloin eat time and going to make it with ground turkey next.I mix all the spices with the meat and refrigerate a few hours before I cook them and it gives the spices time to work though the meat.

I'm a 16 year old girl who barely started cooking, and this came out AMAZING. Seriously, if a novice like me can do it, anyone can. I followed the recipe completely, except I added bell peppers to it. The meatballs melt in your mouth, and they have such a nice flavor. It's so good! I made it along with My Mama Iuliucci's "Dont Skip A Step" Spagetti Sauce and it was perfect! My dad and brother are such critics, and even they loved it! Everybody should try this. Next time I think I'll add more veggies into the meatballs. I can't wait. lol.

After a huge fail using another meatball recipe, I made some using this one.  The only change was using sweet bread rolls instead of regular bread, which made the meatballs just a tad bit sweeter.  The process was very easy to follow and these meatballs were very easy to cook.  My daughter took one bite and proclaimed her dislike of meatballs changed!  Along with a great meat sauce recipe found online, these paired up very nicely!  Thanks for the great recipe!
Excellent meatballs.  I am on making my second batch in less than a month....we can't get enough of them!
Very good and easy!  I halved the recipe using 1 lb of meat and it turned out great.  To save time, I used the blender for the bead.

Used 1 lb. beef so cut the ingredients in half, but used a lot more seasoning, oregano and basil. Grind the bread in a mini food chopper for finer crumbs and moisten them with 2 tablespoons of milk. If you have fresh parsley, use it! Great basic recipe. I bake mine and get about 25 1 1/2" meatballs. Mama's sauce is also a great recipe.

I have used this recipe many times. It's absolutely EXCELLENT. My wife and I love these things. I usually make the full recipe and freeze them in 3 or 4 bags. Then during the week when I'm feeling lazy, I buy some store bought pasta sauce and simmer the meatballs in it for about it hour. It thaws out the meatballs and add some flavor the the sauce. Seriously, stop reading reviews and go make some meatballs!
The most amazing meatballs I have ever eaten. In combination with the homemade sauce mentioned in the recipe, wow. My entire family are now converts. Thank you so much for posting!

Hands down the BEST Meatballs I have ever had.  I cannot tell you how many times I have made this recipe.  It's a family favorite.  I always follow the recipe exactly and have always had success.  Thank you so much for sharing this.

Excellent meatballs for a party!  I made these as directed, they held together perfectly.  I used a cookie scoop to shape them and I put them on cookie sheets to bake.  I did not make my own sauce this time as I was crunched for time but I would like to try that.

Tried these with great result. I've modified the recipe slightly tho. First I've combined the beef with a bit of pork (to get in some additional juices and flavors) and then by finely dicing some bacon and onions and put both on heat until the onion turned gold. Left it to cool down and added into the meatballs mixture. Also fresh parsley and oregano make them even better.

I've also tried cooking them directly in the sauce and frying them a bit first. If you fry them in the pan, don't forget to put a bit of water (or broth, wine...) into the pan when you're done, scrape or cook off all that is left from the meatballs and then put it into the sauce. You'd be missing out great addition to the flavor of those awesome meatballs ;)

My wife and I run a little country store in Tennessee. I started making your meatballs and sauce for meatball subs on Wednesday lunch only. They are a hit - we sell out every time! Our customers can't wait for the next batch.

Let me just say, OMG. Best meatballs I have ever tasted. I baked them in the oven so I can freeze them for later use. Next time I make them I will use a little lest garlic powder. ( my own personal preference). Highly recommend this recipe.

These meatballs were outstanding!! My husband ate an entire plate full before I even put them in the sauce??. From now on I will double the recipe. We love fresh basil so I added a large handful, best meatballs EVER!!

Love this recipe! This has been my go to meatball recipe. This is good as is. I eventually changed it up to be 1/2 pork and 1/2 beef. Recently I've switched to gluten free bread. I pair this with Don't Skip a Step sauce, and my family is very happy.

Very tasty and easy to put together!  I made a minor substitution...used ricotta mixed with egg in place of the cottage cheese.  I didn't miss the meat in this one at all!  Thanks Miss Annie, this will be made often!

I had no idea these stuffed shells would turn out so well cooked in a crock pot. Tasted so yummy and with very little time spent in the kitchen. Thanks so much Miss Annie. Very filling and loved that rich cheesy taste.

This was really yummy! I needed more sauce, though. My spaghetti sauce can was only 26 oz. (ever notice how "they" start w/ large sizes, then gradually get smaller, but keep the price the same??!!) SO - some of my shells burned to the sides of the crockpot. (I was gone all day, or would've checked on it & caught this) Also - when reheating the leftovers, they were kinda dry - so I'd recommended using at least the stated amount of spaghetti sauce. 

As another note here- my husband hates spinach, and ate these w/o hesitation, as did my ds's (ages 5 & 3) - so this is a "keeper!" 

Thanks for sharing, Miss Annie! I never tried pasta in the crockpot before. My cousin unexpectedly popped in for lunch, so I heated her a plate, and she is taking home the recipe, too! She LOVED it, as did her 5 yr old DS. So - again, my thanks!
Wonderful!  My husband ate this for 3 days straight!  He couldn't get enough!  Thanks for posting.

This was ok, though a bit bland for me.  If making it again I would add a hefty amount of garlic.  Also, I ran out of cheese/spinach mixture halfway through stuffing the shells, so I would make double of that.  I used ricotta instead of cottage cheese but otherwise followed the recipe.  I'll have to admit, my son ate a whole shell, and said he now likes spinach!  So that's a great plus for this recipe!

These were terrific! I used extra sauce, just because I like lots of sauce...I didn't have any spinach so I doubled up on the cottage cheese mixture so that I'd have enough (which I did)...I skipped the onions since there were onions in the spag. sauce...I was out of ital. seasoning so I used Mrs. Dash...My crockpot doesn't get very hot on LOW like others crocks so I cooked them on HIGH for 2 hours (although 3 hours wouldn't have hurt it either)...This one's going into permanent rotation for sure! Thank you for posting this recipe!

These were excellent! I've made this several times and it always comes out great. I double the recipe for the filling like another reviewer. Stuffing the shells is quite tedious but the outcome is well worth it! Oh, and I rarely add the onions as I don't think it adds much to the taste. (Take this from someone who loves onions and looks for excuses to add it to my dishes.) I also never use cottage cheese but use ricotta instead.

Loved the idea and it could not be easier to prepare. I used whole milk ricotta instead of the cottage cheese and added some garlic salt to the cheese mixture. While we all enjoyed this we felt it was a tad bland. The family wants me to layer browned ground italian sausage on top of the sauce on the bottom and before the sauce on top.

I made this in a baking dish in my oven. It was really good, I added some black pepper, garlic powder, and 3 cheese blend mix, and it worked well. I baked it for about 20 minutes, added a mix of 3 cheese blend again ontop and back in the oven until the cheese melted. Enjoyed by the whole family. Served it with Garlic bread. Thank you, will make it again :)

Very good! I didn't think it was bland at all, but then, I use my own spaghetti sauce (6 cloves of garlic!!! Yumm!!) and I followed some other peoples suggestion and substituted ricotta cheese and an egg in place of the cottage cheese. Next time I"ll saute the onions first as they were almost overpowering and I'll use 1/2 the amount of noodles also. Thanks for sharing!

GREAT recipe!  I made as directed with just a few changes - substituted ricotta for the cottage cheese, lightly sauteed the onion before adding to stuffing mixture, used cheddar for the mozzerella (what I had on hand), and omitted the italian seasoning and just seasoned with salt & pepper instead.  I also used two 25oz jars of our favorite spaghetti sauce just 'cause we like our dishes "saucy".  Undercooked the shells just slightly to avoid them turning mushy in the crock.  Super Yummy!  Received thumbs up rating from young and old in our home!  Thanks Miss Annie!

Ok. In order for this to work, you need to initially under cook your shells. I cooked mine al-dente, and they totally mushed out after a few hours in the crock pot. ALSO USE  a heavy hand with your cheese and seasonings  for the filling,so the flavor of the filling doesn't get lost under all the sauce, and definitely substitute whole milk ricotta for the cottage cheese. I also skipped the onions totally and just flavored the filling with onion powder instead. I will say this is the first time my kids ate spinach, so it is a thumbs up for that. Thanks for a nice recipe!

Excellent with a few changes. Used ricotta instead of cottage cheese, no onion, and only half the spinach. Next time we will add much more sauce - it was tasty but not saucy enough for us. Also we only boiled the pasta for half the time on the box so the shells were easy to stuff but did become mushy. My teen who resists eating veggies did not even question the "green stuff" and ate it all!

This was only okay for us. I tried adding some fresh chopped bail which helped a little. I usually make my own red sauce so it probably just wasn't flavorful enough. I'd try it again with homemade sauce and more cheese on top.

Made as per recipe but with the Ricotta not the Cottage cheese. Absolutely delicious. I cooked the pasta for 6 mins then stuffed it with filling. Added to slow cooker and set it for 4 hrs on low as directed. I have a Hamilton Beach model 33265 slow cooker. I decided to check for doneness after 3.5 hrs and it was ever so slghtly overdone at that point. Next time I will check it after 2.5 or 3 hrs and it should be perfect. Of course this is due to variances in temps of different slow cookers and nothing to do with this recipe. An absolute 5 star!

Super recipe! It was so good when finished that I didn't regret the prep time. By the end of cooking, the shells wanted to fall apart a bit. Still yummy, but not so picture perfect. Thanks for a terrific recipe!
Was skeptical of the shrimp and spinach combo, but this was really good.  Everyone liked it.

What a great recipe!  I was taking an inventory of the things in my freezer that needed to be used, and just happened to have all the ingredients for this dish, so I threw everything together and came out with a delicious meal!  However, I used penne  instead of fettuccine ... (that's all I had), and added some ground nutmeg to the sauce.  My husband said is was better than the sit down restaurants we've been to.  This is     a real keeper! Thank you  *:)

These made great munchies at a recent football gathering we had. The guys really dug the hot sausage.They need to be eaten while hot though, not to good after they cool off. Next time I think I'll mix the cheese into the stuffing instead of topping it off. It made them look pretty but didn't really incorporate into the around flavor as it just sort of fell off when you tried to eat.

These were very tastie, I made tonight for some light snacking.  I made just a couple of changes.  I mixed one cup of mozz cheese in the mix, along with a bunch more garlic then called for also a few sprigs of fresh Basil. You did not state what temp to bake at, I guessed 375, it took a little longer then the 15 minutes, but it was a very nice treat, thank you.

Charlee
This came in handy on Fathers' Day. We doubled the recipe to cover French bread sliced lengthwise. Great side for foods off the grill!

My dad loved this!  He even asked for the recipe and he NEVER asks for a recipe!

Thanks for sharing!
This pretty good. I aaded some spices to it though, cause it tasted like it was missing something. But all in all it's good
I liked this recipe. It tasted very good.I would probably use less liquid next time. I thought it was a little soupy. I also used steamed carrotts instead of squash.

We loved 'em!  I tossed in some Italian seasoning, a little fresh parsley and sliced scallion to the meat mixture.  Next time I will use additional spaghetti sauce.  My teenage son thought these meatloaves were great.  Easy to put together, delicious with buttered noodles, crispy bread and a big salad.  Yum!

This was just sooo delicious - not having had "panna cotta" before I wasn't really sure what this would be like but it is really yummy. As this was part of a dessert buffet, rather than use ramekins I just poured the mixture into muffin tray.  Once it had set I put all on plate and spooned the sauce over the top - dessert went very quickly!

This was a delicious dessert that I plan to include in my "best of the best" cookbook. I know I will be making this again for company just "as is", but I may try to tinker with it a bit to lower the fat, and make it more diabetic friendly for family meals.
I doubled the recipe, using 1 TBSP of regular vanilla, and 1 TBSP of pure vanilla bean paste, giving it not only a wonderful taste, but when the ramekins were unmoulded, the top surface had those tiny black flecks from the vanilla seeds, which I found very attractive. 
Belated thanks to Mean Chef for this terrific recipe, and thanks to Ninna for adopting it.
This is so elegant!  I like to use marsala wine/grape juice, rosemary and balsamic vinegar with my berries.  Thanks for posting!
This is a wonderful dessert.  We used mixed berries, and this was a wonderful summer dessert as it was so lite.  I will definitely make this again.

I'm giving this five stars because it came out exactly as described. Texture was perfect. However, I do feel it could benefit from a little more flavoring. I did use the highest quality vanilla extract, but it just wasn't enough. I'll make it again, but I'll bump up the flavor intensity of the Panna Cotta next time.

I've only recently started eating Panna Cotta, and decided to prepare it for an anniversary date. It was very excellent and very well received.

I added the paste of one vanilla bean to the recipe, and my inexperience with gelatin gave it a few extra lumps.

My small ramekins gave me four servings, and it turned out to be best after 24 hours in the fridge.

For a topping I used mixed berries with honey, a tablespoon of lemon juice, a splash of balsamic vinegar, and three minutes over low heat.

WONDERFUL !!!!! made this as written, and couldn't be more pleased with this delicious dinner!! We grilled the chicken before chopping and adding it to the recipe...this is definitely a keeper !!!!! Thank you!! Teresa
Oh, my gosh. This is delicious. Thank you. I also grilled the chicken first.
This was pretty good.  I had to make another batch of the sauce.  Not enought with just one.  But it was really tasty.

Terrific flavor and a great way to use up left-over chicken breasts.  I could probably go for making extra sauce too as our only "complaint" was that it was a little dry.  But that didn't stop us from gobbling it up!  I also used fat-free half n half in place of the cream (every calorie saved helps!)  Will definitely make this one again!

My picky kids thought this was outstanding so I  am giving it 5 stars.  A little too much fat for my taste but I probably will make it again with a lot less butter and might substitute sour cream or Creme Legere for the heavy cream.  Comfort food at its best!
We loved this recipe.  Very easy to make.  Will make this again.  Thanks for posting.

I hate to go against the crowd here, but this recipe didn't really work out for us... There didn't seem to be enough of the butter/cream mixture and, unless we coated the pasta in parmesan cheese, it pretty much just seemed like we were eating plain noodles.
Finally getting around to rating this. 5 stars! I will double the sauce recipe next time because it's delicious and doesn't make enough. That's easy to fix, though. Thanks, PanNan

This is one of my family's favorite meals.  Sometimes, we saute a small can of mushrooms and 1/2 chopped onion together, and add it to the recipe for a different taste.  It's really good.  But even without the mushroom and onions, it's a great dish!

Made this tonight for the Hubby's b-day, which is also Valentines Day.  The entire family went back for seconds.  I was a little concerned that the cream mixture wasn't "creamy", but after adding it to the pasta, it literally "melts" into a wonderful sauce.  I grilled the chicken first on the G.Foreman and added some garlic & pepper seasoning.  Delicious!

I liked this recipe because you don't have to make the cream sauce in another pan. In my opinon you should add crushed fresh garlic to the creaming process listed below to add more flavor to the dish. Everyone enjoyed the dish and i would make it again.
excellent!!! so quick and easy.  A huge hit with the family.
