Checked at 1 1/2 hours and pasta was close to being done.  At exactly 2 hours we tried this dish, the noodles were cooked but seemed gummy.  I went back for seconds after letting the dish set for a while and the pasta was good but still gummy.  Still went back though for leftovers the next day for the flavor it sooo good!  Thank you for posting.
We did not enjoy this, sorry. The texture of the noodles chnaged to mush. The combo of ingredients would make a great baked casserole, but as a crockpot meal it did not go over well for us.
Waste of ingredients. At 2 hrs, rotini was totally mushed out and vegies were still crunchy. (onions & green peppers) Tomato/pizza sauce did not seem to blend well with rest of ingredients.

This was just ok.I would add an egg to the rice mixture. If I make again I`ll try stuffing it with a touch of cooked ground beef and peas. I also used 2 cups of cooked rice and this made 8 nice size balls. They browned up nicely. This sauce was good but with rice balls I like a thicker sauce.

Easy enough for a novice chef - just follow the simple directions and the outcome is a new family favorite!  All the flavors compliment each other while not being too rich, and with around 8 adult portions it works out around $2 per head to make which is very reasonable for a quality dish you would get at a nice Italian restaurant.

This was quick and easy, and turned out great!  I highly recommend it!  I halved the recipe and cooked it in an 8x8 glass dish.  I thought it was a little dry, so next time I will add closer to a whole 24 oz. jar of spaghetti sause (1 1/2 to  2 jars if making the full recipe).  I used Barilla marinara sause, and next time I will spice the sause up a little with crushed red pepper, black pepper and itailian seasoning to add more flavor.

We love this recipe.  I usually add garlic and a bit more Parmesan cheese.  Make sure you use a great sauce such as San Marzano or Rao's.  It truly makes a huge difference.  I serve the lasagna with either green beans as a side or an Italian style salad.  I also make my own garlic bread!
I have this exact recipe and serve it over fresh pasta, it is absoultley the BEST!!!!!
Excellent. I've toyed with a couple of the ingredients here and there (i.e. i add a LOT of garlic - I love garlic!) and I use it in my lasagna.

OH My. this is so good with the blue cheese. The nutmeg added a good touch. So nice and creamy, I used regular polenta, added chopped chives and parsley. DH loved it. The recipe is a keeper, thank you Rita.

This was very good!  I took it to my weekly dinner group and it got fairly good reviews.  The only negative was that it tasted too much like blue cheese ( and I used a very mild cheese).  Myself, I really enjoyed it.  I added fresh rosemary and parsley (that is what I had on hand).   I was really pleased to try this.  I have been very intimidated by polenta, thinking it would be difficult to make but it was really quite easy.  I wonder about putting it in a loaf pan and then slicing it and grilling it??  Thanks Rita for a wonderful recipe!!

I used a Danish blue cheese and fresh thyme as that is what was available. Very creamy. I would add a little chicken flavoured boullion powder to the water next time as I found it needed a touch of salt. The blue cheese amount was about right.

What a creative recipe! Tummy warming and very deliscious. I did use 1 cup of full fat milk instead of milk and cream. Still wonderfully creamy. I am thinking of adding some chopped walnuts, they go so well with blue cheese.
Chia, this is so good, loved the tarragon, didn't have fresh so used dried. Served it over rice. DH loved it. Thank you so very much for another yummy recipe.

What an easy and quick to prepare dish!  Wonderful for those times when you need a quick but satisfying meal.  I liked the subtle fresh tarragon flavor.  We like a stronger garlic flavor for scampi, so next time, I will mince the garlic and mix it with room temperature butter and olive oil ahead of time, to give more time for the garlic flavor to penetrate.

This was delicious!  It was so quick and easy; peeling and deveining the shrimp took the longest. We found half a cup of wine was plenty and we used dried tarragon.  The recipe was not clear with how much shrimp or garlic to use; we used a pound of shrimp and only one clove of garlic. Thanks Chia, we will certainly make this dish again!
Really good. I do like a more garlic flavour though.  I found adding sliced garlic early in the recipe made it too bland for me.  Next time I'll add minced garlic after the shrimp are cooked.

The tarragon makes this scampi deliciously different.  I was a little doubtful, but it really does work with the shrimp. We love garlic too and I did mince the 6 cloves to increase the flavor and bite.  The juices were happily sopped up with crusty bread. We really enjoyed this recipe, Chia.

I was in the mood for shrimp and Scampi is my fav, but was looking for something differant. Never had tarragon on it before. It was outstanding. I only used half the shrimp, as it was just me and all of the sauce, with a wee bit more butter. ;)

This tomato sauce is absolutely delicious.  This will be my regular tomato sauce from now on, seriously!  I needed tomato sauce to make nawja's chicken vindaloo, and I didnt have any, so I made yours using tons of tomatoes I had on hand. The flavors are just amazing, yet the ingredients are so simple!! I used the fresh thyme, and wouldnt use anything but fresh.

This was really good! We used it on pizza made with s'kat's Easy Pizza Dough (#16331) and s'kat's Easy Cornmeal Crust, and it was delicious. My husband normally orders his pizza with no sauce (he's not a fan of thick tomato sauce), but I spread a very light layer on the pizza, and he loved it! Thanks, s'kat, for another great recipe!
I made this sauce for the Timpano recipe and it's delicious. Too bad my crust for the Timpano didn't turn out well.
Excellent made as directed and simmered meatballs in sauce

This soup is so tasty and filling.
I was a little bit courious about cooking the meatballs in the chicken broth {I used cream of chicken soup in a can} The flavors blended beautifully.I have also added onion powder to the meatballs. This rates very highly in our family. It's a keeper. Thanks for making mealtime easier.

Comfort soup is the perfect name for this.  I made it on a rainy bummer of a day and this tasted absolutely soulful to us.  I made it with beef and I used real parmesan that I grated myself instead of the canned type, and I also used fresh spinach as you can't get frozen spinach where I live in England.  This is a delicious soup that I will make more frequently in the cooler weather.  Thank you, Olive Blossom!

This was very good... I would tweak the meatballs to add a little more flavor and perhaps some onion to the broth. Very simple to make, and was a very satisfying meal. I will definately make this again!
Will also take the advice of the other reviewers and try the other combinations of broths and add mushrooms.

great low carb meal, and indeed very hearty. i seasoned my meatball mix with some sauteed onions and garlic, italian seasonings and a pinch of curry powder. it was yummy. only problem i had was with there being too little broth. perhaps my "package" of spinach was bigger than average, because the chunks in the soup were disproportionately greater than the soup itself, but i'll definitely make this again with a smaller spinach package and/or a few more cups broth.
I doubled the recipe. and had to add seasonings, but on the whole it is a great soup..  I cooked it a bit longer then recipe

"Seaweed Soup" was not a hit in our home - way too slimy and strong flavored.

The meatballs were nice cooked in the broth, but once the spinach was added it was just not appetizing at all.

I really liked this, as did the man who ate three bowls!  I followed the recipe exactly but added some cooked pasta (rings) at the end.  Topped it with some more parmesan cheese....yummy!!!  I was told to make this one again!  Thanks!
This is very similar to my favorite comfort soup called Italian Wedding soup.  Throw in some orzo pasta at the end of your recipe and you have it! Absoulutely delicious!  Thanks for sharing.

This is a great pantry meal.  I use Asiago because we didn't have Parmesan.  I also added 1t Italian seasoning because it seemed like it needed more zing for grownups.  It was pretty good.  I will consider adding eggs like in rag soup.  Eggs are a major comfort food in our house!  I did not stay awake dreaming of this food, but will include it in my repetoire of quick meals with ingredients on hand.  Thanks for sharing!
Made the meatballs for a recipe requiring mild seasoning. Turned out to be the perfect answer.  Made them with half beef and half pork.  Delicious!  Thanks, Inkling.

YUM!  This is definitely a keeper.  So easy!!  I accidentally broke my pepper grinder into the meat & the whole peppercorns really added a punch.  I add them whole on purpose now.  I always double the recipe for my family of 5 - we eat it all up!  Sometimes there\'s a little left over for my husband to take to work for lunch.  I have used broccoli instead of spinach on occasion with good results.  And I grate my own Parmesan or Romano cheese.

This was good.  Easy to prepare ahead of time.  Sauce could use more flavoring (I'm a sauce fan).

Thanks.

Yum!  Had a great flavor, and was really easy to make.  I used fresh spinach (hate the frozen stuff!), veggie broth, and lots of seasoning.  I think I made the meatballs too big... they cooked fine, but it was pretty sloppy to eat.  There was one little bowl left for lunch the next day, and I threw in some leftover rice.  Very hearty and satisfying that way!  Thanks.

this was really good, I use a pound of frozen (still frozen)turkey meatballs, and then doubled the spinach and the rest of the ingredients and then threw it in the crockpot on low for 8 hours. Really good

I can't believe that I've never rated this recipe! We have been enjoying this soup for a couple of years now. It is delicious. Great for low carbers. I usually use ground turkey or chicken in the meatballs. I bet that ground pork would be good too. Occasionally I add a small pasta such as macaroni. I just boil the pasta in the soup for however long the package instructs.

This smells great when it is cooking!  I did start by sauteeing onions, carrots, celery, garlic and  shallots before I added the chicken stock.  To the meatballs, I also added onion powder, garlic powder and some fresh chopped parsley.  Next time, I think I will add some salt as they seemed to need a little punch.  I do skim the fat from the top to get rid of the saturated fat but I add a splash of quality olive and some fresh grated parm cheese and it gives great flavor.  Thanks for the recipe.  Will definately make again!

This is the most incredible recipe. It is so simple and super delicious. I will definately continue making it. I took a few suggestions from the other ratings (pasta, onions...) Thanks for the great recipe!

Thanks Picholine, for the great, simple recipe! I used ground venison (which has a low fat content) to make the meatballs, and it was still tasty. Served the soup with a shake of parm cheese on top, and a side of crusty italian bread. A great comfort meal for our below zero temps! And, it made the perfect amount of soup for two people, plus one meal of leftovers! I will try this with pasta as well, for a twist, but definately is not needed from our standpoint.

Mmmm, great soup, Picholine!  I used four cups each of chicken broth and beef broth (I felt like it needed extra broth - for my family, at least), and only about 1/2 a package of spinach (my kids are two and four, and all that spinach was a bit much for them).  The verdict?  Simply excellent!  Thanks so much!

I have made this more times than I can count, and I always love it.  Its great for a quick meal with sandwiches and it tastes even better the second day - - if you can manage to keep some around for leftovers.  I have tries to mess with the recipe on occasion,but to tell the truth the best way to prepare it is just like it is in recipe.  Thanks Picholine!!!
Really tasty and it's a great comfort food on chilly winter nights.

Yummy and easy.  The recipe is so simple to prepare and really delicious.  I stupidly used up all of the parmesan cheese so instead I used some bread crumbs, minced garlic, onion powder, fresh parsley, and lots of black pepper in the meatballs.  This soup is even fancy enough for company or special dinners.  Thanks for posting another winning recipe.  :)
Our family was about half and half on this.  I liked it.
this is ok - i was expecting the yummy italian wedding soup-esque flavor, and this just didn't live up to those expectations

I really enjoyed this although the kids wouldn't eat it (no surprise to me).  I used ready made, pre cooked meatballs to make it faster and easier and to clean out my fridge.  I also increased the amount of spinach used.

I really think this soup has potential, but it was a little flat for me.  I ended up adding the juice of one lemon, a little freshly grated nutmeg, and some salt.  This made a huge difference; even my children liked it (they tend to be healthy eaters, though).  I do think that I will also make the meatballs much smaller next time.  Overall, a good starting point, just needed a little brightness added to the flavor.
Love it!!  My second time making and I tweaked it a little.  Sauteed onion and mushrooms and added to the soup and it was DEE-LISH!!
I love this soup.  The meatballs are so simple but somehow so tasty.  I agree with the suggestion to make them on the small side so they are bite-sized.   It's definitely a comfort soup.

Delicious.  Will definitely make this again.  I used beef this time and added a pinch of sage and a bit of garlic to the meatballs.  I think I will use turkey next time.  I also used fresh kale 
(blanched it first) because that is what I had on hand.  Frozen spinach would just make it even simpler!

Better than I would have thought! I will echo some other comments - tweak to your spice likings (I added garlic powder to the meatballs and onions to the broth) but definitely a yummy base and a great low-carb staple. And something different to do with ground beef! Thanks!

Great soup and easy to make! I added cayenne pepper, white onion, and small pasta to make it a little heartier. I also used a veggie beef substitute, which tasted just as good, but does not form meatballs as well. If you're using a non-meat substitute for the meatballs, I'd suggest pan searing or frying the "meat" first and then adding it to the broth. If you put it directly into the broth to cook, it'll come apart almost immediately. This still tastes just as good, but doesn't look quite as attractive...

Very yummy! Made this for the 2nd time. This time I chopped an onion & sauted that with the meatballs before I added the broth to the pot. I think it added a lot of flavor. Also I was out of cheese but it was awesome any way. My 2yr old son had a 2nd bowl! How's that for a rave review?

I used 16 oz spinach instead of 10 oz  so I will rate without stars because that might have affected the flavor. We found this extremely plain and boring. The meatballs tasted like plain meat. I used ground chuck, so I don't think it was too lean. This needs something, quite a few somethings. Yes, it was easy.

Wonderful!  I used a package of fresh spinach, chopped.  I aso added some asiago cheese to the meat balls becasue I had some grated.  In total I used about 1/2 cup of parmesan/asiago but I think that extra flavor is what made this soup so addictive!  I also added six whole cloved of garlic while cooking and then fished them out at the end.  Served over rice.  YUMMM!

This was just ok for me. I followed the recipe as written, except that I used less meat (i prefer meat as a garnish rather than the main show) and less spinach, since I can only eat cooked spinach in small doses, and in fact it was some spinach i had left over from another recipe that i wanted to use up. So i halved both the meat and the spinach; after all, there were only 2 cans of liquid here. If I here to try this again, I'd add seasoned bread crumbs to the meatballs, which were rather bland. I didn't really taste the Parmesan cheese. I'd also add some orzo to the soup and make at least 1 of the 2 cans a low-sodium broth.

By the time I was done, I realized that I barely used the recipe. I used fresh spinach, a carton of beef stock, celery, garlic, Italian seasoning, cut spaghetti noodles and meatballs. Next time, I think I'll use chicken stock as suggested in the recipe. I thought it tasted pretty good. I think I would have preferred more broth next time. I thought it was a little fatty. I probably could have skimmed the top before I served it. I don't know if it's because of the stock I used or the meat? It will take some tweaking to get it perfect but I'm really happy I found this recipe.

We cooked an Australind Butcher's Corned Beef cooked with carrot, onion, celery and peppercorns, then strained the liquid and used as the stock for this recipe.  We also used mince made of pork and veal as an alternative.  Subtle flavours but delicious - I can imagine eating this when feeling unwell and needing a food hug.  Thanks Picholine.
This was fantastic and so easy to make! I added to it as it didn't seem like there were many herbs/spices. I also browned the meatballs before adding the broth to the pan.

Found the meatballs to be bland. Used 3 cans of broth as 1 seemed not soupy enough.  Added grated pecorino when serving that added some missing saltiness.  Next time will add seasonings and onions to the meat.

As indicated by another reviewer, this soup is a great base for tailoring it to your own preferences.  I did that by adding sliced carrots and 1/2 box of Ditalini pasta.  Really tasty accompanied by hot French bread.  Yum!
My husband found this recipe here and made it for dinner last night.  I HATE lasagna but this recipe has changed my mind!!!

This was very good and very easy to make.  I used the prosciutto and fontina, the fontina is a must (I've found a new cheese).  I baked the chicken in the oven for about20 minutes.  We're having the leftovers as sandwiches, can't wait for lunch.

While I thought this was very tasty my housemates just thought it was "nice". I used honey-baked ham and mozarella and I'm glad I did because I think it would have been way too salty for me with the prosciutto. I followed this up with your Strawberry Mousse (#62067)for a nice light dessert.

What a delightful bread! I actually had a recipe for focaccia bread before this, which I thought was pretty good, but I will be using this one from now on. It is light, cooks to a beautiful golden brown and easily makes two 12 inch rounds. Make sure you use fresh, real Parmesan cheese and fresh rosemary for the best taste. And I thought it got even better the next day for lunch! Worth noting: the time given to prepare and cook it is a bit misleading. If you count all the rising times you'll need at least an hour and a half from start to finish. Still, it's definitely worth the effort. Also, I only needed about 2/3 cup potato water to bring the dough together.
This was so delicous that half of it was eaten before dinner was even ready. Great Flavor and pretty easy to make. I will make this one again and again!

Well, I had to try this and seeing as it did not require a bread machine, off to making this I went!  At first I thought it may be more than I could handle, but as surprised as I was, this came out GREAT and was delicious!!  I am now the proud maker of bread, and thank you for a great focaccia recipe that I will use over and over again.  This will be great for sandwiches and you MUST use fresh herbs! :)
Rita this was very good and easy to make.  Served this with baked spaghetti that my sister and I put together for our home study group.  Thanks

With the potato, this was a bit more work than my other facaccia recipe, but the end result was very good.  I had a bit of a problem with the center not being really done when the edges were quite done.  I am wondering if I should remove the bread from the oven while it preheats up to temperature; or maybe I need to make sure my pan underneath has boiling water in it.  The flavor combination of the rosemary, olives, and parmesan was excellent.
Yum!!! Very easy to make since you're mostly using the food processor. The flavor is excellent and it rose beautifully. Highly recommended! Thanks Rita!

This is one of those "if I can do it, anybody can do it" recipes. I'm the world's worst bread baker, but I managed to turn out just about perfect focaccia with this recipe. I divided the dough in half and baked half plain and the other half with the olives and rosemary. I actually prefer the plain, but both are delicious. This has perfect focaccia texture - golden, crispy crust with chewy interior. Wonderful.

Great bread, I used olives, some sundried tomatoes and a little onion.  All three.

But loved the recipe. Turned out great.

Very delish!  This turned out so nice and moist.  Hubby asked what I was doing with a pot of water sitting in the oven, but now we know!  I added some carmelized onion to one half of the loaf and some dried tomatoes to the whole thing.  Yummy!
I did use cranberries and the cooking time was right on. This recipe does have to be kneaded. These are very generous with nuts and cranberries. Crunchy and Chewy Good! Thanks Barb!

Thanks Barb Gertz!.
I have made it many times, I have tryed many versions of it with whole weath. It is delicious and healthy, no oil, not butter, no margarine, not shortening, no lard....I love it.

great recipe!  i took a cue from a very similar recipe at marthastewart.com and increased the vanilla to 1.5 tsp. and added 1 t. lemon zest.  also, i don't know if my eggs were too small, but the dough seemed too dry, so i added another egg to make the dough stick together.  i think i should've added a little more time in the oven b/c it was a little doughy in the middle, but they still turned out great and hardened up nicely after cooling.
this was good! except it was VERY VERY DRY so I added another egg .. they came out tastey just kinda flat though
The dough DEFINITELY was dry. I also think the baking time was too long...for my oven, at least.  The recipe, overall was o.k...I think I will stick to my old one, though.

Like others, I found that the batter was too dry.  In fact, I could not make it stick together at all, and today is a very damp day.  I looked up other biscotti recipes and they all contained butter, so I added 1/2 cup of butter, and zap!  Wonderful!  Everything worked as described and the family loves it!

I thought this worked out very well!  The taste is excellent and it comes out just like a pretty coffee drink you would get in a European cafe.  I used freshly brewed espresso and then proceeded with the rest of the recipe.  Also,I didn't notice until after I had already prepared this successfully with skim milk that I was supposed to use whole.  I thought it was just wonderful using the skim milk and it frothed up fine using a wand style blender.  Thanks for sharing.

I've been trying to make this for a year, ever since I had it at a cafe in Galveston, TX. Have tried several other methods but it never would layer. This worked great first try! I used 1% milk and a hand frother in an Irish coffe mug. Perfect.

I haven't tried this method but I do know that the less fat in the milk the better frothing it is. I have a cappucino maker so I will try this using it. I've heard of the Macchiato  but I read the Macchiato means mark... because the espresso leaves a mark in the froth. Either way it's attractive when served in a glass.

i am amazed at this recipe!  Having just returned from my honeymoon in otaly i was desperate to re-kindle the experience i had of enjoying the latte machiatto overlooking the glorious views of Lake Garda.  This recipe is fantastic.  I thought i was going to find it hard to find instant espresso powder, but my local supermarket stoked it!  I followed the recipe and was amazed at the results!  I even took a photograph!!  Thank you so much for helping me to revive my honeymoon memories!

This was new to me and I loved it.  I used 2% milk and not quite the required amount of espresso powder (all I had in the pantry).  It was delicious and surprisingly sweet for something with no added sugar.  Can't wait to make this for my coffee-loving SIL.  Thanks, I know I'll be repeating this often.

I have an espresso/cappuccino machine, but lost the frothing tube.  Never thought about heating up the milk and then whipping it up in the blender.  Now I can enjoy lattes and cappuccino at home again, so thanks for sharing.  Also, I added about a tablespoon of simple syrup into the blender with the milk since a like it to be a little sweet.
I made this with regular soy milk and brewed espresso and it was fabulous!  Thanks for posting the recipe!  Much cheaper than going to the local coffee shop... and better, too.

Don't let the # of steps (27) fool you - this is a very easy recipe & absolutely delicious - in fact, its almost the same as my own recipe - for which, I've never measured the spices! 
I used ground beef, olive oil & red pepper flakes - no mushrooms, olives or bell pepper & simmered for 4 hours - the sauce was thick & tasty. Thanx Wally!

Without a doubt, the best spaghetti I've ever had.  For the optional ingredients I used ground beef and sliced mushrooms.  For the spices I used 1 tbsp dried oregano, 1 tbsp dried basil, 1/2 tsp dried thyme, 1 tsp fresh rosemary, 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, a sprinkling of garlic and onion powders, and 3 bay leaves.  Besides the flavor, the best part is that it makes plenty for the freezer for future easy weeknights.  This wonderful recipe is going into my Perfection cookbook - very few make that one.

I chose to make this from Pic A chef 07. I chose to freeze mine and have this on hand when I was ready for a great sauce now that it is getting hot out. I put mine in freezer zip loc bags layed flat until frozen then stacked up along the door. This one you do not want to loose in the freezer.  Excellant, changed nothing.  Thanks for posting this for us to try.

Simple great-tasting middle-of-the-week dish that will wait for you. We enjoyed this dish with Multi-Grain and More Bread recipe#52795. Thanks Lorac for posting this keeper recipe. We will definitely be having this often.

Carol, you have a winner in this one!  The flavors of the herbs combined with the sausage brought out the best of the canned beans (I used cannellini).  This is a hearty, and filling dish with plenty of flavor.  Thanks for sharing this tasty recipe that is now in my t&t cookbook. :-)

We really enjoyed this one!  I was pinched for time and rather than chopping the garlic & onion, I had a can of diced tomatoes seasoned with garlic and onion.  I also added 1 tsp of Italian seasoning, which includes the rosemary, oregano and basil. It was so easy and quick to whip up and so flavorful.  What a tummy warmer this will be when fall/winter comes, if I can wait that long.  Thanks Lorac!

Really great!Be sure to serve with crusty bread or rolls to soak up the great juices!  This will make a terrific supper on my late nights at work.  I'm sure we'll be having this again and again!  Thank you.

I love anything with kielbasa, and this is excellent. The seasoning was perfect and not over powering. 
Added some chopped fresh spinach at the end. It plated up really nice with the colors of the veggies. Great with a good bread.
Didn't have high hopes b/c the recipe seemed too simple, but my husband RAVED!
Very good with cornbread! The rosemary adds a neat twist; thanks.
Oh, yum!  Used a can of butter beans, threw in some green peppers with the onion and then some corn later on. Very rich and filling. So easy and so tasty. Thanks Lorac!

I took another reviewer's suggestion and added spinach, but went a step further and sprinkled mozzarella atop each serving. I also substituted thyme for rosemary and didn't remove the meat to cook the onions. I will definitely make this again, but add another can of beans to balance out the meat and stretch it further.  Thanks for an easy and super delicious recipe!

This is great. I used turkey kielbasa and omitted the butter. I, too, left the meat in when cooking the onion/garlic. This is a great low-carb meal. It's flavorful and filling. I like the idea of adding spinach at the end, and I think next time I'll also add a 2nd can of beans (I used Great Northern) to stretch it more.

I declare this absoulutely delicious! DH who normally does not like Keilbasa ate 2 bowls!  I confess I followed the directions to the tee and then put it in the crockpot and let it just simmer. It was like a soup and stew at the same time! I served it with cornbread and DH declared it a good southern meal! :) It was so cold out today and this was a good stick to your ribs meal!  Thank you for sharing a great recipe!
This was so good and easy also!  I cant believe how much I liked it.  Thanks so much!  I substituted 1/2 env.onvion soup mix for the onion and 12 oz. size can of navy beans. GREAT!!!!!!!
This was a great and filling dinner!  Quick too!  Four stars only because my daughter didn't like the beans.  It was even better the next day for lunch.

This is a really good recipe.  I didn't have navy beans (Discovered this when the onions and spices were already in the pan---eeeeek.)  In a pinch, I used kidney beans.  The dish was wonderful and the family ate every last bite.  Just think what the recipe would have tasted like, had I all the ingredients.  I can't wait to make it again, the right way.

A super fast dinner from the pantry that everyone in my family enjoyed! I made as directed except using a nonstick skillet and pouring off the fat after cooking the sausage. I'm always looking for quick meals for baseball nights, this is sure to become a favorite. Thanks, Lorac!

This was very good and quick to make. Great for nights when my boys have baseball and soccer.Made it exactly as directed and sprinkled with fresh mozzarella cheese. I served it with a caesar salad and sourdough bread.

Hey there Carol! I made this tonite for dinner and really enjoyed it. I am not a big fan of diced tomatoes and next time will just use another can of great northerns (what I used tonite). Other than that, great use of kielbasa and I will be checking out your other recipes using it! Thanks!
This is so great and easy to make.  Served with perogies.  Yum !  And great leftovers for lunch !

Wonderful flavor & easy to make.  I halved the recipe for the 2 of us & had to sub with what I had on hand - used Hillshire Farms Lite smoked sausage, a small can of limas & threw in a cubed, medium potato just for grins.  I just ate the leftovers & I think it got even tastier as it sat in the fridge for a day.  Thanks for sharing a winner!

We really liked these.  I good stay with you meal.
Margie

I loved this recipe. Never would have thought that these flavors would meld together so good, but they really do.Simple, budget friendly, and taste  comforting. I will definately add this to my regular list. Thanks for the recipe.
My DH and I couldn't get enough of this!  I will definitely double the recipe so we have LOTS more!  Thanks for such a great recipe.
This was quick and easy! The seasoning was perfect and the few ingredients complemented one another. Next time I would add the cheese as one reviewer suggested. Thanks!

Totally delicious comfort food!  We loved how such simple ingredients and quick preparation blended into such a wonderful dish. I served this with crackling bread and the whole family raved. This recipe is my favorite! Alot of people would think making the crepes take too much time and prefer to buy the Manicotti shells, but try this once.  Once you do, you'll never buy storebought again!  Another thing that i love to do is make several batches of the cheese filled crepes and lay them on a baking sheet.  I put them in the freezer till frozen.  Once frozen i put them in a ziplock bag and try to remove as much of the air as i can.  They freeze very well and that way whenever you feel like having a big "sunday meal" just put a layer of sauce on the bottom of a 13x9 baking dish...add the frozen Manicotti and again put another layer of Sauce. During the last 5 minutes, remove foil and add a layer of shredded mozarella.  put back in over till melted.  take out of over and let sit about 5-10 minutes and enjoy!
