Delicious soup!  Tastes exactly like the Olive Garden.  A keeper for sure!

I can't say it was good. It was only fair. I didn't use as many beans as it called for, because I knew it would be too many, still had a beany taste though. No body, nothing melded together. I tried it this morning and still got the same taste. I've tasted Olive Garden's soup, this is not it. Sorry. I'm sticking with Giada's recipe. Now that's a great minestrone!

This soup is amazing! Even if it's not EXACTLY like Olive Garden's, it's just as delicious. I have a friend who has told me it's some of the best she's ever had! I changed it a little bit: I only added one can of each of the beans, doubled the amount of water, eyeballed the amount of vegetables (probably more than what the recipe calls for), sliced (instead of chopped) the zucchini, and per recommendation of other reviewers, added in a can of tomato paste. I also didn't drain the diced tomatoes or add as much spinach. Didn't have any red wine on hand, but next time I'll definitely have to try that.

I read this recipe and it sounded delicious. That is how I start most of my recipes, is to start with one that is good to begin with.  I like meat in my soups so I started with about 1 1/2 lbs. of mild Italian sausage, casings removed and sauted until cooked and slightly browned.  Drain grease.  Add onions, green beans, celery and garlic.  Saute. Instead of 4 cups vegetable broth I used 2 - 1 Litre tetra boxes of vegetable broth and minus the hot water.  I also used 4 cups Italian stewed (homemade) instead of the diced tomatoes plus I did not drained the tomatoes.  As the tomatoes were Italian, I also did not use the spices, although if I had used regular stewed tomatoes I would have used the spices stated.  I also used 3/4 cup of small shell pasta.  I also used only 1 can each of the beans.  This made for a very delicious and hearty soup. I thank you for my good beginnings.
This soup was fabulous and very easy!
Wonderful!  I only used i can of each bean and used ditalini pasta instead of shells.
My whole family loves this soup even my three year old daughter who does not usually eat many vegetables!  This recipe is not exactly like Olive Gardens but it is close and so good!

Thank you Todd for sharing this recipe. I made the soup according to your recipe with all the suggested ingrediants and it was perfect. It's a very hearthy, fiber rich soup. My entire family loves it and I'm making it again today!
I made half a recipe as written minus the zucchini. Wonderful soup for a cold, snowy day we are having.  Served with Recipe #13584 toasted in the oven.

This is a wonderful soup at any time of the year!  This week I went to Olive Garden, and as usual, ordered the soup.  My waitperson said that they don't give out the recipe, but she did tell me that they put Chianti in it.  Is this correct??

I just have to say that the wine makes all of the difference in this recipe. It's good without it...but it's totally Olive Garden's soup with it. I used about 1/2 cup of Yellowtail Shiraz in the last 15-20 minutes. When it was done I nearly died. This is seriously the secret to Olive Garden's minestrone!!!!!!
Awesome! Used stewed tomatoes cuz that is what i had on hand.
I made this recipe several times so far.  It is excellent .... worth trying!

I've never had the Olive Garden soup but this was delicious!  Made the soup pretty much as indicated except that I did not drain the tomatoes, added a bit more veggies, left out the pasta, and used unsalted vegetable broth (I like to control the amount of salt myself later after cooking is complete).  Delicious!

Though it did come close it wasn't what I was hoping for. I tried it again with the broth (swansons vegetable broth) suggested, once I came across some, and it was just not good at all... looked and tasted more like a chinese soup recipe... :(

This soup was ALMOST EXACTLY like Olive Garden's minestrone. SO GOOD!  Thanks Todd!  When I first tasted it it was really good but, I thought it wasn't quite as red or tomato-y as Olive Garden's so I added a very small 5.5 oz can of low-sodium V-8 juice and it was perfect! Excellent! I used regular frozen green beans because I couldn't find the french cut. I didn't drain the tomatoes either. I felt it was a little thicker than I'd like so next time I'll be making some of the changes recommended by other reviewers. Thanks for a great starting point!
I'll add my five star review to the list. Great soup. I added the wine, doubled the carrots and celery and used diced tomatoes with green peppers. Thanks for posting such a delicious recipe.

I want to give 4.5. I thought it was delicious, but I agree with a few other reviewers, there was just that certain something missing. I will use on a rotation because it is really tasty and very healthy.

Yum!! I tasted the soup with no red wine, and decided that it "needed" something. I had doubled the recipe and so for wine quantity added about a cup of a really nice Zin. i love this soup !!

This soup is really good, especially on a cold winters day.  I doubled the recipe but kept the amount of beans the same & there were still plenty of beans in the soup. I also added a small can of tomato puree for a more pronounced tomato flavour, didn't bother to drain the diced tomatoes & used only veggie stock (no water) .  I will be making this one again.  Thanks for sharing!

MAKE IT, MAKE IT MAKE IT!!!!  I followed the recipe and added a cup of dry red wine while it was simmering with the noodles and spinach.   Fresh grated parmigiano-reggiano and you have yourself a bowl of heaven.   One of the best recipes I've tried and will quickly become a family favorite around here.

O-M-G!!!  If I could give this 10 stars I would!!  SO DELISH!  I am on Weight Watchers and this recipe is so point friendly.  You can add as many vegetables or as little as you like and it won't change the point value!  I only add 1 can of kidney beans and 1 can of white beans (instead of 2 each).  You will never miss those two cans!!!  I also like to add a 6 oz can of tomato paste to give the base more of a tomato flavor!  You can add the red wine if you like, but I would rather not have the extra points and I don't think you will miss it either!!  And if you like things spicy like I do, add a few splashes of Tabasco!!  I also add a little shredded parmesan cheese on top!  So delicious!!  You have to try this recipe if you love Minestrone soup.  I think this recipe is even better than Olive Garden's!!!  I use to work at Olive Garden and had a copy of their recipe.  The list of ingredients in their recipe was twice as long as this and they definitely add red wine.  To each his own!  You really can't mess this recipe up!  So, so, so good!  I can't say it enough!

I am stunned! This is one of the best soups I have ever eaten. I didn't have any zucchini though, so had to go without. And I did add some salt at the end after it was done. I have never had this soup at Olive Garden, but if it tastes like this, they should sell it by the gallon.

Truly delicious!!! I followed the recipe exactly, then tasted. I decided it needed more pasta and tomato so I added more shells and chopped up a can of stewed tomatoes and added it sauce and all. Garnished with fresh parm and Italian bread to sop it all up!  So good and so healthy! My 2 year old loves it too!

This soup is amazing!  I've been searching for years for a good minestrone soup.  I followed a few suggestions that others had posted.  I didn't add extra salt, didn't drain the tomatoes and added 2 cans of small white beans and 1 can of kidney....  I added 3/4 cup of pasta shells and next time will do 1 cup.  I added about 1/4 cup of tomato paste after all the main ingredients were in.....Also added 1/2 cup of Chianti when I added the spinach, which I did a rough chop on.  This will be a staple in this house and it was relatively quick and easy to make :)

This recipe is great and is an excellent meal to make for company. You can visit while it is simmering and many compliments are paid when it is done! It however needs a few tweaks. I fully agree it needs red wine. I use whatever kind I have on hand. I add 1/4 a cup to 1/2 a cup depending on how strong the wine is. DO NOT DRAIN THE TOMATOES! I add an extra 1/4 a cup of tomato sauce or V8 juice to get more flavor in the broth. I always use fresh ingredients and so the thyme, oregano, and basil were fresh and minced and that really jazzed it up,. Finally, I felt there was not enough broth (it%u2019s easy to go overboard with the vegetables). To fix this, on the side in a separate saucepan, I mixed 3 cups of vegetable broth, 2  1/2 cups hot water, and 1/4 a cup of tomato sauce/V8 juice to a boil then added 1/4 a cup of red wine and brought it to a boil again then let it simmer alongside the soup. You can just not do this part separately and just add it to the soup but I did it this way so I could store some broth separately for leftovers. That way, the liquid that is lost in the refrigerator can be restored. When I serve, I mix this in with the soup and it doesn't taste any different.

This soup is delicious.  I added four different cans of beans, kidney, cannelli, black, and garbonzo.  I also increased the pasta to 3/4 cup and added a half cup of red cooking wine.  I am addicted to this soup!!!!!!
Best soup ever!  Always liked by guests!  DO NOT forget the red wine!  It does the make the difference!

Made this and took it to a "Darden Dinner"  (we don't have the wonderful Darden restaurants--Olive Garden & Red Lobster, etc here, so we made our own).  It was by far the best-loved dish there!  SOOOO goooooood.  I did add in some red wine once the veggies were sweated down and I left out the beans due to personal preference.  Divine!

I made this soup tonight and it was AWESOME!  I doubled the pasta, added 1/2 cup of red wine and a small can of tomato paste.  My husband, you really isnt a "soup guy", had two bowls! He loved it. I would say this is the best soup I've made. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

DELISH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I made this dish to take to work for lunch and it was so hearty and healthy! I enjoyed every bite without guilt! Thanks for sharing!

Delicious soup.  Since I knew that I wanted leftovers for work, I added another cup of water, and proportionately increased the veggies in the soup.  Like others, I added 1/2 cup of red wine.  Also, this recipe allowed me to sneak in some spinach into a meal to unsuspecting parties who just devoured the soup.  Thank you for the recipe!

Made this tonight!  It was really great!  I didn't think it was as good as OG's, but that was probably because I didn't use red wine.  I only had white cooking wine so I used a half cup of that.  I also added the tomato paste, an extra can of veg. broth, extra veggies, and one extra cup of pasta.  This made enough for supper, lunch, and left some to freeze for 5 people.  I will be making this again!  Love that it is so healthy!

Absolutely perfect!
I used to be a server at OG and this is spot on..red wine is a must for it to taste like theirs.:) Sooo loved this!!!

This was a very nice soup. Was it Olive Garden Minestrone ... NO. There was a few flavors off, not enough tomato flavor and depth of flavors. Spinach, MY OG does not add spinach, but ...
Yes, this was a very nice soup. And I did enjoy it. And yes, there is a little red wine vinegar at the end of cooking, but also red wine in the broth. NOW, everyone has to remember, that a lot of their ingredients are commercial, so we can't duplicate it exactly. But this was very nice.
I added a bit of tomato paste for a little richness, and as I said ... it is close, and very good which is why I gave it 5 stars. I just can't say it is just like OG's recipe.
But definitely worth making!

Great Soup!  I did make a few adjustments.  I did not chop my celery, I sliced it with leaves.  I did not add my garlic or zucchini (sliced) until I added my spinach.  I hate mushy zucchini and I wanted the garlic punch.  I did not drain my tomatoes.  After reading the reviews about adding tomato paste I thought why toss out all that good juice.  Due to the added liquid and the fact that I cook my pasta per servings in a separate pot (due to freezing) I only added 2 cups of hot water.  I did add the 1/2 cup red wine and about 1 T. red wine vinegar with about 15 minutes to go.  I topped it with grated asiago at the table.  I'm in soup heaven!  Thanks for posting!  Di ;-)

This has become one of my favorite soups.  Love it!  Have never had the Olive Garden minestrone, so I can't compare, and I did make a few changes to this recipe.  Did not drain the tomatoes, used chicken Better Than Bullion rather than veg broth, did not add wine or pasta.
I love this soup!  At Olive Garden I always order their minestrone soup and this was just as good as theirs!  I didn't add the red wine (personal reasons) and it was still a great.
This is a very hearty soup and there is a ton of it for leftovers.  I am only giving it three stars, because it seemed to need a bit more seasoning for my tastes. Thank you for sharing.

This has become a staple, so much so that I freeze sufficient prepared zucchini and green beans for this winter treat. Have followed suggestions to include tomato paste, undrained tomatoes, red wine, parmesan rind and double garlic. I found the bought stock too salty and use only my own. This is further from the original recipe, but I also substitute cavelo nero from my garden for the spinach. Blend it up with some water and add. A hearty soup indeed.
Probably the most flavorful minestrone I have made to date, but I still think it could use some improvement. I personally would have liked a more savory, tomato-y broth; maybe even a little sausage.

We absolutely loved this soup.  I added a small can of tomato paste, used Italian stewed tomatoes which I had on hand, and added 2/3 cup red wine.  I had to use half chicken broth, because I live in a hick town that doesn't have veggie broth.  And I only used 1 can each of the beans because, really, 4 cans is just too much!  Now if I could just have some OG breadsticks and salad with it...

This is truly a great minestrone recipe.  When I told my husband it was a copycat of Olive Garden's soup, he said it was better! If you'd like to see the modified version of this recipe and additional pictures, it can be found on my cooking blog:  http://redlab27.alissahebert.com/2011/09/minestrone-soup.html
I used this recipe in a cooking class for kids... it was an absolute hit!!! It is now a staple in my home as well.

This soup is absolutely amazing. I did use fresh basil, which makes a huge difference. I used half the beans and I used broken up thin spaghetti for the pasta. It was so good that I couldn't get enough of it. I stopped by Olive Garden recently and ordered a bowl of theirs. Honestly, it wasn't as good and the sea shell pasta was too much pasta for the amount of soup. This is much better. Thank you for this amazing soup.

I am usually so anal about avoiding those two things. Oh well. The soup is good. Next time I'll make it with different veggie stock and try adding red wine. Tasted like Olive Garden, but I think wine would give it more nice depth like others suggested. Thanks!

Delicious!  I made as exactly as posted and was rewarded with a flavorful and hearty soup.  I've never had this at Olive Garden, so I don't know how it compares, but it's wonderful in its own right.  Thanks for sharing!
Good, easy, filling, and healthy! As per other users' suggestion, I added half a cup of red wine at the end of the cooking.

I have made this so many times and shared it just as many. It always turns out, even if I'm missing an ingredient or two. This is one of my all-time favorite soups and I always try to make it exactly like the recipe states. I'm sure alterations would be good, too, but I just don't want to mess with a GREAT thing!

DD was less than thrilled with the idea of eating a soup filled with beans and spinach.  But she was more than willing to give it a try once she got a whiff of it cooking.  "That smells sooooo good!"  Well I guess it didn't disappoint.  Everyone in my family gave it 4 or 5 stars, which is excellent coming from this crew.  Thanks so much for a wonderful recipe.

This is really good. I had to sub kale for spinach as I am allergic to spinach. I have never had olive gardens for that reason. I followed a couple of suggestions of another reviewer. I added a can of tomatoes, half head of cabbage, extra cup of green beans, a handful of Parmesan cheese, and a couple splashes red wine vinegar, omitted a can of beans. I will make again.

Yum~  I cut the beans in half and added extra veggies and noodles.  Also threw in some red bell pepper that needed used up in the fridge. This delicious vegetable soup is an important part of the Northern Italian repertoire. Naturally, there is a lot of latitude in a recipe such as this one in terms of ingredients and quantities. For personal preference I leave out green beans, peas and prosciutto, but I think leeks and spinach are inspired choices. I prefer pinto beans (fagioli borlotti) to canellini. I also don't use extravirgin oil, since it has a definite taste and body which is incompatible with this soup. I do add a big pat of butter to the regular olive oil. The method could be enhanced by adding the vegetables sequentially to the saute, each for two minutes. The broth could be a mixture of dilute beef, chicken or vegetable stock. The soup should not be served hothothot. It is best served comfortably warm in the winter, and in the summer it can be served tepid or even at room temperature, making it a pleasant alternative to pasta. If you let your soup cool down a bit, though, the rice will suck up all the broth and become too thick. Thus, if you add rice, cook it for only 5-10 minutes before turning off the heat, or even cook it separately and stir it in just before serving. My major criticisms, though, are two: 1) it needs to be cooked on low heat for MUCH longer, at least two hours before adding the beans. The vegetables should be soft; 2) the flavored oil is not traditional, particularly the oregano, and not helpful. Bean-based Tuscan soups may be served with flavored oil, but never alla milanese. A little chopped fresh basil added just before serving would be OK.

Update: as I've prepared this recipe about 5 times since writing this review, I've noted a few things.  Not everyone in our house likes celery and carrots, so I kept the veggie pieces large (3" long) so that people were able to remove them easily.  The large chunks of veg made this a chewier, more satisfying soup to eat on its own, but I still eat this with crackers and cheddar.  I doubled the amount of tomatoes this last time, and it produced an acceptable flavor.  Reduced-sodium chicken bouillion cubes are okay in this soup, but be prepared for the decrease in flavor if you use them in place of broth.  And if you accidentally buy quick barley instead of regular barley, it's okay to cook the quick barley separate from the soup on stovetop or in microwave, and throw in as much cooked barley as you like during the last half hour of the soup cooking.  Hope this helps!

I adapted the recipe for stovetop, since I don't have a crockpot. I sauted the veggies and minced garlic in olive oil and the herbs. Important: I more than doubled the garlic, and doubled the herbs, to suit our tastes. I doubled the barley, and cut down on the liquid (I used mostly my homemade rabbit stock, and added some water). I ended up with a nice stew-like texture. Since it's sometimes hard to know how a soup will turn out with barley in the mix, I will add about another cup of liquid next time (and there will be a next time!). I finished it with balsamic vinegar, which really added to the Italian flair, and put the soup to over the top goodness. =) Forgot the parsley, or ran out of energy to chop it, but it would have been a tasty addition. Anyway, this soup is going in my permanent cookbook. I served it with salad and breadsticks. Oh, almost forgot! Don't forget to add some salt! I figure about a teaspoon of sea salt would be perfect (I approximated), or split it between sea salt and garlic salt... yum! The salt should be written into the recipe more clearly, because I'm betting that at least some of the reviews that called this soup bland and tasteless forgot to add salt to taste at the end.

I thought this was fantastic. Made as directed, BUT I didn't make mine vegetarian - I used 6 cups of chicken broth and added a pound of crumbled italian turkey sausage. Also added about a cup of pasta sauce to give it even more of an italian feel. Grate fresh parmesan on top, too! Everyone LOVED it. Thanks!

This is a good base recipe, but I had to tweak it a little to suit my tastes. I added some destemmed kale to the slowcooker about 45 minutes before it was supposed to be done for some added nutrition. I've tried stirring in pesto, and that flavored it a little. I also tried adding balsamic vinegar, which adds a nice flavor, but is not what I am expecting from a soup. It's missing something, but maybe it'll taste better tomorrow.

Very good soup. I followed all directions and also added a little bit of tomato juice I had in the fridge (maybe 6oz). This soup was perfect to make on a rainy day and is very filling. I love that it is so healthy!
Update: I have this soup (with some variations added or subtracted) EVERY day for lunch. Low calorie, very filling and I can make enough to last me awhile!
This soup is excellent. I would give it 10 stars if I could. The only change that I made was to cook it on top of the stove, for 60 minutes, because I was in a hurry for dinner. Thanks.
Easy and delicious. Made as written. Thanks!

Not bad...a little bland. And I did add salt and pepper, but added extra vinegar and about 1/4 cup of pickle juice...(my newest favourite soup addition - dill pickle soup anyone?!)Definitely hearty although I have to say I probably won't make it again.
This was really good, simple to make, and easily adaptable to individual tastes.  Thank you, I will be making this again!

Super delicious and so easy to make!  My husband and I are trying to eat healthier and lose some weight and this is a great soup to have around for a low-fat snacks or an easy meal.  I even freeze some in individual servings.  I love this recipe!

Great autumn afternoon soup.  My vegetables were fresh from the farm stand.  Although listed as optional, the cider vinegar is important for additional flavor.  The combination of lentils and barley was an unexpected treat.

No need to cook anything in advance or make this a difficult recipe.  Just put it all in the crockpot as directed.  Ours took 5 hrs on high.  I did try balsamic vinegar as one review suggested and would NOT endorse that idea because it adds too much sweetness.
I needed to use up the barley and lentils I had and this was a great way to do that. It was very filling and made a lot so I froze portions for later on since it's just the two of us. Thanks!

I really liked this recipe. I cooked it over night and made the following changes: <br/>- I didn't have broth, so I added 6 cups of water and 4 bouillon cubes (the tiny ones)<br/>- I only had quick barley in the house, so I added 1/3 cup once I woke up and waited about 30 minutes. It cooked perfectly<br/>- I added 2 bay leafs instead of one
We liked this soup, but did not love it. We thought the herbs were a little overwhelming. Next time I make this and I will do make it again, I will add more garlic and add black pepper.

This was a hit, especially with the four year old.  If the little one eats it, and he at 10 of them, then it's got to be ok.  For my personal taste, the sauce was a little bland, and next time I may try a ready made pizza or pasta sauce.  I also like the copycat version of Pizza Huts' stuffed crust pizza sauce, but this is a recipe that we will make again.  Thanks kellie2
This was very easy to put together for a quick lunch.  I think the sauce could use a bit more zing....but all in all it was good!  Thank you for posting this recipe!

Loved these little pizza bites. Reading the other reviews about the sauce being bland, I added extra oregano, added garlic powder, and just a smidgen of salt to taste and they were fabulous. Thanks for the recipe, I will use it again.
Really easy and really yummy!  Thanks, Chris!! :)

While not the healthiest choice, this made for a very yummy dinner for our family.  The LOVED the meat filling.  I think I might use the filling again with a homemade bread dough recipe.  THanks so much for the keeper.

Thanks for a great family recipe.  My husband and kids all liked these.  Since I only had one packet of crescent rolls, I used the remaining filling on a zucchini that I sliced in half (long way) and hollowed out.  This was great too!

This was really good.
I used pizza sauce, and I doubled the amount of cheese, I still think it needed a little more cheese. Instead of ground beef I used cut up meatball.

These were great!  I substituted cream cheese for sauce since we really don't care that much for it and used chicken...everyone here at the Family Circus gobbled them up!  Even doubled the recipe!  Thanks.

My guys eat alot of these and they can be expensive.  I looked for a recipe to make my own and this is a great one.  Use green peppers not red - the red get too mushy.  I made 2 gallon jars and about 1/2 dozen quarts last year.  Will make more soon.

Loved this recipe.  I've made about 2 qts so far and plan to do another 3 or 4 qts.  The pickling in vinegar seems to work well preserving the crunch of the peppers.  I agree with the other comment, you should only use the green cherry peppers.  The reds, despite being pickled are too soft.  Great recipe.  Thanks so much.

Uncle Bill, this is fantastic.  I followed your recipe exactly but I used vegetable stock instead of water because I had some I needed to use up.  My husband takes soup for lunch in the winter and he raved about this when he came home. Thanks for another great recipe.

Thanks, Uncle Bill! We had this soup for supper last night and it was so good. I, too, used vegetable broth instead of water and other than that I followed the recipe. The flavor is so hearty and you don't miss having any meat in the soup. This is a keeper for our family. Carole in Orlando

This is just the flavor I was looking for in a minestrone soup when I was searching the web for a recipe. It tastes so much like the one at a local cafe that I like. I might add cubed red potatoes next time.

Excellent minestrone and sooo easy.  My kind of recipe.  Hard to believe you can have so much flavor in just 40 minutes but it's true.  Used broth instead of water but otherwise didn't change a thing.

Excellent recipe!  I made as posted except I used kidney beans (all I had) and left out the celery.  I think this would taste great with a splash of wine in it as well.  The recipe is a keeper!  Thanks for posting!

I'm really sorry, but I followed this recipe to the letter and found it bland.  I would definitely use a good stock to boost the flavour.  On the plus side, I felt like I was eating something VERY good for me, and it was fast and easy to put together.

How is easy is this?  Chop up a bunch of vegetables and end up with a hearty and filling soup. My coworkers are all sick right now and I brought a quart of this into the office.  Lots of slurping and smiles. I doubled the oregano and otherwise followed the reicpe.  Thanks Uncle Bill.
Had to come back and say - it is even more delicious the next day!

Thanks again Uncle Bill for a truly delicious (and healthy) soup.  I followed the recipe exactly but we found it needed additional salt and pepper once it was served.  I have to agree with Xanthe.....it was even more delicious the next day.   Yum!!
This is an excellent flavourful tasting soup.  I do feel that more liquid should be added.  I will certainly make this again.

Very delightful soup.  I did add a small amount of vegetable bouillon. I like very much that the soup is not over-spiced.  You can taste all the individual flavors of the vegetables without them being masked by a strong-flavored broth.

This is an easy recipe to prepare and it results in a delicious and healthy soup!  I did add an extra clove of garlic, but that's normal for me.  I also added one can of vegetable broth.  Thank you for yet another delightfully delicious, quick and healthy meal Uncle Bill!
Easy and yummy. I used vegetable broth and cut back on the celery. I used canned tomatoes with red peppers and left out the zucchini. It tasted even better the next day.

Uncle Bill, this was very good! What a nice way to use up some zucchini I got from my dd Jen. I did however, substituted 2 (14.5 oz.) cans chicken broth for the water, (which I got 3-1/2 cups of broth) and I also substituted Mrs. Dash Tableblend Salt-Free Seasoning for the regular salt. I accidentally added 1/4 tsp. black pepper, (instead of the 1/8 tsp. which the recipe called for) but it still tasted great. I also added the whole (15 oz.) can of Progresso's Cannellini Beans, (drained)  but I added it during the last 10 minutes of cooking time, when I added the ditalini (so they wouldn't become mushy). Who ever makes this recipe, please don't forget to add the canned tomatoes, which wasn't mentioned (to add it) in the directions. I will definitely be making this soup again. Thanx for recipe Uncle Bill.
Really good! I used pinto beans cause I had just cooked a bunch up in the crockpot, and shell macaroni, cause I had just the right amount. My  DH and I loved it. Thank you Uncle Bill!
Really good!  I added a can of kidney beans, half a can of green beans, some corn and an extra can of crushed tomatoes.  Everyone loved it and I will definitely make this again and again.  Thanks!

It's fall and I had a taste for minnestrone soup.  I'm so glad I found this recipe cause it's so easy and very flavorful.  Like many others, I added broth instead using all the water the recipe called for.  Thanks for a great recipe Uncle Bill.
This was very good.  I made as directed with two exceptions: used 2 cans of vegetable broth in place of some of the water....and added a can of green beans.  Thanks for posting this, Uncle Bill.

Another great recipe from Uncle Bill! My husband really liked that the celery kept its crunch alongside the chewy macaroni. I didn't really change a thing, only added the full veggies rather than measure them out. That bulked up a soup a bit, so I used a 28oz can of tomatoes and vegetable broth rather than water. I added some string beans, too, because I had some handy. It made plenty of soup to keep us full for days. Lots of chunks and loads of flavor - terrific minestrone!

Grrrrrrrrrrrreat soup. Being a crockpot person, after sauteing the onions I threw everything into the crockpot and let it cook on low all day. In place of the water I used 6c vegetable stock. Also for the tomatoes I used one can chopped with liquid and a 28oz can crushed tomatoes. Cooked my macaroni seperate and added the last half hr or so before serving. My daughter says it's the best soup she's ever had....and I make many different soups. Thanks

A tasty soup. It was a little too 'watery' and plain for my taste despite following the instructions, so I used clear vegetable stock instead of water, used 2 tablespoons more virgin olive oil and sauteed it on low flame for a couple more minutes to infuse the onion taste. I also used fresh tomatoes and used potatoes instead of macaroni. A superb dish - I'll be making this for many more years to come. :)
I subbed out the water for vegetable broth and added a can of tomato juice.  It had a ton of flavor and was very filling.  2 points for those on WW.  Thanks!
Very good.  My husband asked me to add sliced kielbasa since he's not a vegetarian soup fan and it was a very nice addition.

I'm not going to rate it because I changed the recipe, but I doubled the recipe, used vegetable broth in place of the water, and pureed one half of the canned tomatoes. I also added more salt and pepper than called for, and wasn't terribly precise about measuring the vegetables. It worked well with the changes, and I'll definitely use it again as a great starting point for minestrone. Thanks!

This is ok, made per the recipe, however I think it needs more tomato taste.  (Also, the directions do not indicate when to add the canned tomatoes, so I added them with the rest of the veggies.)  The vegetables are good, I think next time I will use tomato or vegetable juice instead of water to give it more of a tomato taste.  Thanks Uncle Bill.

Beautiful presentation, simple, and delicious. Added 1 cup green beans, 1/2 cup kidney beans, and 1/3 cup chopped green pepper, all ingredients fit in nicely. Hearty meal when you're feeling a bit under the weather too. Parmesan taste great on top or with a bit of garlic bread on the side.
Thank you so much Uncle Bill. Will use again and again.

I found this recipe when I was trying to use up some post-entertaining veggies.  I had no zucchini, so I used extra carrots, onions, and celery.  I used a full can (16 oz.)of pinto beans and I used chicken stock instead of water.  The canned tomatoes had peppers in them, but were not too spicy.  The end result was absolutely delicious.  We also sprinkled fresh Parmesan cheese on top.  What a wonderful basic recipe!  The spices were just right.  Thank you very much, Uncle Bill.

Outstanding! Even better than Olive Garden's...I have replaced the water with broth ( chicken or Veggie)...and added  a med. sized can of tomato sauce as well ( 14 0z I think)...makes for a more flavorful soup...:)
another great recipe from uncle bill!  the soup has excellent flavor thanks for posting.

This is delicious.  I tripled the recipe to feed a crowd and it was a hit all the way around.  I was a little concerned that the zucchini would get too mushy adding it in so early in the cooking process, but not to worry it turned out just fine.
I have several recipes for minestrone and this is my favorite.  I think it would also be good with dark kidney beans instead of white.  Thanks for posting Uncle Bill!

Absolutely delicious! Very easy to make too. The only thing I changed was that I added in broth instead of water. DH who is not a soup person and DD a very picky eater enjoyed it too!! I served it with French Tart's Recipe #268753. Thank you, Uncle Bill, for sharing your wonderful recipe. Definitely will be making this again!
Very very good! I followed the recipe to a 'T'', except I added a little more macaroni and some corn starch to thicken it up. Simple, low cal, low sodium and delicious!
Don't know what I did wrong, perhaps having to substitute green beans for carrots, but it was utterly flavourless for me too.
Delicious and low calorie.  What a perfect fall soup!  Very versatile and tasty.

This recipe is GREAT! I took the suggestion of the other reviewers and added cubed red potatoes as well as vegetable broth instead of the water. I also added some halved frozen beans and chopped cabbage instead of Zucchini. I found the salt and seasoning suggestions to be less, so I added a full teaspoon of Italian seasoning and 1.5 tsp of Salt. And ofcourse I doubled up on the Basil - I heart Basil! : )
Overall, I guess you can modify this recipe as you please, and I'm sure it will always be wonderful! Thanks Bill!
If I could give it six I would.  This soup is easy to make and very tasty.  This is a new staple in my home.  I made a double batch and will make another this week to freeze.  Thanks for posting!

Uncle Bill, 
What a great soup!!! This is comfort food at it's healthiest...( and a great way to use up those zucchini!!!=) A bowl of minestone, a chuck of peasant bread and a glass of wine made last Friday's late supper just right! Thanks for posting!!!

My boyfriend is a vegetarian and I am always looking for recipes that fit his lifestyle and that I can enjoy also.  I made this last week and we both loved it!!!!  It's definitely a "keeper" for both of us.  Thanks so much Uncle Bill for a delicious and healthy soup.

This is a delicious soup. I used crushed tomatoes with basil instead of the whole canned tomatoes, but follow the rest of the recipe as is. The result the best vegetarian minestrone soup that I ever had. I love it. Thanks Uncle bill

Granted, I did not follow this recipe to a "T", I did find it a little watery.  I ended up adding garlic salt and Tabasco, which greatly improved the flavor of the soup.  Next time I will take the advice from others and use a vegetable soup base.  Otherwise, good color and texture, the beginnings of a great soup!
My family & guests loved this minestrone!
Yum!  So easy & so delicious.  I used veggie stock instead of water & added more macaroni because I love pasta.  I'll definitely make this again.

The soup is good as written, but substitute white or red wine for half of the water - and use veggie stock for the other half....it is amazing! :) Even meat lovers will love this soup made with the wine.

This was excellent !!  I did take reviewers advice and used vegetable broth in place of water, and I used a can of Northern beans, and one can of Dark Red Kidney beans also, just because I wanted to LOL, it was great. Thanks for letting me try this recipe !

Let me tell you, this recipe is a winner!!!  The only changes that I made were using a can of diced tomatoes, instead of dicing them myself, and using a whole can of cannellini beans.  Some time back I had some fresh zucchini and celery that I didn't want to waste, so I froze them (the zucchini in slices, the celery diced).  I just dumped them into the recipe and they worked great!  This is most certainly as good as the minestrone at a certain Italian restaurant chain that is my favorite with their unlimited breadsticks and big bowl of salad.  I think the next time I'll add some kidney beans, as they are a favorite of mine.  The bottom line, this is FABULOUS!!

superb!!! I used water instead of stock and found it had plenty of flavour.
I also used chick peas instead of cannellini beans as my children prefer those.
Really filling and wholesome.My children love !!!!

This was good soup and very hearty.  I used vegetable broth instead of water, and accidentaly added kidney beans along with white beans.  The next time I make it, I will not add the kidney beans, but add a bit more seasoning for my personal taste.  Thank you for sharing.  Will make again.

Excellent soup, and very filling!  I made this because I'm dieting and it's low calorie, but I would make this again even if I could eat whatever I wanted.  I used vegetable broth instead of water, and added asparagus, arugula, and shiitake mushrooms because I had them on hand and it sounded good.

This was delicious! I added about 1/2 cup mushrooms and sauteed them with the onion. I also used great northern beans since it's all I have. It tasted fantastic, but I think I will add some more spices next time (needs a bit more salt)

Absolutely delicious! I can't find canned plum tomatoes here, so used plain 'ole tomatoes. We're not too fond of salt, so I omitted it & added 1/4 tsp. Italian Seasoning. Served with warm rye bread. What a lovely meal!

I just made this minestrone today and wanted to add my praise to all the others for this wonderful recipe.  This soup has just the right proportion of broth, vegetables, pasta, and seasonings.  Delicious.  Thanks, Uncle Bill!
This was wonderful!  Made it with  fresh picked tomatoes, zucchini, carrots and potatoes from the garden.  My only change was adding some potatoes, obviously :)
very tasty!! I added a spoon of tomato paste to thicken it..otherwise its amazing!
Excellent recipe! second time I made this I substituted 6oz of water with tomato juice. Tasted so much better.

Delicious! I used vegetable stock and 1/2 cup red wine in place of the water. Added garbanzo beans along with the cannellini  beans. This was by far the best soup I have tasted in a long time, if not ever. Plus, it's so easy that we will be a winter staple in my house.

Fantastically better than the Progresso Minestrone I'm used to.  Big wonderful chunks of tomatoes and zucchini and carrots.  Just the right amount of beans (not too much).  Only recommendation is a slightly more salt.  I guess you wouldn't need to add more salt if you used stock instead of water though.
Very, very good, and the wonder of it is that it is low calorie!
Very good and simple. Omitted the salt since the tomatoes have plenty. Added extra veggies. Excellent on any day.

Excellent and hearty soup! Wonderful for the autumn and winter season when you want a nice hot homemade soup. I added diced potatoes, kidney beans instead of cannellini, and added garbanzo beans. Used chicken stock (4 cups total), but added at least a cup of water more. Instead of plum tomatoes, I used a 16 oz can of fire roasted diced tomatoes with all its juices. Omitted the salt, but my husband thought it could have used some. Will make again, especially when I have lots of veggies leftover!
We really enjoyed this!
Delicious and very filling.  I did add 2 diced red potatoes with the noodles and a little corn for color & txsture  at the end of the cooking.

It is wonderful!!
I faithfully followed the recipe. 
And, it was a big success. 
 I am glad to eat always readily and delicious. 
I am glad to find this recipe. 
Thank you for sharing the recipe.

From kitchen in Japan.

This is yummy and easy to make recipe. I did feel as if it was lacking a bit in flavor for my tastes, so I did the following: I substituted vegetable broth for the water, and I increased the amount of oregano and salt to 1 tsp each. Also, after the macaroni was finished cooking, I added 1 tbsp of red wine vinegar. This definitely added some more sparkle to the dish for me. Also, I use an entire can (14 oz) of cannellini beans. I've made this a number of times and it is a hit each time. Thanks!

This is delicious. I felt that the flavor was a little bland.  Next time I will make with chicken broth (yes I know this is a vegetarian recipe).  I also browned a pound of hamburger and added it to this soup.  
I like that the celery still had a little snap and that I get a lot of good veggies into me.  Thank you Uncle Bill.

YUM! I got my meatacarnivore hubby going back for 2nds on this!

I"m not big on meat, so this was perfect for me.

I have made this soup on numerous occasions, and it is always easy and yummy! I also use broth instead of water, and seem to always end up putting more veggies in than the recipe calls for, but I'm not much for measuring. As with many soups, the longer the ingredients are allowed to blend, the better it tastes! This is my go-to minestrone soup recipe!
I've used this recipe several times and my family loves it!

This is a great soup recipe! It's easy, nutritious and full of flavor. I used vegetable stock and served the soup with grated parmesan cheese. It was wonderful on this rainy night! I will make this recipe on a regular basis. Thanks!

I have made this recipe many times and it is wonderful. The changes I have made are: use Â½ cup of whole wheat pasta, veggie broth instead of water and diced tomatoes instead of plum tomatoes. I also add parmesan cheese on top. I just made it again today and it was perfect! Thanks!

mmmmm so good. I used homemade stock instead of water. I had it for dinner last night and lunch today and now I'm sad it's gone. Great flavor, filling, and the proportions of the ingredients was great.

Always great soups. We chopped up a 7-bone chuck steak, browned the pieces, and then made the soup in the pot (needed something to do with a big chunk of meat). The chuck pieces turned out very tender and the soup is delicious. Thanks.

I thought this soup tasted great while being healthy and low-fat.  I followed the recipe and did not add broth like other reviewers did.  There is plenty of flavor without adding broth.  I did add cauliflower and kale to the soup and I also pureed the tomatoes because I don't like chunks.  Thanks for the recipe.  I'm making another batch this afternoon!

This soup is incredible.  I've made it a few times now and it never fails to impress me!  I use vegetable stock (4 cups) instead of the water and use a grand total of 5 garlic cloves.  I also cut out some calories and fat by not using any olive oil.  Instead, I just coat the onions and garlic with Pam Olive Oil flavor.  I add an 8-oz can of tomato sauce, omit the pasta, and use the entire can of beans.  One of the best soups I've ever tasted, hands down!
Wow, this is a really good soup! I made it with water, but added 1 cup of spiral pasta and 2 cups of chard. This is really healthy and yummy!
Followed the recipe exactly, it was a big hit with the family!  Yum!

I am so full from eating so much soup.  This is the second time I have made this soup. The first time I followed the recipe, but added so vegetable broth for some of the water.  This time my boyfriend and I added ground beef and some tumeric spice. This soup is a really good base and can be so versatile. You go Uncle Bill!

This was so delicious and healthy also..great combination! I made this as stated but used fire roasted tomatoes as that is what was in the pantry. I did grate a tiny bit of parmesan on the top of mine and also "blessed" the soup with a drizzle of olive oil right before eating.

Thank you, Uncle Bill, for sharing this wonderful soup!
Made this last night and had it again tonight. Very good! I did add a little too much pasta and I had to add a little more liquid but all in all it was delish! Will be making this one again!
I modified this slightly, adding squash, spinach, and crushed tomatoes. It turned out amazingly. Very tasty.
AMAZING! Our neighbors made this for us when I was sick and it is delicious! Thanks so much!
I made this for a soup potluck we had at work on a cold, rainy day and it was perfect!!!  Got lots of compliments at how delicious it was.

Excellent soup, Uncle Bill!  I didn't use the zucchini this time (but will next time), used regular canned, diced tomatoes, 1 can of great northern beans and added 3 chicken bouillon cubes.  I did have to cook it quite a bit longer than the time stated because my celery was still crunchy.  But I sure enjoyed this soup on a cool, rainy, dreary day.  Thanks!
This was a very tasty soup.  Everything blended together perfectly.  Thanks for posting.

I cook this every three or four weeks, it's delicious. I use 1/2 a teaspoon of oregano instead of 1/4, a dash of Worcestershire and Tabasco sauces and a teaspoon of Vegeta. My boyfriend loves it for dinner with hot toast and butter. Yum!
I did not like this at all but my husband thought it was good. Did everything as described but just not a soup for us.
I love all the veggies in this soup, but we had to spice it up quite a bit because it was a little bland.
I know this sounds weird, but I added a can of vegetarian refried beans to thicken it up.  Family loved it!
Mmmmm!  Delish!  I used chicken broth instead of water and added the whole can of beans.  I love this recipe.  I will make again and again.  Thanks!

Delicious and very simple to prepare.  Following the recipe to a "T", however adding in 3 teaspoons "Better Than Vegetable Bouillon" Vegetable Base and also 2 links of Tofurky Kielbasa, cut into small pieces.  I would not change a thing!  We really enjoyed this soup and will look forward to having it again.  Thanks so much for sharing all your wonderful recipes with us Uncle Bill!!

I don't understand the excitement and rave reviews about this recipe. It's just a plain vegetable soup with too much zucchini and celery, and rather bland even with the addition of broth instead of water and extra spices.

I make this soup a lot- and it is great!  I do use about half chicken broth and half water- and I love all the zucchini- I throw in any leftover vegetables I have- I also up the amount of oregano, garlic and basil a bit and use a whole can of beans- I think the rave reviews are because it is really so simple but tasty!  When I serve it I grate some fresh parm and we have it with a hearty bread- Fantastic on a cold January day!

Thank you Uncle Bill for this recipe.  So simple and delicious!  I was looking for a vegetarian version for minestrone soup.  I used chicken stock instead of vegetable, because well I'm not a vegetarian and wanted the flavor of chicken stock.  My husband and two small children ate this up with crusty french bread for dipping.
Made half a recipe and it was perfect for us.  Loved it for meatless Mon.

Absolutely delicious!
I'm the world's worst cook but this has given me quite a morale boost. So pleased to find a recipe that works for me. Being in Australia I used one 400g can of Italian tomato pieces & it was perfect - allowed all the flavours to come through. THANKS ??
Just made this for dinner... amazing ?

My 11 year old daughter is a vegetarian, and it can be challenging to find recipes that the rest of the family will eat along with her (besides pasta and pizza). Other vegetarian soups sometimes call for veggie stock, which is vile (seriously, google it, it is gross). This just has the fresh veggies and canned tomatoes, beans and pasta. Delicious, and my husband liked it (he hates veggies). We served with parmesan to sprinkle and crusty bread and butter. A definite keeper.

Just made this tonight. Was rather disappointed. Flavors got lost. I would presume it is because of the water and no broth. Next time will substitute beef broth consommé for water and see how that tastes.

I made this for Christmas Eve dinner, and it was FABULOUS!!!!  My husband loved it, and he's not a big fan of my cooking! ?  That proves this recipe is the real deal.  I did use vegetable broth instead of 3 cups of water, and put about 14 fresh spinach leaves in at the last minute.  Will definitely make this many times in the future.
Turned out very simple and amazing.

Awesome, easy recipe. It's super flavorful. I used macaroni instead because that's what I had. I added a splash of spicy pickle juice because it seemed like a good idea and it turned out nicely. Upped the beans because I love beans. Recommended for cold and rainy days! Thanks Uncle Bill!

I used organic lentils instead of cannellini beans and used fresh tomatoes instead of canned. All the ingredients were fresh and organic and it turned out great! Your recipe was the inspiration for my own version. Thank you for making it easy to follow.
Thank you for this information. It was helpful in my first try at this type of breadmaking. I've never seen this explanation before, Thanks again Chef Kate

I was in the mood for Italian and had a lot of ground beef, so I found this manicotti recipe. It turned out great! I halved the recipe since it was just me and my husband. Next time I'll probably add more mozzarella cheese to the filling since we're cheese lovers - we'll probably adding some mroe spices to the beef next time too. Still came out great, though!
Great dish to create and freeze for later use.  Easy preparation and you can vary the ingredients to suit your tastes.  Cheese lovers may want to double the amount of mozzarella cheese ;)

This is a easy to follow recipe but it didn't really say "wow" for us. I personally didn't like the texture of the cooked ground beef that was stuffed in the manicotti, I usually prefer something much smoother...perhaps next time I'll simply try it with only cheese with a meat sauce on top. Had a recipe call for Italian seasoning, so I needed a recipe.  This site never lets me down.  Perfect flavors!  I didn't have enough basil so I did without.  Wonderful!  My 9 year old ate the ham and cheese spirals that I used this in and said it tasted great.  Thanks!

This smells wonderful! I didn't have any dried rosemary, so I substituted dried sage instead (I added about a tablespoon). I mixed everything in a jar and didn't bother with grinding it. Just what I needed to make Italian tomato salad. DH used the last of my seasoning and I whipped this up in seconds. I did process it as dried Rosemary can be too toothsome.
Thank you for a great recipe. I use this often and I believe it is the reason my spaghetti sauce is so darn good.

I tried this Italian Seasoning on some Steamed Salmon & It's great on Fish dishes also, & Chicken also. Thanks for putting this up, As this will be my go to seasoning from now on, Instead of the store bought stuff, That you don't know how long it's been sitting on the Grocers Shelves.?

I give this five stars because it is robust and flavorful, and onion and garlic free, which is what I wanted because I am allergic to both. It is very difficult to find tasty seasonings for ANYTHING that don't include either of those ingredients. THIS one is definitely a keeper and a lifesaver!

We were taught by my Italian relatives a cuisine known to five-star star chefs as "la pauvre cuisine" which roughly means "the poor cuisine" which is also synonymous with southern Italian cooking. Neapolitan. So, in this wonderful world of the originators of pizza pie and red tomato pasta sauce, they rarely if ever used rosemary and thyme, those herbs are respectable and have their place but in my sauce is not one of them. This recipe I view as more of a northern Italian spice blend, so I omit thyme and rosemary. I also omit the garlic powder and onion powder, preferring to add those separately to taste, really a purist would say to "sweat" or lightly simmer the minced fresh garlic first in olive oil before adding tomatoes, but that takes time and money I'm not willing to part with. All that having been said, I was looking for a recipe like this to make cooking easier than my mothers style, which was add a little and taste, add a little and taste, standing over each pot for at least an hour. No time for that in this world, so this prevents all that and comes out great! I make a huge batch and use it often. It's very practical AND most importantly, DELICIOUS. This is a keeper, we will never buy store-bought again. Thanks for sharing this recipe!

This went over so-so.  Not planning on making again but it was a nice change of pace.
Gooey, cheesy goodness!

Oh man!  This is sooo good!  I made this especially for DH whose favorite pizza topping is ground beef... and my most hated but this has definitely changed my mind.  It was awesome and I will definitely be making this often.  Thanks for posting!
This was very good.. A great way to have a different kind of pizza.
Excellent...very cheesy and super filling.  We had two meals on one pizza.

This was very good. I love pizza and was kinda scared of the velveeta but it was awesome. The only thing I did diff was ues all hamb. 5 starrs!!

Surprisingly delicious!  We're not fans of velveeta but I had some that needed to be used up.  Now I'll have to keep it on hand. I used all hamburger for the meat and topped with some pepperoni. Very quick & easy!
We all really liked this pizza. It is very filling. I used all ground beef and left out the green pepper. Will definitley make again!
This was amazing. I'd say the best pizza I've ever made at home.

I made these meatballs for the Timpano recipe. The meatballs were excellent, too bad my Timpano did not turn out as good.

And, I put the tofu under a plate with weights (the jars of spaghetti sauce) to pull out more moisture and drain it before mixing the filling.  I made the filling early in the morning on Christmas Eve and let the flavors mix for about 5-6 hours while we ran errands.  Came home, made the shells, and stuffed them.  It was really easy and fast.  I use Tinkyada gluten-free pasta shells for the 1st time which said to decrease the (boiling) cooking time by 2 minutes if they were going to be used in baking.  Next time, I would not do that because they were still not cooked after 30 minutes.  I ended up having to add an extra 1/2 cup water to the pan and baking for another 15-20 minutes just to make them al dente.  I am new to this, so I learned from the experience.  Next time I will boil the pasta shells at least to al dente.  My DH loved the shells, too, which is great because this is a very easy way to add tofu to our diet and not even notice it.  It could also be fun to experiment with the filling.  Maybe try subbing 1 extra firm silken tofu (Mori Nu lite) for the firm version.  And, I wonder...adding roasted eggplant or broccoli might be really yummy, too.
