When I took the dough out of the machine when it was finished, what I had was a very liquid slurry; to be fair, you do instruct to add more flour if necessary, but I estimate I added about 3/4 to 1 cup more to make it workable. At this point I despaired that it would ever rise, but after about 1 1/2 hours, it did (and did even more during the baking). So the only problem, I think, was the amount of flour given in the ingredients list (I've since done some looking at other focaccia recipes and discovered that for the amount of water given in this recipe, 1 cup, they generally call for 3 to 3 1/2 cups flour, and only a couple TBS of oil). I'm certainly not going to suggest that anyone add more flour in at the beginning because I haven't tried that yet, and I DO NOT want to put anyone off trying this because it is VERY TASTY and makes lovely bread; I'm just saying be prepared to add in quite a bit more flour, and don't panic :) Thanks for posting, Judy!
I had this at a friends house last night for dinner - Lovely blend of herbs, very attractive and tasty

This is a real neat, simple and colourful side dish.  I let it marinate most of the day.  It was very tasty and is just a nice dish to add to any meal.  A little tomato always looks good on a plate too.  Thanks for posting this Alan.

As already posted. They are tomatoes with herbs and as a plate filler they look good. Not the "wow" part of a dish but if you need something to fill a plate for your family during the week its a good option.

I used balsamic vinegar with this and it was fabulous. Even better the next day after marinading. I forgot they were on the plate and stuck them in the microwave with the rest of my dinner plate. They were even very good cooked. I will make these often this summer. Thanks Alan for a healthy and wonderful addition to my repertoire.

This sauce is great!! It does take quite a while to cook, but WELL WORTH the effort. I also use this for pizza sauce and people go "ga-ga" over it. I didnt use the msg, but still tasted great. Thanks!!!!
This recipe is very spicy and sweet. It is a must keep at our house. The chops were very tender and moist. I served it with baked potatoes.

Great meal.  I used Splenda instead of real sugar and thought I had the artichoke hearts, but I didn't - otherwise made this just as written.  Real tasty sauce I served over pasta.  Glad I have some leftover for lunch today!

Forgive me for not reviewing this sooner! This is woderfully good. Easy to prepare to boot! I did sub a jar of drained artichokes for water packed as that was all I had on had but it was scrumptious none the less. A nice hearty winter supper. I also added some mushrooms which I needed to use up. The kids thought it a little spicy but still gave it a thumbs up!
Outstanding.  We loved it and it was so easy to throw together.  Thanks for sharing!

This was an easy to put together and good weekday meal. I didn't brown the chops and just put everything in the crockpot on low for 6 hours. The pork was tender and had good flavor, reminiscient of a caccitore type dish. We served this over brown rice and though it wasn't something we were bowled over by, it was still pretty good and healthy. This was a great remedy when I was not sure what to do with my pork chops and we enjoyed.  Bonus was that the flavor was even better the next day.
nice way to make pork chops.  I served it over spaghetti and thought it was pretty good.  Thanks!
This was my first time cooking all by myself and it was easy. The recipe was easy to follow and it turned out great.
I served this over pasta.  The chops were moist and there was plenty of sauce, but it just didn't suit our tastebuds.  Thanks anyway!

My family loved this.  So did I.  I didn't have any tomato sauce and used a can of diced tomatoes instead.  Also used a red instead of green pepper.  Served it over noodles.  My 3-year-old grandson, a very picky eater, asked for seconds and ate 2 servings the next day for lunch!

Loved This!
  Easy to prepare, great flavor-I did add about 1/2 cup shredded Parmesan to the top of the chops the last 5 minutes, and didnt have artichoke hearts on hand, but other than that I stuck to your recipe.  We will have this again, and I would easily prepare this for guests!
Thanks for posting,
Di

We really enjoyed this recipe. I appreciated the amount of pork being given by weight as I had some smallish pork steaks to use up. I thought I had tomato sauce on hand but did not so I substituted jarred pasta sauce, and used yellow bell pepper. The crushed red pepper gave it a nice little kick and I loved the artichokes in this. Thanks for a keeper, Sue.

This was very tasty! I made it when I had company that night and everyone loved it! A lot of people went for seconds and were disappointed when it was all gone! The only things I did different was I used a regular sized can of olives, chopped instead of the bell pepper. Also, I left out the crushed red pepper flakes. I served it with corn and garlic bread. Yummy!

Won some pork chops in a raffle. Didn't want to grill them, come out tuff when I do that. So loved the taste of this recipe. The next time I make it, I think I will make extra sauce and turn it into soup. Thanks for a lovely meal. Just made this for the second time and hubby says this is the only way he wants pork chops from now on.
Nice, easy, hearty dish...great for a cold night.

This was so good!  I served with egg noodles.  

Made exactly as directed.

Darn fine for alittle something into the crockpot... really enjoyed the flavours. Nice change to do artichoke with pork (vs. chicken).  I did recipe as written except I cooked mine in the pressure cooker instead.  I agree with other reviewers that it was abit too much sauce so I'll probably cut back abit next time.

this was insanely tasty!!  the flavors are outstanding.  i'm making this tonight for the second time this week!  i pretty much followed recipe exactly, except for the sauce.  i use a store bought sauce that i jazz up with chicken boullion, garlic powder, cayenne and the balsamic vinegar.  i really love the flavor from the balsamic...what a great idea!  i finished the whole dish off with capers...which i think was a nice addition and shredded parm.  this recipe is a real winner.  thanks so much for an elegant crockpot keeper!  served over pasta with garlic bread.  mmm-mmm! thanks again, sue!
I thought they were good and my kids ate them too but mny husband was not a fan. I would make them again if he was out of town.

Made this wonderful recipe in my favorite kitchen appliance a pressure cooker (8 qt. Cooks Essentials from QVC). I browned the pork chops removed them, sauteed the onions and added all of the other ingredients, then put the chops back in. It took only 20 minutes to cook and the meat fell off the bone no knives needed.  I left out the peppers and artichoke hearts since my husband doesn't eat them, doubled the tomato sauce and it was still full of flavor.  I made plenty of rice to soak up the sauce.  I recommend using pork chops on the bone. Bon Appetit!
This was an easy recipe and came together just as written.  Lots of leftover sauce.

This is an EXCELLENT recipe.My Wife and Son loved it! The essential secret for a good dish like this,is the long slow cooking in the Crockpot.The basil and bay leaves work well in the flavour as it slowly cooks- and the magic aroma!
If you are ever selling your house,put this dish on while buyers are looking through.
Cheers from another crockpot lover in West Oz.

Sarah!
Great recipe! I never use celery or carrots in bolognese usually, but I can say I really liked it with these added.
It was great to come home on a cold winter's night from work and have the meal just about ready for you, and tuckerbox is so right the fantastic aroma that permeated through the house It was the first thing that hit me when I first walked in .... WOW.... It just smelt so good!!!
Great recipe Sarah! Will be using the crockpot a little more often now I have this recipe!!!

This is yummy, easy to do, but more of a savoury mince rather than a sauce for spaghetti. I personally would add another 2-3 tins of tomatoes, and some tomato paste, maybe a bit more water to get a saucier consistency. The capsicum is lovely, and I added lots of extra basil because we've got a LOT growing in the garden. Could also grate zucchini or other veges and they would hide well in the sauce.

My household loves this and we serve it with radiatore. It's meant to be thick, and I find 2 cans of diced tomato has plenty of moisture. I don't bother to chop my veggies very small, so I usually cook it for the full 8 hours.
Really loved this! I cut the recipe down to serve 2 people and it turned out wonderfully! It would be excellent with some berries on top. Very different but very tasty.

Super easy & fast to prepare.  Short ingredient list; you can't go wrong.  If you're having a dinner party, this is the kind of simple dessert that will wow your guests and can be made well ahead of time.  Served this with a sweetened raspberry puree.

DH adored this dessert,  and has asked for it to be put into my handwritten cookbook. I liked it a little less, but that was definiately due to my personal taste in desserts rather than there being anything at all wrong with this recipe :) One of our houseguests chose this recipe for us and made it too... I didn't have any whipped cream to accompany it with so presented the dish with some chocolate shavings  scattered over the top. We used 2.5 teaspoons of gelatine and the consistancy was excellent. Buttermilk is called "Karnemelk" here in The Netherlands and it gives this recipe a little something extra that using ordinary milk just wouldn't give. We were impressed by the ease of making, simplicity of the recipe, but most of all the great taste. Please see my rating system, a very well deserved 4 stars. Thanks !!!

Props to the man who decided to put buttermilk in panna cotta.  I  didn't notice the recommendation for what to put on top of it, I put blueberries in juice with lemon juice and port on top and the whole thing was perfect.  This recipe is the perfect approach to panna cotta, 5 stars.

This was great! So simple and enjoyable, and the buttermilk really makes the dish. Now I know what to do when I have leftover buttermilk. Oh, and I topped it with raspberry puree.
Thanks!
Wow!  I had never heard of panna cotta before, so this is the first one I've tried. I served mine with strawberry coulis (also new to me) and I very much enjoyed this.  Thank-you!
Excellent and far better and easier than another buttermilk panna cotta recipe I tried recently. Nice texture and flavor. Thanks!
A lovely, EASY appy.
Delicious brushetta! I followed your directions, except for adding a little diced Mozzarella cheese and some black pepper.  We will definitely be making this again!

Made the tomato mixture ahead and let the flavors marry.  I loved the addition of Balsamic vinegar and lemon to this.  I usually just make mine with olive oil, garlic and basil.  Had to leave out the oregano; DH does not like it. Thanks for posting, CL - will definitely make this again.

Had some neighbors over for cocktails and I served this appetizer.  Everyone loved them.  I made the tomato mixture early in the day.  Once my guests arrived, all I had to do was top the toasted bread with it.  Easy and very tasty and I wouldn't change a thing.  Another winner, CountryLady.

Plus five more stars. I used 2 cups grain alcohol,4 cups whole milk,I really don`t like scotch whiskey but thats what I had and it worked great. I added a sliced vanilla bean to the milk and sugar at step #2. I used a total of 3 cups of sugar. Everone that had this just loved it. My Sis said it tasted like lemon pudding! I did serve this in cordial glasses to make it go farther as the picture shows. Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe!

I made this back in September and have only just realized that I didn't review it.  This drink is astounding!  I followed the recipe exactly, the only change being that I used soy milk instead of regular moo juice because I didn't want this to be dairy. I zested the lemons with my Microplane.  Make sure you clean your lemons with soap and water and then make sure they are dry, there's nothing worse than wet, dirty lemon zest.  This made enough to almost fill a 1 1/2 liter bottle, which I now keep in the freezer.  Watch out for this drink, it's very potent, but so sweet and delicious you don't realize quite how potent, until you've had several shot glasses full and find yourself trying to find the Off switch to stop the room turning.

For recipes like this, they should let you put more stars!  This liqueur is the perfect balance of lemon tanginess, sweet, and creaminess.  Wonderful!  The only problem is that it's easy to drink too much!  We have two bottles waiting in the freezer, calling our name just a little too loudly!  Easy to make, inexpensive, delicious.  Would make a great christmas gift, too!

Everyone who's tasted this say "wow, this is great, how did you do it"
Very easy to make.
I used 100 proof vodka, and a shot of cognac. Organic lemons. Next time I'll try with lime.
Mine got a skin on the top after freezing. It's better to remove the skin rather than try to stir it into the liqueur, as it won't blend so well.

Yummy!! My first attempt at liqueur making - I'll definitely make this again. I'll also try lime and orange, maybe other fruits.

Next time I'd cut back the whisky a little, because I felt the balance wasn't quite perfect. Maybe it's because I used single malt Scotch.

It went down pretty well at my last dinner party, even with the guy who doesn't like spirits or lemon!

So smooth and creamy!! I made mine with limes from my backyard and some cognac and it came out great. It yields a plenty compared to other homemade liqueurs and it's pretty economical as well. I'll keep on experimenting with this awesome recipe. Thanks a lot for posting!!

The (Canadian) Liquor store would not sell me grain alcohol because they said I needed a perscription for it!  So I bought some alcool--a tasteless hard liquor.  It turned out amazing and was soooo delicous.  I used splenda for the sugar and whole milk instead of cream.  I also make a lime version and called key lime pie cocktail -- it was such a hit with everyone.

I forgot to review this.  This is my fourth year preparing it for friends.  I sure have a lot of  new friends . This is the best recipe on the web.  I cant believe you have such a delicacy with so little time.  I'm from the US, I'm older and I  havent done conversions since College chemistry but I used for each batch  2 cups  vodka  for alcohol,  and 3 cups of sugar for others having problem with conversions. Magnificant

I'm not going to rate this because I didn't totally follow the recipe. I'm sure it would have been much better with the grain alcohol and whiskey or cognac, but I didn't have any, so I followed another reviewer's advice and substituted 2 c. vodka for the alchohol. I really, really wanted to like it, but the vodka was just way too strong for my taste. I hope to make it again the right way. The directions were easy to follow, and it still sounds delish!

I made this for a large group of Italian relatives and it was a huge success.  I doubled (and then some) the recipe, using 2 pounds of fresh lasagna and a large pan (maybe 24 x 12?).  It weighed a ton!  Half served 9 people as a first course and I froze the rest in small portions. My philosophy: when you're going to all the work of preparing a big "pasticcio", as they say here, why not make more and enjoy it with ease in the future?  Having no shiitakes, I used a generous pound of fresh, sliced button mushrooms and 1/2 ounce dried, soaked and drained porcini.  I sauteed both mushrooms in olive oil just until they were going to release their juices.  Other change:  didn't like the idea of serving the tomato sauce on the side - they just don't do that here in Northern Italy.  So I did each layer with a thin radicchio/mushroom spread, a big dollop of the tomato/white sauce spread over it, mozzarella strewn about and  a big handful of parmesan cheese.  Top layer, as the recipe directs, I ended with a couple of cups of white sauce painted on, lots of chopped mozzarella and parmesan again.  As it was so large, I cooked it 1 1/2 hours, removed the foil to brown for 20 minutes, and let it rest 15 minutes.  My only complaint?  The prep time is really UNDER-exaggerated.  To do it properly, each element must be ready and then assembling it is a snap (and creatively fun).  I cook alot and this took me over 2 hours to prep.  But don't let that deter you.  It you've got a big group, and they're discerning (it is an "adult" recipe), this is authentic Italian cooking at it's best.  Complimenti!
I made this for Easter.  The loaf was really dense and dry.  The taste was o.k. - not very strongly flavored.

I used this recipe on the dough cycle of my bread machine  and left out the anise seed. I also used bread machine yeast rather than active dry yeast. Dough was divided  into 3 ropes; braided it; placed it on parchment lined cookie sheet; covered it with a teatowel and let it rise in slightly warmed oven for approximately 3/4 hour until double in sie.   Baked it  in a 375 Deg F. oven for 35 minutes.  After cooling, covered with icing made of milk, icing sugar and lemon juice.
Makes an extremely large loaf.  Excellent results.

I loved this bread (a little too much, to be honest)...such a great combination of flavors. The recipe was too large for my bread machine, and puffed over the top a bit...so next time I'll probably do as another reviewer did and bake it in the oven after letting the bread machine knead it for me. The finished product was very fluffy, with a large crumb, and was very moist (I'm sure because of all of the butter in it). Thanks for sharing this...it was so good!

This was absolutely the best Stuffed Pepper recipe I have had. I used black chopped olives as that is what I had in the fridge.  The fennel together with the eggplant give an awesome flavour, if you like italian flavours you will just love this.
I will definately be doing this again and again.

I just loved the different flavors in this dish. I halved the recipe. The red peppers were so soft, I just layed them in the pan, then poured the stuffing over. I used green olives, because that is what I had on hand.Each bite was a taste treat! Thanks Recipe Fairy!

I made this and thought they were alright.  I had to add pasta sauce to them because I found them to be a little too dry.  The combination of flavors was great and with some more added cheese and sauce, they turned out pretty good.

This soup is intended to have a 'watery' broth, with medium garlic/onion flavor.  The broth is best made by purchasing addition clam broth from the fish monger when you purchase the clams.  "Dom's" (no long open) in Boston, MA served the difinitive soup.  Do not use tomatoes but rather use tomato paste.  The onions should be in large circular ring (Vidalia) and should be served with crunchy bread and a good sharp Chablis or Cabernet Sauvignon (White)

This was the easiest sauce to make and it tasted great! The best part is, I always have these ingredients on hand.  I did think the sauce was a little bit watery, but I have found that draining the tomatoes and using a couple tablespoons of tomato paste makes it perfect. Recipe #236785 works great for a crust. Will keep making this over and over again! Thanks!

This was an extremely flavourful pasta dish and much appreciated.  I am lucky enough to find lardons here, so I could follow the recipe exactly.  The lardons provided a smoky backdrop to the intense tomato sauce and the sun-dried tomatoes added a salty/sweet note that I thought was just right but DH thought was a bit too much of a good thing, so next time I'll add a couple (or three) less - maybe my sun-dried tomatoes were just extra-large, plump ones (they were).  The butter and cheese added at the end really 'rounded' out the flavour.

I did not have lardons but had smoked sun dried tomatoes, I also used penne pasta.  This was a pretty tasty dish, but the smoky ingredients overpowered the cheese.  We added more to the top with fresh ground black pepper.

This was a disappointment. I paid $5 for the tiny baby zucchini and another $5 for the fresh figs. Add the pork to that and this was quite an expensive meal, so I hoped for something equally delicious. It was not. Neither me nor my husband liked it. I think I would omit the cardamom - it gave it a very antiseptic taste. I would not make it again.

I gave this unusual recipe a try with ingredients I had on hand (substituting pork cutlets instead of tenderloin, one large zucchini instead of the small ones and dried figs in place of the fresh ones, which I rehydrated by adding to the onions simmering in water).  Unlike Melanie D, I didn't mind the cardamon and would suggest using the green pods. For a quick dinner, it was not bad served on basmati rice, but as written, this recipe is not a show stopper. 
The sauce would probably benefit from a bit of cornstarch added to the liquid at the end to thicken the sauce, and it would be pretty served with fresh tomato.

This is excellent! It's very light but has a wonderful flavor. I left out the shrimp to make it vegetarian and used soy cream cheese and soy parmesan, but other than that I followed the recipe exactly. The instructions were very easy to follow and in no time flat we had a wonderful dinner that my family raved about. I'll be making this again soon!

I just started cooking about a month and a bit ago, and this was a dish that was SIMPLE SIMPLE SIMPLE and tasted incredibly good. My fiance (who comes from a long line of french chefs) ate three helpings and would have eaten more...thank you!
Delicious, light, lemony sauce.  A perfect weeknight dinner, goes together quickly.  I used frozen mixed veges in place of carrot and peas.

What a treat! This colorful tasty dish was a delight to serve for supper last night! The combination of the carrots & peas along with the pasta and pink cooked shrimp was very eye catching! I had to substitute rotini pasta for the farfalle, but it worked perfectly. I added just one more clove of garlic (personal choice)and I'm afraid a few more than 1/2 cup of peas fell into the mix, but the rest, I followed your directions to the letter. Very quick to prepare.  I will make this again, Paula!  Thanks for submitting it to Zaar to share with us!

So fast and easy and totally delicious! I used flash frozen shrimp and just thawed them and threw them in the pan. Excellent recipe for a night when you are running behind and want something healthy and quick! Thanks!
I rarely follow a recipe step-by-step, but did so last night with this one - GREAT recipe, no alterations needed!

Very good, quick and easy.  I left out the cream cheese since I didn't have any.  I also added some lemon juice along with the zest.  It has been added to my dinner rotation.  Thanks so much for sharing.

What a lovely meal Paula thanks for sharing your recipe.
My husband can’t have any fat, oil or dairy in his diet so the following changes were made.   I left out the olive oil, cream cheese and the parmesan, although I did add parmesan to my own serve. I used vegetable stock and used a little extra stock to replace the oil when I sautéed the garlic etc. It has now been added to our regulars.  Thanks Glen.

This was delicious and healthy too! I was using bought chicken broth so I reduced it by about half. I added some cornstarch to thicken up the sauce. For the veggies I used red pepper and zucchini. The red peppers particularly went well in this dish, I thought. I thought the garlic might be a little overpowering, but it wasn't and the lemon flavour was just great! A plust was how quick and easy it was to make! I will definitely make this again
Unfortunately, I did not care for this recipe.  There was barley a lemon taste to the dish and the sauce didn't seem to thicken up at all...I don't think I will make this again.

We loved this, and I was sorry that I was out of carrots, because it would have been even better, I'm sure.  The only pasta I had on hand was ditalini, and it worked very well with the sauce.  I had to double the recipe for 3 of us (2 are active guys), and next time I will double the sauce part again to make it just a little creamier.  Great World Tour recipe Paula!
I love the taste of this.  There was just enough lemon zest for my liking.  The only thing that had changed was that my parm cheese had basil in it.
We really liked this simple dish, doubling it for the three of us was easy. Thanks for sharing!
Quick to put together, easy, and delicious, what could be better?  I used some homemade chicken broth and about half a can of baby peas, with finely chopped baby carrots.  Will definitely make again!
Easy and delicious!  I used onions and green peppers for the veggies (personal preference).  I also used whole wheat pasta, and it worked really well with this sauce.  Thanks for sharing!

MMMMMMMmmm was this ever good!  We enjoyed it very much.  We had with some baked pita wedges and my DH just about inhaled his plate!  He gives it 5 stars and I do too.  It's a winner all the way to the table!  Thanks Paula!

Made this tonight, a Survivor night so had to be quick, relatively easy and very good.  Indeed it was.  Excellent recipe that I'll use in my regular rotation.  Didn't change anything except I didn't really measure anything. Close enough was good enough. Thanks for sharing.

Very good & easy. I doubled the recipe & my family loved it. I did add some old bay seasoning to give it some more flavor & I doubled the recommended cream cheese. It was good :) Thank you for posting :)
Every bite was awesome, and we liked it very much!
Absolutely a hit with the kids!  I doubled the cream cheese and used asparagus instead of peas.  It was quick and easy enough for my daughter to make mostly on her own.

My 11-yr old and 15-yr old sons both loved this, as did my DH and I. I also loved that it is fairly simple and fast to make if you prep the shrimp in advance. I confess I used less garlic as I was spooked by the amount (even though I love garlic I was worried about the boys) but learned that you must use the minimum amount of garlic listed for the flavor to be at its best, otherwise it will be bland. And I just love the lemon in this. Next time I will try it with either asparagus or spinach, just for a change. This is a keeper! Thanks for posting!

I must say this was easy to prepare (especially since I prepped everything earlier in the afternoon.)
We enjoyed the idea of the recipe, but guess our tastes are just not "Italian" enough to enjoy such a strong parmesan flavor. 
I may make this again, and reduce the amount to our tastes. 
Thanks though for a recipe can be adapted to many preferences. 
Donna

Excellent !  I just made this for myself for dinner ( hubby is out of town )  . All I can say is "Wow" . so easy and tasted like it came from an italian restaurant .  I added capers and left of the veggies (didnt have them around ) I am going to try it with chicken next time. I think if would be great.  thanks so much for sharing
Needed something quick for dinner and this popped up. Very much enjoyed. :)
Both my husband and I thought this was DELICIOUS!!  Perfect for two.  I did not use the peas and served it on spaghetti squash instead of pasta.  So easy but so good!!

Working with only the ingredients I have available in my house, I started searching on Food.com for a recipe that would accommodate the after-work-Monday-night dinner. I knew I was going to prep with Shrimp so with my options narrowed to an extent I found your recipe. I followed the ingredients as close as possible. I did not have farfalle pasta, so I substituted in Yakisoba noodles that I had laying around. Instead of only adding in the lemon zest, I used the juice of the lemon too, allowing it too cook with the shrimp, carrots and peas. I did not have Parmesan cheese so sadly, it was omitted, however, I doubled the amount of cream cheese and used a Chive flavor to kick it up a notch. In the end I broke it into about 4 servings, laying each serving over a bed of fresh spinach (This so my family gets the other vitamins and nutrients squeezed in to the dish). Lastly, I did not have fresh chives so therefore I substituted for dried herb chives. It was perfect and delicious. I will make it again. Thanks so much for sharing PaulaG.
Best Regards
Fabulous!
This was quick and easy but the sauce didn't thicken.  Based on other reviews it was probably the cooks error:)
It was good- really good.
Great flavor!  This is so easy to make and everyone loved it.  The sauce is light and flavorful.  Served this with a green salad and had a great family dinner.

I made this for Valentine's Day for DH and me and he loved it.  I admit, I used more cream cheese than called for and I think I might add lemon juice along with peel in the future but this was very good and very fast and it made my Valentine feel loved.  Thanks, PaulaG.
Yummy!  Made perfect with a squeeze of fresh lemon and a few pine nuts.
This was awesome! I added a little extra park and squeezed in one fresh lemon! I also used I can't believe its not butter instead of the oil and it was awesome! Enjoy!

This is a beautiful recipe. (Apart from halving the amount of Parmesan, I followed the recipe to a T.) My whole family asked for more and that's always a wonderful thing to hear, right! However, when I make it again I would add twice as much broth & cream cheese as the sauce didn't go very far and we like a lot of sauce.
Good flavour, easy to make.
makes very little sauce as written... you need to double or triple the sauce. I also had a problem with the cream cheese melting and mixing. Overall the taste is good.

Seriously delish! Double the stock & cream cheese. I am a big fan of lemony pasta things. Was tempted to use asparagus, which would have been fantastic! I followed the recipe and now I'm ready to play!

Light, flavorful, delicious. I expected it to be more creamy but found it to be so full of flavor that I didn't really miss it. Be careful not to burn the garlic at the beginning (I missed the cue of using medium high heat and scorched mine -- yuck. Threw it out and started over. Love the peas and carrots in it - nice balance. Garnished mine with a handful of parsley (I love parsley). Good find, thanks.
Beautiful light but filling meal for a summer day. Loads of flavor and quick and easy to make. Works very well with gluten free noodles.

This was very good, the only thing I skipped was the wine and added apple juice instead since I dont care for wine in my food.  I think any seafood would work well in this dish.  It is one of those ellegent but easy meals.

Interesting casserole, but felt the seafood lost some of its flavor cooked in the casserole (rather than stir fryed as we usually prepare shrimp and scallops) and felt the sacue could use a bit more seasoning, but for a WW meal it is very filling. Thanks for sharing!

I omitted the lemon zest and thought this dish was very tasty. I will probably omit the oregano next time. I like oregano, but I think an herb with a milder flavor (maybe basil) would work a bit better.  I love the slight sweetness that the carrots bring to this dish.  Other than needing to tweak it a little for my own tastes, I think this is a very good recipe.  I'm glad you shared it ~ Thank you.

Made this last night and was enjoyed by all. A few adjutments, not many i promised,lol. I opened crushed tom (with garlic & basil) i didn't read the can and assumed they were diced. And i used white wine. I had ziti on hand so i used the whole box. I did it in stages. I made the sauce and cooked the pasta early in the day. Then finished up at dinner time. It did make alot my pan was over flowing so it did take extra time in the oven It was in almost 40 mins. The shrimp and scallops came out perfect. We really enjoyed this and are having the left overs tom. 
Thanks for the post!

Wonderful zabaglione! I order it for dessert at my favorite Italian restaurant but this is so much better!! I loved the rum soaked strawberries and amaretti cookies along with the azbaglione. Another great recipe, thank you Ev!

OUTSTANDING! This sauce was so yummy - a huge hit here! I doubled the recipe to make it with italian sausage sandwiches, and the next day I served it over pasta. Yumm!! One of my favorite things to cook and eat are pasta sauces, i love them. And it gives me a chance to go crazy with the spices, lol. Great Sauce!  I usually make up a BIG batch of sauce (gravy) and freeze it.  We enjoyed having a fresh sauce on the Chicken Parmesan. (I posted the picture). Thanks for sharing.
I freeze this and use it for lasagna, pasta, anything that calls for it.  I usually add 1/4-1/2 cup of zinfandel or other red and it comes out perfect every time.  Good one.
You did not exaggerate when you said "this is the best pasta sauce you will ever have".  Totally awesome!!  I'm going to use it to make lasagna for our next trailer trip.  Thanks for posting.

Very good, very easy!  I paired this with Wildflour's meatballs #135104 (cooking them right in the sauce). This was my first home-made sauce, it was incredible. I added sliced mushrooms when the onions were almost done. I also used fresh Italian parsley and topped with parmesean cheese. Amazing.
No need to ever try another sauce. Really, Really good.

Thanks for a great, delicious pasta sauce!  I omitted the salt, used low-sodium chicken broth, and used fresh tomatoes instead of canned whole tomatoes.  I also added some dried oregano.  It's fantastic!
My husband and I adore this! Sooo good. We cook the meatballs first to make sure they're cooked all the way through, add them to the sauce and they turn out so soft they melt in your mouth.
Awesome sauce.  But I skipped the sugar because I wanted it less sweet.
This sauce is so good . I used a can of crushed tomatoes instead of whole.

i adore this sauce! i've been making it for months. i've made it with tomato sauce, crushed tomatoes, or whole tomatoes and it works fine no matter which i use.  The perfect amount of sweet and spicy! It's the only sauce i make now. Thanks!

Wow! 
I just started cooking more from scratch, concerned of all the hidden MSG in foods. I tried this tonight and will NEVER go back to store bought sauce again!

Made the following subs:
*Instead of black pepper, used white
*Instead of the liquid from the canned toms, I used 1/4 cup of really good red wine.
*Used no sugar or salt

My children family loved it and so did I. Thick, tasty, with just the right kick. Just lovely! You will never eat someone else's pasta sauce again!

I feel like a chef. Thanks for the receipe.

It really is the best sauce I've made and I've made a few.  What I love about this sauce is how fresh it tastes as soon as you make it.  Not like a lot of recipes that say they taste better as leftovers.  Also, I've had excellent results simmering for as little as 40 minutes which makes it part of making dinner instead of something you have to plan ahead.  Some pasta sauce recipes say simmer for 6 to 8 hrs. HA! never again! I omit the red pepper flakes as my wife does not like them.  Otherwise followed recipe to the letter.  Thank you for posting my new favorite sauce.  My whole family loves it!!
This pasta sauce is wonderful! Tastes great...I love the consistency. Crushing the tomatoes by hand really makes a difference. Be sure to buy a good quality brand of tomatoes. This is a keeper!
very good pasta sauce, nice base to build up on.  Will definitely do this again. thanks
Fabulous!  This is going into my Best of the Best Cookbook.

Oi Oi! Thought i'd pop in to say that the sauce was pretty darn good, didnt change a thing and so got myself a decent sauce :)
 
Thanks, 1 step closer to no more take outs!

The sauce isn't even finished cooking down in the pan yet and it is already unbelievably good! I ended up cooking the onions and garlic down until they were quite brown and almost crispy. Wow!  Sooo yummy!  I ended up adding a little bit of red wine.  I also cut a tiny bit back on the sugar and added ketchup instead for sweetness (I know it sounds weird, but we do this in Scandinavia).  This sauce was so delicious.  It was also very easy to prepare.  No need for can sauce anymore.

Fantastic, easy marinara recipe.  Really.  I did add 1/2 teaspoon of thyme and about 1/8 teaspoon fennel seeds and cut the oil in half to lighten the recipe.  So good!  Using canned crushed tomatoes instead of whole allows you to skip that step.  I will add this to my classics.
This was a very good, perfectly seasoned sauce.  I added about 1/4 cup red wine.

Delicious!! I didn't think I could make a good homemade pasta sauce, but was I ever wrong! I loved that I got to use canned tomatoes for this as well - it gave a good texture. This was an easy pasta sauce and fun to play around with. I just threw in a bunch of different spices such as italian seasoning, crushed pepper, etc. Anyways this is a very flexible pasta sauce and worked great for me! Thanks!
This turned out  great! one of the best sauces I've ever had!
This is the best pasta sauce I've ever had! We mostly use it with the Chicken Parmigiana (recipe # 25094). Even just with spaghetti its perfect! Thanks for posting :)

Delicious sauce recipe! I will definitely prepare this again. It is great because it is chunky enough but not too chunky that you don't get any actual sauce. It does have a bit of a kick to it so I may decrease the amount of red pepper for guests, but we liked it. Thank you!
Very nice rich and tomato-ey sauce! I added sliced mushrooms and meatballs. Deeeeelish spaghetti sauce!

SOOO GOOD!  This was my first attempt at making sauce from scratch and it was easy and amazing!  Will definitely use instead of jarred sauce from now on.

Excellent - we really enjoyed!

v. good. made with three whole italian heirlooms from our garden, as well as 1/2 a zucchini, and two sweet red italian peppers, finely chopped. added a splash of red wine. pureed in the blender. very tasty. oh, i ended up adding just a bit more salt and sugar to bring out the flavors.
Robust!  This actually tasted more like a Cajun style meal than Italian.  Not bad, just surprisingly bold.  Thanks!
Great rich flavor, but as others said, I think I'd cut the red pepper flakes back a bit.

I tried a few different pasta sauce recipes on here after my cookbooks went missing from our move 5 months ago. This one is my favorite! I add italian sausage or grd beef. I sauteed the red pepper, garlic and onions in a pan and then added it to the slow cooker later.  I think the key to this recipe is to let the sauce simmer for as long as possible.  It really lets the flavors combine.  Also - crush the dry spices in your hand before you add them to the sauce.  It helps bring out the natural oils in the spice.

This sauce was good.  The only thing I did different was to add fresh oregano, parsley, thyme and basil.  This will be good for my grandkids, after I blend the chucks out of it.  They are picky that way. Thanks for sharing.

I would recommend adding 1/4 tsp of crushed red pepper at a time until you find your desired hotness.

Great sauce.  The chicken stock is the magic here.  I would cut the pepper flakes back a bit.  I used Penzy's red pepper flakes and next time I might use a 1/4 rounded tsp.  I like food with a kick, but this was just a wee bit over.   This recipe is now my standard.  Thanks
Nice and easy!

i love the spicy flavor to this. i actually added more pepper flakes.
Excellent sauce!  I did add some sauteed mushrooms 'cuz I love them!
Simple and delicious. I've been making this since I found it here years ago...and I always crush the tomatoes by hand. Wonderful. Thank you!

i ab-sooo-lut-ly LOVE this recipe......now make huge batches of it and freeze it for the "other half" for when he's "home alone fending for himself".....He Loves it...ive added mascarpone to some batches which worked brilliant....and tinkered with different herbs (whatever is lurking in the cupboard.....its Truly a great find on the internet for me...so simple but yet so Lush....

i like this on pizza.

This is a great chicken dish.  I doubled the sauce and served it over fettuccine.  My Dh is asking for it again soon.  Thanks for posting.

Heavenly!  This was the best (and very easy) meal I made in a long time!  I have made it three times and once forgot the mushrooms - it was good either way!  Thanks!

Great for potluck - enjoyed by all. Want to try it with pasta and can hardly wait for the harvest.

This was an excellent combination of flavors and so easy to prepare. Thanks for sharing.

This recipe gets a standing ovation, AdriMicina!  This was easy, quick and very tasty. My husband just raved of the flavor it had. I follwed the recipe as stated and would not change a thing. Thank you for a wonderful recipe.

I have made this bread 3 times in the past three weeks and each time it was beautiful.  It tastes wonderful and is perfect for toast in the morning or brushetta in the evening  I used my bread machine to mix and go thru the first rise.  After that I let the dough rest for 10 minutes, shape and rise for the 2nd time.  I have had to let the bread rise the second time for 40-50 minutes, but that may just be the cold New England weather. Its a wonderful recipe sure to please.
Comfort food heaven.  I loved this bread and will make it again...soon...Thanks for posting.

Excellent bread with great flavor and texture!  My DH raved as he loves bread that does not have a really hard exterior.  Earlier in the day I placed some olive oil in a ramekin with a smashed garlic clove, fresh rosemary and fresh thyme.  It was wonderful "dipping oil" for the bread.  I served the bread with salmon with balsamic glaze (Recipe #118010), asparagus and roasted baby potatoes (Recipe #133526).  One of the best meals I've made in a long time.

I made this on 4/15/08 for the "Flour Power Photo Challenge", and also as part of mine and SO's dinner. I've always used store bought italian bread,but after making this recipe never again.Since there was only two of us,the recipe was cut in half.And if anyone else decides to do that you'll be sorry,because you'll want the whole loaf. I took the dough and made two mini loaves, and let it rise in a slightly warmed oven for about 30 minutes.Then I baked it for about 25 minutes. The smell as it was baking was just so wonderful.Then after it cooled a bit I split it in half lenghtwise buttered each cut side and sprinkled a little bit of garlic powder on each piece, and popped it under the broiler for about 5 minutes.The taste of fresh made bread was just wonderful. This will be made again. Thank you for posting and "Keep Smiling :)"

The is excellent Italian Bread!! I was about to give up on making homemade Italian Bread. Very easy to throw everything into the bread machine and let the bread machine do all the work. Take the dough out when it beeps and roll into a loaf or like I did 2 loaves. One loaf was the perfect size for my family to have with my Recipe #223402. Thanks for posting this, I will be making this from now on!!

I was making this daily for our regular bread. I doubled it and used the kitchenaid. Came out wonderfully every time. I use instant yeast so after I was done kneading I just divided the dough and let it rise on the pan, then baked. It couldn't have been any easier. I don't use the cornmeal or egg, just spray my cookie sheet with cooking spray. Thanks for sharing!

Quite easy to make and so good!  My DW and I made the bread to go with burgers and Recipe #218828 for dinner last night.  We really enjoyed sopping up all the juices from the beans with the bread.  This bread has excellent texture and this recipe is really easy to follow.  Will make again next week when I make some spaghetti sauce!  Don

Perfect!

eta: I used this dough recipe to make bread bowls - It made 4 small round loaves= turned out wonderful!  :)

Very yummy!  I added a 1/4 tsp garlic which gave it a nice flavor. I think next time I will increase the amount a little.  I used rokmelon's way of cooking, non-bread machine, but I let it raise two times instead of the once.  Turned out very nicely.  Thanks for the great recipe, I will be making this again.

I am so happy with this recipe! Although I consider myself an accomplished cook, I've always been a bit shy about homemade bread. Also, so many recipes make 2 loaves, and we just don't eat that much bread, (unfortunately!) I've had this recipe saved for some time now, so today I decided to get in the kitchen and go for it. I used the dough cycle on my bread machine, and as I watched it, ended up adding a bit of water. Just about 2 teaspoons.  After the cycle was complete, I rolled it out and then rolled up the long way, (for prettiness of the loaf). It took about 40 minutes, (cool kitchen), to double, then I baked it for 25 minutes. VOILA! Perfect crust, perfect innards, not too airy, just perfectly chewy, just like we like our bread! Thanks Andypandy...I am now a bread-baker!
Excellent recipe Andy!  The loaf was crusty on the outside and tender and moist on the inside.  It was enjoyed by all of us at work, when I brought in a lasagna to share with the crew!
Delicious bread Andy!  Went great with our stuffed shells!  Thanks for sharing!
This worked just perfectly. I followed the instructions to the letter and now, we don't buy bread anymore. Thanks!

This recipe is about as easy as they come and has wonderful taste.  My husband has recently started making bread and this is one of our favorite finds.  The texture is perfect and it comes out beautiful every time.

I used a combination of white and whole wheat flour and accidentally put the egg in the dough instead of on top of the loaf and it still turned out AMAZING! I will be using this recipe again and again.

I made this recipe with my kitchenaid mixer.   I reduced the olive oil by half and because I live at altitude, I decreased the yeast by 1/4 tsp.  I had to add some water as the dough was mixing to incorporate all the flour.  I let the dough rise for about an hour then I split into two loaves.  One I streched flat and brushed it with olive oil and sprinkled with fresh rosemary, thyme and pepper.  Then I rolled it up and placed seam side down on a baking sheet.  The other I left plain.  I let them rise another 30 minutes or so and then baked at 400 for about 25 minutes.  The bread was wonderful -- not too dense or too dry.  Two common problems with baking up here.  Thanks for the recipe!
Loved this recipe.  I used my bread machine to make the dough and it was very easy. After taking it out of my bread machine and making it into the log, I let it rise at least 35 minutes.

Terrific...I'm not an overly experienced bread baker, but this was one of my best (and easiest) yet.  I used the stand mixer and after reading some of the reviews, followed the method outlined on kitchenaidtv (yeast and warm water in first, then sugar, let dissolve for a few minutes, add in rest of the ingredients...flour goes in last....watch it as it kneads, took approx 5 minutes for me...when done it clings to the hook and not to the sides of the bowl).  Used some ww flour as suggested (1/2 cup).  Worked out really well, I made three loaves!
Your recipe made me look like an expert bread maker! Tasted really good with a big bowl of soup. Will make again!

Delicious! I made this using my kitchen aide and sub'd 1 cup of whole wheat flour for 1 cup of white. I also was able to set the dough in the fridge for several hours, bring it back to room temp for it's rise and it was a beautiful, flavorful loaf.
I decided to make two loaves today using my kitchen aid mixer and they came out fantastic! It will go great with my chicken soup on this cold and snowy day! Thank you andypandy!

Great bread. It turned out so soft. It is just like the Italian bread we used to buy from the grocery store. I did it all by hand and didn't end up adding all the flour called for (I stopped at 2 1/2 cups) It was delicious! I also set the oven temp. up to 425F and sprayed it every 10 min with water so that the crust would be crispy. It cooked in about the same time. Thanks for posting!

WOWZY...what can one and to so many great reviews except a couple of more gushing praises...easy, delish, perfect- can't get any better that this {{ !!! :) }}...I did it by hand ...mixing wet in to dry and adding a sprinkle or two of garlic powder and white pepper (next time I will try the suggested mixing of the other reviewers with the cupa at a time approach just to see the difference in results - I really didn't read them till it was on the rising stage in my eagerness to give it a try)...I brushed the top w/ a powdered egg sub and a sprinkle of Celtic Sea Salt...really just fabulously yums!- again, ;)...I can see myself making this on a regular basis from the here on out and want to try all sorts add ins like herbs, roasted garlic, sun-dried 'matos and such...made for "I Recommend Game" and it is definitely recommended to try this...you can not go wrong (my husband fell in love with me again) ;)...Thanks for a great recipe share!!! :)

I came upon this recipe a few months ago and have made it several times.  It always comes out beatifully.  The crust is kinda crunchy and the inside is soft and moist.  My whole family loves this bread so much that whenever I make spaghett & meatballs I also have to make this bread!  So Awesome! Thanks Andy!

Definitely an excellent loaf that I will be making often, extremely simple and I very much like some of the suggestions made by other reviewers, I'll be trying them out!  Smelled wonderful, tasted great, we enjoyed this with soup on a chilly autumn evening!

thanks, Andypandy!
Tastes great, excellent texture.  I added another coat of egg wash half way through baking.
We loved this with our spaghetti and meatball dinner!  I loved the crusty outside, tender inside bread!

I've been making this for a couple of years now and just realized that I never reviewed it.  Super easy to make, mins. to throw into bread machine and very easy to form into the loaf.  I do put the egg wash on it and slit the top with scissors.  This also freezes very well.

Haha, this is almost the exact same recipe that was on the bag of bread flour I bought. I made it tonight and it was delicious! I don't have a bread machine, so it was a lot of work doing all the kneading, but it was worth it!

I have made this recipe..thrown all ingrediants into breadmachine dough cycle many time...wonderful!  I let it rise in a round peasant loaf shape, brush w egg and  spread w dehydrated onion bits.. that i soaked in water for 15 mins.. coarse salt, pepper and sesame seeds. I then bake in a dutch oven w lid on that i preheated in oven..bake for 20 mins w lid on , then lid off...OUT OF THIS WORLD!

Fabulous bread! I basted it with the egg whites twice during baking, and also spritzed some water into the oven a few times. It made a gorgeously browned loaf that was delicious! I did have to add water to the dough while it was mixing in the bread machine...a couple tablespoons. I also took another reviewer's advice and rolled it into a log before the second rise.

Very good, basic bread. I used my Kitchenaid mixer to do the kneading, but didn't need to proof the yeast like another reviewer suggested, as I use instant yeast.

If you let it rise at a cooler temperature (like 68 degrees) you will get a better texture to the bread. It will take longer, though, so plan accordingly.

I made this today had to join just to tell you how good it was. just Wonderful, I will make it quite often. I did learn something form this, I did not know you could use all-purpose flour making this kind of bread. Thank you

FANTASTIC!  I can't really add much to the review that hasn't been said already.  And after making it with my bread machine, I'm going to try it again with my Kitchenaid mixer.  What a great idea to add in some roasted garlic!  My only suggestion is to watch how deeply you cut the slits in the top, as mine rose so large that the loaf deformed because I cut it too deep.  Thanks for posting a keeper!

I made this exactly as written the first time, and it is great!  I think next time I will play around a little with adding some garlic powder, fresly grated parmesan cheese, and/or italian seasonings.  I can tell you my bread machine is going to be getting a work-out with this one! :)  Thank you for posting.

I loved this bread.  The second time I made it, I punched the dough down too much and it didn't rise as much, making it a little too dense.  I also brushed the crust with an olive oil while baking- and it added wonderful flavour
I've made bread for years and this is the best recipe I've found.  Moist and delicious.  We LOVE it.
I have made this 3x now and it is perfection each time. I am so glad I did not do what I usually do and toy with it, Now I have followed if exact every time because it turned out so good the 1st time

Great recipe!!  I don't have a bread maker so I did it by hand.  Works up into a lovely dough & yummy bread.  As some of the other posters, I added roasted garlic, but then added a few chopped black olives.  Thank you!!
I've made this countless times and forgot to write the review until now. This is such an easy and great recipe. It results in a perfect loaf every time. Thanks for sharing!
This bread turned out okay in its appearance, but I did not think it had any taste.  Toasting it helps. I don't know where I went wrong!

Dh had gotten italian bread from store that was SO Good! I knew I could make some every bit as good but kids were sceptical. When the loaf was baking ds was impressed. When we cut into it they were ALL impressed!!! This is so good and so easy!!!!!!
Delicious!  I incorporated the ingredient, kneaded well by hand, allowed to rise an hour and then formed two loaves, allowed those to rise 25 minutes and baked.  Yum!!  Perfect with pasta sauce!!

This is pretty good bread.  I also used 1/2 c whole wheat for more of a rustic taste and rolled the dough out and then rolled it up again and baked seam side down.  It took about 30 minutes for my last rise.  Thanks

I have made this many times. It is delicious and has many uses and flavors; loaves, sandwich buns, different spices, flours, etc.  It is a very forgiving recipe. I make it in my stand mixer. Just mix all of the dry ingredients in the bowl, then add the water with olive oil mixed into it. Use dough hook on mixer. The secret is as stated in the recipe "... round, soft, sticky to the touch ball." Thanks so much for a delightful and easy bread!    Terra

This was a great basic bread recipe.  The texture of the crunchy crust with the soft inside was spot on.   Easy to make with the bread machine doing the dough.  I shaped mine into a braided loaf before baking and it worked really well.

This is a delicious recipe! I don't have a working bread machine, so I used my KitchenAid Stand Mixer. I added the sugar and yeast to the warm water, let it foam for 10 minutes before adding it to the other ingredients. Using the bread hook, I kneaded the dough for a few minutes, covered it in a little oil (so it wouldn't stick to the bowl), and covered it for about 25-30 minutes. Then I punched it down, formed the load, and covered it again to rise. I didn't use egg wash, just sprayed water on it before baking. When she says "large loaf," she means it. It's hard to tell in the photo, but it's about enough to feed 8-10 people. I will definitely be making it again. Thanks for sharing!

Perfect!  We loved this bread and it made a beautiful loaf.  Very easy to do in the bread machine, then allowing for the additional rising and baking time.  I scored the top of the loaf in an "X" pattern down the entire length of the loaf before applying the egg white and it baked up so beautifully.  The four of us  demolished the entire loaf in one sitting, except for one piece the dog stole.

I used my Kitchenaid for this recipe. I had to add a little more water, as the dough seemed a bit to dry and my machine wasn't working as it normally would when I make yeast breads. I used the final product with this recipe Recipe #382698 and it was delicious. :)

Very good. Used ABM and had to add a bit of water. Have to remember how humidity affects the flour. I really liked the crust stayed softer, and interior was really nice. TY  Edit 4/23, used left-over bread in Bread Salad 82037.  Perfect pairing.

This dough is wonderful. I am making a loaf as I write this.  The first time I used it for a pizza dough. After using the dough cycle on the bread machine, I put it into a greased pizza pan and just spread it out with my fingers. Put the topping on and let it rise about 30 min. and then in the oven till done at about 375F. Turned out great.

Have made this three times already and just love it!  I don't think I will ever actually COOK bread in my machine again.  This technique of doing the kneading in the bread machine and then taking it out to shape, rise, and bake, produces the BEST bread and this recipe is wonderful.

Good bread. My bread came out a little dense but I think it's because I did it by hand instead of in the bread machine. Really nice and easy to make. Rises really high in the oven so you might want to move the top rack up a bit.
Easy and tasty. I used my mixer to mix the dough and let it rise for a little over an hour for the first rise.

I've been using this recipe for quite a while and didn't realize I didn't rate it.  So, here goes - it's a wonderful, simple Italian bread recipe.  I use my KitchenAid mixer to make the dough, and it always turns out wonderful.  Great with a bowl of homemade soup, or sometimes I form it into rolls for wonderful homemade hoagie rolls.  Yum!!

This is the bread recipe I now use. I kept jumping from one to another because I wasn't satisfied. I use half whole wheat flour in the recipe. Most of the time the loaves tasted too dense using half whole wheat. This one doesn't. I am making this right now and this is about the 5th time making. Wonderful. I use my dough cycle in my bread machine and decide from there whether I want rolls or Italian bread. Great recipe.
EXCELLENT!  If I could give it more stars, I would!  Had to adapt recipe to a KitchenAid mixer, and it worked beautifully.  Thank you so much for an excellent recipe!!!

This is the first time I've made homemade bread.  I too mixed it in my KitchenAid, then kneaded a few times before letting it rise.  The bread was not too dense with great texture and crust.  Let it cool and bake it again for 5-8 min to really crisp the crust.  Delicious and easy.  Thanks andypandy for a great recipe for the rookie bread maker.
Excellent and great bread, nice crust and crumb.
Wow! Great Italian bread.  Made to serve with an Italian meal.  Will use this one all the time, it is the best one I've found.

While looking for recipes to try out my new bread maker found this one and tried it for dinner last night.  Followed the directions to the letter and when putting in the oven sprayed with water for steam at 5 minutes and 10 and it was wonderful.  Nice crunchy crust with a soft, light center and a wonderful taste of fresh bread.  Between DH and me we ate almost half the loaf before the day was over.  It makes a nice big loaf and I'm wondering how it would do to cut the dough in half and freeze half for another day - might just give that a try next time.

I made this tonight for the first time and its the best bread Ive ever made!!  I used my bread maker on the dough setting, and when it beeped...it was time to take out & bake in the oven.  I used a non glazed tile brushed with olive oil, and brushed on the whipped eggs on the bread and it WAS PERFECT!!!  I cant thank you enough!!

This was prepared in my Kitchen Aid mixer like many others that have done reviews! This is a very fluffy and not dense like so many other Italian bread's! It's also because I added more yeast than it called for! Other than that I followed the recipe! For those of us that do it in the mixed, the water should be around 105-110 so the yeast will work properly, no higher than 115 and that's pushing the temp! Also this will freeze well!
I've made this a few times now. It's a wonderful bread recipe. I leave the egg wash off, as I enjoy the bread more without it. This ones a keeper for sure!

I am a picky person when it comes to bread.  A lot of bread recipes I've tried are just plain and many are heavy.  This is great and needs no changing.  All you have to do is follow it, it lacks nothing.  I've made it about 5 times now and my husband and I finish this one, where a lot of loaves never get finished.
Made it for a group of Sisters and they loved it. Excellent.  I didn't change a thing!

Absolutely perfect recipe!!  I opted for the stand mixer method of preparing and mixed the yeast, sugar and warm water in the mixer bowl and allowed to froth for 10 minutes.  I then added in the EVOO and flour directly to the yeast mixture.  I added some salt, pepper and garlic powder to this as well and then let it beat with the dough hook for about 3-4 minutes.  I rolled it in a bowl that'd I'd rubbed down with EVOO to cover the outside of all the dough with a light layer of the oil and then covered it to rise for about 30 minutes.  I punched it down and shaped it into a loaf and covered it to rise once again for 30 more minutes.  I did the egg white wash and baked for about 25 minutes.  Absolutely unbelievable.  Probably my new favorite bread recipe.  Kids and adults devoured this!

Another great way to get that nice hard crust is to fill a little spray bottle with water. Every 8-9 mins slip open the oven door and spray the oven a few times. Its amazing the difference it makes in the crust. Happy eating....I just finished making about 40lbs of lasagna, so Im looking forward to making this bread to go along....

This recipe is fabulous. My family asks me to make it several times a week. The flavor is terrific, the crust is amazing, and it disappears fast in our home. Makes terrific rolls, buns, toast, etc. You can shape it any way you like - add toppings, herbs, whatever., I will make this for years to come - so glad I found this recipe.

I followed danakscully64's instructions for the stand mixer. The bread smelled great, looked professional a the texture is nice. I did not give it 5 stars because we found the taste bland in comparison to other white breads that I make. I think next time I will add a bit more salt.
Thanks for sharing!

Good tasting bread, but I was looking for a more rustic bread. I wanted a bread that has a thick crusty, crunchy crust with a soft,moist crumb.
This is a great bread to get done quick for a meal.Nice size also.

Love this bread... So easy using the bread machine. I used vegetable oil instead of olive oil as I don't like the smell of olive oil and instead of using egg white I used the vegetable oil to brush on top of the bread,then sprinkled rolled oats. Wonderfully soft inside and slightly crusty on top. I baked for 35 minutes before I could get a golden colour and a hollow sound on tapping the bread.

This was super easy to make in my Kitchenaid mixer. The bread rose well and looked beautiful when baked. The texture was perfect - a good crust and soft and airy on the inside. The only issue I had was that it did not have a lot of flavour, as another reviewer has pointed out. Maybe more sugar or salt is needed?
This bread is soooooo good.  I love the texture, and like the author I make the dough in the bread machine and then take it out and shape it for the last rise.  Thanks for posting andypandy!!!!
Very yummy and easy to do.
This bakes up really beautiful.  We loved it.  I like the fact the the bread machine does most of the work.  Thank you for sharing with us.

This was amazing! I did however use about 1/2 cup whole grain flower and also added about 1 Tbsp of Italian spice, and 1/2 tsp of garlic powder to the dough.  I made a second batch and  made it into Hoagies to which I added the italian spice, garlic powder, and parmesan cheese.  It made an amazing sandwich with crock pot Italian Beef (#18462).  I'll definitely be adding this to my favorites.

I was looking for a quick recipe for Italian bread that would go with my lasagna and came across this.  I doubled it and mixed it up in my bread machine but had to take it out to rise because it was overflowing.  It turned out just like the picture, two nice large loaves.  It tasted so good!
I don't own a bread maker or stand mixer with hook, so I used your recipe and kneaded this on my bench top myself. It worked perfectly! It's a great recipe that I'll be using again thank you.
Absolutely a great recipe.  Extremely easy to follow and with a bread machine it seams as if it makes itself.  I have another batch going right now for dinner definitely recommend!
Great !

OMG!!! This is the best bread I've ever made and I make a lot of bread! The taste is authentically Italian. I made this into 2 loaves and baked them on an overturned cookie sheet with a pan of warm water below them on the bottom shelf. They were perfectly browned in 20 minutes. I can't wait to try this recipe as pizza crusts and rolls. Follow this recipe and impress your family and friends.
An other great bread recipe.  I love baking bread there is just nothing like it.  This was amazing!  Thank you for the recipe.  Will make it again for sure.

Wonderful and easy recipe - and foolproof, too!  I'd realized part way through the bread machine cycle that the loaf wasn't rising and that I'd forgotten the yeast.  So I reset the machine, added the yeast, and let it run again.  It turned out beautiful!  I probably should have left it in the oven for five more minutes to brown it a wee bit more, and I chose not to add the egg white (more lazyness than anything).  I will make this one often!  Thanks, andypandy!
First bread I ever made that was edible.  Easy and Awesome, thanks!

I was tempted by this recipe for Italian bread that was easier than the one I've made for the last four years.  I was lured by all the positive reviews but paid for my laziness.  I wish all the bakers out there would try this one: http://www.cookography.com/2008/rustic-italian-bread.  It takes longer and I would love to have my KitchenAid back but I do it from scratch and the effort is well worth it. The only deviation I make is not to bother with the parchment paper -- it isn't necessary and it burns.  I started doing this as I needed a good bread recipe where I could reduce the salt content.  I don't mean to offend the other bread recipe poster nor any of the people who enjoy the simpler recipe but you have to think, if so many Italian grandmothers have been doing it the old-fashioned way, how could they be wrong?
152 reviews!  Well, looks like every review that I couldn't think up has been taken.  Great bread.

I double this recipe for two large loaves. Substitute white flour with 1 cup white bread flour, 4 cups whole wheat, 1 cup flaxseed. Add 3 bulbs roasted garlic, kalamata olives (dry in paper towel before folding into dough) and cut fresh rosemary inside and rolled on outside. Cook on parchment paper with cornmeal. Takes a while to make buy completely worth it...so delicious!

Andypandy, you are my hero! This is truly an amazing, delectable, addicting bread recipe! I made one minor substitution, quite by accident, which, luckily, worked out just fine. Thought I'd share: 
Discovered at the last second that I was out of eggs. I reached into the cabinet for what I thought to be dried egg whites but being blind as a bat, I grabbed meringue powder instead. Didn't discover the switch until my loaf was in the oven. I fretted and stressed until the first bite, which was heavenly! Thank you so much for posting this recipe.
Very nice abm recipe. Will try upping salt amount or adding other spices as well next time.

Wow! This was the easiest bread I've ever made, and delicious to boot! I put everything in the bread machine, pushed start, then 1 1/2 hours later I punched it down, formed a loaf and let it sit for another 1/2 hour. All that was left was to slash, brush with egg wash and pop it in the oven. Voila! Delicious bread. DH and DD are lobbying for this to be our everyday bread. With such an easy recipe, they just might get their wish!
Just baked a loaf of this. Used my bread machine to make the dough. Very nice recipe. Next time will increase it by 50% and make two smaller loaves for the freezer. :)

One of best recipes to date for Italian bread. FYI, baked for 15 mins, brushed with a bit more eggwhite, then topped with a bit of grated gruyere, and shredded mixed Italian cheese, then baked for another 15 mins. (Baked for 30 mins total). Really really good!

Excellent recipe. The bread has a wonderful taste and a lovely crumb. I had to add a bit more water to the recipe to get the right consistency of the dough, but it was a hot dry day here and when making bread I have found that sometimes the liquid/flour ratio needs to be adjusted. I was very pleased with this recipe and have added it to my files.
I love this recipe! I bake it in a tagine since I like a round loaf. It's not only beautiful but has lovely texture and flavour.
This recipe is amazing! I've made it several times and it always come out great. I use it sliced thick to make paninis, yum!

My husband is british, and his brother lived in Italy for a while, so they really got the taste for italian cooking. I added diced tomatoes to this and let it marinate a while since DH is a huge onion and tomatoe person. It was fabulous!
delicious.  followed recipe exactly except i added a few squirts of fresh lemon and a few sundried tomatoes chopped up.  very satisfying and easy to make.  thanks!

Wonderful!
I added no salt, but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. Will make many times in the future - this recipe is a keeper!

Delicious and saucy -- just the way we like it. This sauce smells out-of-the-world and tastes even better. I cooked the noodles the old fashioned way and used dried parsley (about 1 tablespoon) instead of fresh--but enjoyed the lasagna with a loaf of bread machine french bread italian style recipe#63380. Thanks for sharing this keeper!

Really, really great! Just loved the spicy sausages, and the cheese sauce layer was perfect - I don't really like a bland white sauce so this was my ideal lasagne! I followed the recipe except for leaving out the capsicum as I don't like them, but I found everything else to be perfect! Oh, and I added a generous shake of Italian seasoning to the cheese mix too. Thanks for an outstanding recipe Rita!

A chocoholic's dream ! This is simple to put together, yet so luscious. It reminds me a bit of chocolate mousse (though slightly stiffer in texture) but much better for me since I can't eat raw whipping cream. Thanks for posting !

I only had one tablespoon of this in a mini tart, and it was very, very rich. I didn't have an bittersweet chocolate squares that everyone uses, and only had cocoa powder. I recommend adding shredded coconut, or toasted even. The taste was just rich, and I'm one that usually eats an enormous amount of chocolate for satiety- one tbsp of this was enough to send me to the sky.

very rich and lovely
my suggestion is to add a liquer for additional flavour
