I was leary of the maple syrup addition to the recipe and tested a bit with a small portion of the bean mixture. It wasn't a flavor that I cared for...so, I omitted it from the rest of the recipe. These were very colorful and had a great flavor (with the changes that I made).
This is a good recipe. I serve with saltines and Valentina hot sauce.Thanks for posting.
Mariposa, thanks for posting this recipe. Excellent, with excellent  instructions!

This was my first attempt at ANY sort of tamale - my Belizean mother-in-law was really impressed!  I thought they were absolutely delish, and so did the whole family.  I'm going to make them for a dinner party soon.  They were fairly simple for somebody who never did tamales before.
This recipe was great! Very easy to make, and freezes well. These were the hit of our tamale party! I will definitely be making these again! Thank you so-ooo much for this recipe!

You must make these tamales. I'm a tamale-novice and these exceeded my expectations. I was skeptical about the addition of canned cream corn, but it worked really well in the dough, adding a slight sweetness, boosting the corn flavor. The roasted poblanos and bell pepper added a wonderful smoky flavor without overpowering the shrimp. Because the vegetables and shrimp are mixed into the masa dough, rather than concealed in the center, the tamale seems to be studded with bits of red, green and pink. Really festive! I received many compliments on these. Thanks for a great recipe.

This was great, i scaled it way down to a pot pie size and had it for an early lunch.  Used kidney beans i had soaked for another dish and didnt use them all rather than canned and frozen corn kernels.

Thanks so much!
Excellent!  I love recipes that are not only great tasting, but that I can get on the table in less than half an hour.  We love Mexican inspired dishes in our house, so I knew this would be a hit!

I couldn't decide between red kidney beans or black beans, so I used both.  It was hearty and "meaty" even without the meat!  None of the boys complained about having no meat.  The mixture seemed dry, so I added an 8 oz can of tomato sauce.  I also doubled the cumin and oregano.  Thanx for posting this easy meal!  We'll be having this again.

ABSOLUTELY LOVED IT!! TRUE!
SO healthy for me too!
Doubled spices like last review did suggest,
Added jalepenos is what I like best!
Added one small can of corn is does not digest great!
Also added small can drained of capsicum...and used vanilla yogurt instead of sour cream as it all adds up, especially around the holiday season!
THANKS!

I truly admire people that can create recipes like this one. I went in a few weeks ago and thought I could maybe find a few recipes to help me on my low fat journey. Through these lower fat and low fat recipes such as this one, I have lost 17 pounds in about 6 weeks. My hat is off to you Kitten, and I commend you for helping to make my journey, and I'm certain many other's, a shorter journey. This is a fantastic, flavorful  recipe that will remain in my often made book. Thanks for this recipe!

Sue, these are wonderful!  I used egg substitute for the eggs and my homemade salsa (Jalapeno Salsa #38442 
by Dancer^).  Also, I used blue corn tortillas and added diced Canadian Bacon to the eggs.  DH and I loved them.  Thanks so much.
Wonderful!! For our low carb lifestyle we didn't use tortillas.. a good change of pace from a boring breaksfast.. Thank you..Oh, used the Texas Red Enchilada Sauce from 42094.
This is the first time I've used adobo seasoning - well worth the trip to the grocery store this morning!  What a nice flavor.  Thanks!  DH says 'This is a keeper', so it MUST be good.
This was a great breakfast!  I used jalapenos and pepper jack cheese to get a nice little kick.  The taste was great.  Thanks for the recipe for the lovely breakfast treat.
Great way to serve up eggs.  I used a couple premade tostada shells I had and some black bean salsa.  Thanks Sue, you Saucy Senorita!
Really easy & full of flavor--pretty, too--this one is a winner!
Great recipe!  I used oven-to-table bakeware and had a fantastic meal in under 20 min.  This is superb!

This was VERY easy to make.  I think my only complaint is that it needed some more flavor.  I think it was the salsa that I had.  I added in some mange and some green olives and it made it much tastier.  This is very easy and you can impress.

This was very good, and so simple! I made this with tilapia fillets. I used velveeta instead of cheese, and next time I make this, I'll use more, cheese is so good on fish! I made my own salsa and used that, and it was delicious. I prepared it ahead of time, and just stuck it in the fridge until it was time to put it in. It took mine 20 minutes to cook.
easy to fix and different from most fish dishes.  would make it again
This tasted wonderful and was VERY easy to make. It's going into my "inexpensive and quick" meal rotation. Thanks Mercy!

My only complaint with this is that it could have used some seasoning. I think next time I'll put a little fajita seasoning or some garlic salt on the fish before adding everything else. Other than that, it was yummy and quick. The chips also stayed crispy on the top. We served it with Spanish rice and black beans and it was pretty yummy! I'll be making it again.

This recipe is the starting point for the Chile Verde con Puerco my wife and I enjoy. I like to roast and peel the peppers and I don't worry about being exact with the quantities. I will let this simmer for 4 or 5 hours on the stove and it keeps getting better. Ideal for the crockpot. We like to garnish with chopped scallions, cilantro and Crema Fresca. Don't forget some fresh homestyle flour tortillas.

This recipe makes the best chile verde pork I have ever tasted.  My husband and I couldn’t stop eating it.  I wasn’t able to find pablanos so I used jalapenos and serrano peppers.  While I chopped the yellow peppers, I put the jalapenos and serranos in the food processor.  Also, I tossed the pork in a little flour, salt and pepper before browning to help thicken the sauce.  We ate it with flour tortillas and refried beans.  So good!

I made this tonight and it was incredible.  I've given up on ording this out, usually the meat is dry and the sauce is mediocre at best.  The meet was tender and juicy and the sauce alone was worth making this.  My store doesn't carry pork stew meat so I used some pork country ribs we had in the freezer and just cut those up to the appropriate size.  I also dredged the meat in some flours before searing as suggest in other reviews.  I also used olive oil instead of vegetable oil but I don't think that really made a difference.  If I could give this 10 stars I would!!!

This was really good! I tasted it halfway through the last simmer and was really worried--it wasn't so great. But once it had reduced a little more, the flavors really came out. Very good! We served it over brown rice.

This is what Chile Verde is supposed to taste like, I've been looking for this recipe. I halved it and just used what peppers we have in the garden. Replaced poblanos with Anaheims, added a local variety and it was excellent. Next time Iâ€™ll use poblanos and an extra jalapeno for heat. I let it simmer for an extra two hours and crushed the meat against the side of the pan with 30 minutes of simmer time left for a better consistency. YUM!

This is an AWESOME recipe! I have been looking for something like this for a long time. I like to add a couple tablespoons of corn starch to thicken it up for burritos. We add sauce from stew, shredded jack cheese and sour cream to the top of burritos. This is a favorite in our house and we use this recipe at least once a month. Thanks for the GREAT recipe!!!!!

THIS WAS WONDERFUL!!!! I cut this in half - did not add all the jalapenos (just one)- because my pablanos chiles were pretty hot ( and yes I love hot food). I did cook this for about 4 hours - then added fried corn tortills strips and monteray cheese to the top of the bowls - IT WAS FANTASTIC!!

This makes a huge portion. I froze the leftovers and used them as an addition to all sorts of mexican recipes-chili, tacos, pulled pork. I fixed it as is. With the leftovers, I used a stick blender, separated the meat out, and blended all the peppers to a finer texture. This is good.

This turned out really well! Concerned that my pork loin was too "lean" of a cut and might be tough, I stewed it all morning in the crock pot having seasoned it over night with dry spices, cumin coriander, chili powder and black pepper.
I added the vegetables in the afternoon to finish it and it turned out great. I did not use any broth, the tomatillos released a ton of water.

Though next time I'll cut back a little on the broth to make a thicker product, the taste of this was spectacular.  I've been wanting to experiment with tomatillos for a while and this was a great start. My wife is from Colombia and it reminded her very much of sancocho. (From a Colombian that is quite the compliment). Personally, I think this taste better than any sancocho I've every had. Even my own.  I think next time I'll also grill my peppers and tomatillos before hand for an even deeper flavor.

Great recipe!  I too would cut back on the amount of broth to allow it to thicken quicker....I thickened it with corn starch and was just what I had been looking for..my wife who is Mexican also gave it a 5 star rating!  Thanks for posting....................Rick B(2)

I have received rave reviews from this chili recipe.  So delicious.
I cooked it about an hour longer than indicated because mine was still quite watery.  I also used a mixture of serranos and poblanos.

This is what I've been searching for!!! Such a simple and delicious recipe! I halved the recipe for dinner for my and DH. My store does not carry pork stew meat so I used a pork shoulder and cut into bite sized pieces. Could not find poblano peppers, so I took a page from BabyKEsq and use serrano peppers. After reading other reviews, I only used 6 cups of broth and it came out lovely. I dredged the meat in flour before browning and this turned out fabulous! Even my DH (who is something of a food snob) enjoyed it! It has been simmering on very low for about an hour or so and it is so good! Thanks for posting. UPDATE: Made again for a recent get together and I left 1 whole jalapeno unseeded; made as directed. It was SOOO good! Had a good amount of kick to it! It was so good, my friend had to chastise her husband for going back for a 4th bowl!

I can't believe it!!  Finally after 15+ years I have found "the" recipe.  After moving to NC from CA I thought I would never again taste the dish that I loved so much from my favorite mexican food place in California!  I have been searching, with no luck, to find a restaurant locally that could duplicate the one thing I craved for years.  Never has anyone even come close to getting the taste right.  NOW... NOW I have it!  I made this tonight with my husband and I was in Heaven after just one bite!  I can't thank you enough for posting this.  
I didn't use the poblano peppers but instead used a combination of jalepenos (seeded and inner ribs removed) and canned green chiles.  I let mine stew for a good 2+ hours and it was perfect. Thick, rich, wonderful pot of goodness!  It doesn't get any better than this!
Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!
Very tasty.  Delish with rice.  I used the crock pot for this recipe and it was great.

I cut this recipe in half but other than that followed to a T. Really good flavor. I think next time I will add more Jalapenos because I like the heat and maybe even try it in the crock pot. Thank you for a great post!
This is the most amazing recipe ever! It tastes best when its fresh, but not bad re-heated. If you make it exact (with just a TAD less liquid) then you will end up with the best dinner ever!

Very good!  I've made chili verde often with chicken and chilis - it was fun to use pork and tomatillos!  I made this in the crockpot.  Started early in the morning and cooked slowly throughout the day.  I used a cut-up pork tenderloin, and regular green peppers instead of pablanos and jalapenos as my kids don't tolerate the heat.  Added a few cans of pinto beans to make this a little thicker.  This turned out flavorful, interesting and filling.

I used pork tender loin instead of pork stew meat -- all I had.  I ended up cooking the stew for a total of 3-4hours to reduce the amount of liquid to thicken up.  Wow, wow, wow - yep, I said it 3 times. Pork was fall apart tender.  Liquid was velvety and thick (after the extra cooking time); extremely flavorful.  This is one of those recipes that will be in my 'go-to' vault.

Excellent.  I left out the bell pepper and the jalapeno, but used the pablanos.  I thought this was plenty of peppers and it wasn't hot since I removed the seeds.   It was so good served over plain rice and refried beans with tortillas.

This was outstanding; my only mistake was making it cause my family now says we don't have to go out for Chile Verde anymore.  The only thing I left out was the cumin (family doesn't like it) and I roasted all the peppers/chiles.  Like others I did let it simmer for about 4 hours.

While this was really good, I thought that it lacked a bit in intensity of flavor. I simmered it for close to 4 hours total, having roasted and peeled the peppers before adding them. Is there just too much liquid in this? Mine was just so much thinner than the picture. I also wish I had left my roast whole, then shredded it. This would have lent a much nicer texture than the cubed pork. I would definitely make this again, though, just with less liquid. Yum!

Excellent!  I made a third of the  recipe and it is great.  Wish I would have made the entire recipe.  I used fresh chicken broth,  roasted anaheim chiles, and fresh tomatillos from the garden.  Will make again soon to use my tomatillos.

Halved the recipe, used pork tenderloin, 1 habernero ppr and some small garden varieties. Should have read the reviews to know to cook longer and ours wasn't hot enough but because I love growing tomatillos, I will give this recipe another try. Well we have tried this again with full amount of pork but still feel there is far too much liquid or we are simmering way too low because after 8 hours it was still very soupy but the flavor is great.  4.5 qts = 16 cups???
Taste wise, this was exactly what I was looking for.. but it was really runny! Next time, I'd definitely cut out some of the broth.

Excellent recipe!!! I read the other reviews and agreed that using a little less broth makes it not as runny. Other than that it is fantastic. I actually used this recipe this year for our mexican themed easter dinner. Everyone loved it!!! Thanks for the recipe...it is one that I will use often.
This is by far the easiet and most authentic tasting Chili Verde... it was a hit with my family. I love it

This is so GOOD!!  I am making it again as I type this!  I had made a batch back in Feb.(Ithought I had posted a review?) and froze a whole bunch of it, which came in really handy for a quick go-to meal, but we just ran out last weekend!  It is simmering away on the stove and the house smells AMAZING when you walk in.  My husband is going to be thrilled when he gets home tonight!  He LOVES this!  Thanks for a great recipe!!

Wow, if I could, I would give this recipe 10 stars. It seemed like a simple enough recipe, and nothing special, but it was delicious. I've been so disappointed by pork lately, always dry. This pork was moist and tastey. My husband is Mexican (from Mexico) and commented several times how good it was. Usually he just eats and doesn't give feedback, so this will be a keeper for me.

I have made this recipe several times(found it on Allrecipes) This is delicious but please note I and many have found the broth is way too much. I think it is a typo. I usually cut the recipe in half(family of 5   leftovers=plenty of food) which then calls for 9 cups, I use 2 cups or less. Otherwise it is delicious. Try it served with white or spanish rice!!

This is a great recipe. I have searched for 12 years for this. Chili Verde was a dish I use to order a lot when I lived in Arizona, and being back in Michigan can not find it anywhere. I will have to agree with a lot of the posters below, the broth is to much. This recipe calls for 4 plus qts, this is my first time making it and I have only used 2 qts and think that may be a bit too much. Be it does have amazing flavor and reminds me of the good times in Arizona!!

This was awesome!

I halved the recipe and used 6 cups of chicken broth and it came out thick & delicious. I also shredded the cubed pork after it had simmered for a couple of hours to make it more burrito friendly.

Excellent flavor!

This is an amazing recipe. It is a must try for those of you who grow tomatillos, as the plants are prolific. We have enjoyed this authentic soup several times, enjoying it as written. We have found that we prefer substituting chicken for the pork & to increase the quantity of tomatillos by another pound. We serve it over rice as the recipe is a litte thin (we don't try to tweak it though because the flavor is SIMPLY AMAZING)!!!! Everyone that has tried this has asked for the recipe. Make it... you will not be disappointed.
Thank you for a keeper!

I just moved to Texas and had never had chili verde, but have tried some other things with poblanos and this seemed like something that sounded really wonderful.  Little did I know......this turned out INCREDIBLE the 1st time, and the flavors are amazing!!  I did read all the reviews 1st, and used less of the liquid which made it a very hearty stew- sort of chili, the way we really like it!  I might try chicken next time just to make it a little more heart-healthy.  All in all, a definite keeper and will be going to this recipe many times in the future for a crowd pleaser!!!!

Delicious chili verde! I let it simmer for about 3 hours to get the pork and peppers to be nice and tender. I only used 2 cups of stock/broth, which was plenty since the pork and peppers release a ton of liquid as they simmer. In fact, next time I'd add only 1 cup of broth. This stew paired well with a Mexican rice side dish and a fresh cilantro garnish. Thanks for posting!

My husband is a gourmet cook and I am a tough critic, but I have to give this recipe 5 stars, hands down!  This is by far the best chili verde recipe we've tried.  I, like other readers, cut the chicken broth in half and let it simmer on low for 3 hours.  I used pork tenderloin and added a few more jalapenos because we enjoy the spice!  It turned out INCREDIBLE!  We had our Pastor's family and a visiting Pastor and his wife over and everyone loved it!  Great Recipe!

Love this recipe. The flavor is great and the heat isn't too much, but I like it super spicy so next time I will add another jalapeño or two! The consistency is a bit runny so next time I will use half the broth but I thickened with cornstarch and that helped. Will definitely make again. I also purred some of the peppers to give it a smooth consistency and added potatoes the last 20 min.
This was very good. I cut the recipe in half and still had tons left. It was great mixed with rice, cheddar cheese on top, and scooped up by tortilla chips. Thanks for posting!
Flavor was good...but waaaaay too runny!  Definitely cut down the liquid.  I'll likely make it again, but with far less liquid.

We love this recipe! I had been searching for a green chili stew like those we have enjoyed while vacationing in New Mexico, and this chili is perfect. I cubed a boneless center cut pork loin roast, cut the broth to 5 cups, roasted and peeled the poblanos for a sweeter, smokey flavor, and cooked for a total of 3 hours like reviewers suggested.  Thanks, Johnney, for sharing this amazing recipe. This is now a family favorite.

This recipe is just amazing. I halved the recipe & It was still a huge amount. I assume it was supposed to be 4 1/2 cups not quarts of broth, so that is what I used. It was perfect. Like other reviews I simmered it for about 3-4 hours to make sure the meat fell apart. It is great to see a recipe that is all fresh food.

I made this for a pot luck at work. After reading other reviews, I was light handed with the chicken stock. I started with only 2 cups and added more as needed. I like mine to thicken and serve it with tortillas to eat it with. The jalis weren't hot so I added some hot sauce for kick. This was the first empty container at the pot luck. Several people asked for the recipe. And others that came late kept asking me where was the chili Verde every one was raving about...Sorry all gone! This is a keeper that will be made over and over again. Only thing bad was...I didn't get to enjoy much myself.
This was so yummy! I made it exactly as written and the only change I would make next time is to use less liquid as other reviews have suggested. Thank you for a great recipe!

I cut back the amount of broth by a bit, and simmered the stew for 3 hours.  At that point, I shredded the cubes of pork (fished them out & shredded them on a plate, then returned it to the pot).  Then I simmered it another hour.  Wow, just wow.  This is a keeper.  The multi-hour simmer reduces the mixture, and makes the pork easy to shred.  From there, the shredded meat really absorbs the flavor.  Best green chili I've ever had.

Flavor is definitely 5-star.  I reduced chicken broth to a quart, vs 4.5qts in the recipe, and it was pretty thin.  Don't use canned green chilies, as they are already too soft and contribute to an even thinner consistency.<br/>Only added ingredient was about a tablespoon of fresh oregano.<br/>I will follow other hints here and continue to reduce liquid, perhaps to 1 or 2 cups of broth in order to thicken it up, but don't know if much can be done to improve flavor which is just outstanding.

Hey guys been making this for years ...we thicken it up if needed and dont add as much broth but top it off with sour cream and  cheddar cheese and grab a tortilla..Its a meal and  is a big hit ALWAYS

I made this tonight and cut the amount of liquid back to 3 quarts....still WAY too much liquid it was very runny. I even simmered on low for like 4 hours and still runny also simmering too long starts to break up the meat too much. The taste was good but tastes a little diluted in that much liquid. Next time I will cut the liquid way back maybe only 1 quart of broth or none might just pour the tomatillo mixture in then add broth as needed. I will definitely give this another try. All and all it was a hit in my house.

While the flavor is five stars the recipe calling for that much liquid dropped it one.

I cut the recipe exactly in half *and used only one cup of broth* and it was still too much. 

My tweeks: I grilled all the vegetables so I could peel them. I did not seed the jalapeño to get some heat. Used giant slab of bone in pork leg, grilled as well after a dry rub, and put whole into crock pot to be taken out when done and shredded. 

I drained some of the excess liquid to simmer on stove and thicken up then returned to main. 

Huge hit. My family likes to add diced potatoes to chile verde stew which is more tex mex, not authentic. Only used one large potatoe.

Hands down the best pork stew I've ever made. My family raved about it and we're all tough critics. Like others, I halved the recipe, only used 2 cups of stock and added some ground coriander. I roasted the poblanos and it gave it a nice smoky flavor. This is a keeper.

This is really a great chili verde. Super balanced and delicious. 

But I gave it 4 stars as it is written with way too much chicken stock shown. I cut it by about 30% and that is still too much fluid.

So I did some thickening by mixing 2 Tbls of masa harina with 3 Tbls of cider vinegar in a bowl until smooth. I stirred this in and simmered for another 10 mins.

This did provide more body but cutting the fluid volume by 50% is probably the better way to go. Maybe both if you like it thicker.

Let me start my husband 100% Mexican and I followed this recipe 100% and it was a total fail!! My husband said it was too white!!! (I'm a good cook, but this a green sauce I cannot perfect) It smelled amazing but was too sweet for his palette! I'm really looking for the perfect restaurant style green sauce!! If anyone can help please do!!
It was great. I should have read the recommendations to use WAY less broth. 2 cups at most. Delicious. Thanks.

I make a lot of chili verde each year, it's one of my most requested potluck dishes and this recipe looks very close to what I do. I visited here to see suggestions on making the dish without roasting the tomatillos first. I digress, this can be a great dish without breaking the bank. To thicken this chili I use xanthan (sometimes called xanthan gum). It takes very little powder, it is clear, shiny and flavorless when fully mixed (and adds no net carbs). With a little practice you will get just the right consistency. To keep it from lumping up mix, first in a separate bowl until smooth, I like to use oil or butter but you can use plain water. I would start off with 1 teaspoon for this recipe and add more (premixed) to achieve the body you like. Stir it in to your chili well and let it sit for a couple of minutes before you decide if you want more.
Perfect for parties! Tastes great too!

Made this for a staff potluck--universal praise. Makes A LOT of dip! Used low fat sour cream and shredded cheese to save a cal or two; also used pre-made deli guac to save time--no problem. Used frito scoops and served with 3 different bottles of hot sauce for fun. Recommended, easy, and impressive.

Delicious comfort food! Great flavor and very quick to make. I used 1 teaspoon of chili powder and cumin, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder instead of taco seasoning. Love the black beans in this. I'm so glad I tried this dish! Thanks for sharing Chipotle Chick!

I used Walnuts (had a huge supply on hand) and they are excellent.  I think Pecans would work too.  Be careful when you are roasting them they burn easily. 17 minutes was all it took for this lot. Thanks Gay for an easy way to have something just a little different

What an addictive treat!! I bought canned cashews to use for this recipe & didn't think to look at the cans before using them.  Next time I will cut back on the salt as the canned cashews were already salted but the flavor is incredible. I loved the flavor & the slight heat. This recipe is a definite keeper!!
Yummy!   I adjusted the spices to my taste and it was a great snack for me and my fiance.   I think I'm going to have to make these on a weekly basis!
Delicious, I made the recipe as stated. Great flavours and very moreish.

These are quite good! I made these along with another nut mix that uses mostly pecans and both were quite popular. I like that these use egg white rather than oil as an spice adhesive because it is much lower in fat, although it provides a slightly different texture than those recipes using oil. Still great all around, easy to prepare and transport to other places- this will be another recipe I enjoy bringing to get togethers as well as giving as food gifts. Thanks for posting!

Thanks for sharing this great recipe Gay! Great flavours and so easy. I only had about 2 cups of cashews but still used all the spices as directed and it worked great. The only problem with this recipe is that it makes nowhere near 24 servings, at least not if I'm around! :)

We liked the flavor of these cashews. They had a little heat but not overly hot. They were easy to make. 

Thanks Gay Gilmore. 

Bullwinkle

Very good mix of flavours with a slow burn heat.  I made them as part of my gift hampers for Christmas.  Had to keep chasing my husband out of the kitchen because of too much sampling:)  Thanks for sharing!

Well, I made these and as they were cooling, I had to chase off DH several times.  He kept eating them and eating them and eating them.  I begged him to save a few for the guests.  He did finally manage to control himself but does love these.  The prep and cooking were easy.  Thanks.
Great!!  Made as directed with no subs.  Worked even for those who aren't into spicy.  Thanks, Gay.
delicious - not what i was expecting at all, better in fact!
Very tasty- used this for our Mardi Gras party. My 9 year old did all the measuring and mixing, as she is quickly becoming a "chef". My husband loved the taste, as did the guests.
Made this as nibbles for a dinner party, and everyone loved them. Thanks for posting!!

Good snack. I have enjoyed them despite an occcasional need for a Tums ;). I think when I make them again I may have to use less cayenne and more salt to tweak for our personal preference. The lime juice sounds good too. This flexible recipe is very easy to prepare. Perhaps almonds next time with a bit more sugar, hmmm...

I have made this recipe several times now and I've used peanuts, cashews and pistachios. They are all great. I also added 1 tsp of lime juice to the egg white (instead of water) for more tang. I also used 2 tsp chili powder (New Mexico Hot Chili powder) and increased the cayenne pepper to 1 tsp. We like them just a little kickier! These are fantastic whatever nut you decide to use. UPDATE:  (8/08) I made these again with peanuts recently and instead of the cayanne pepper I used 1/2 tsp ground Chipotle Chile Pepper - fantastic!!! Very smoky flavor.

these were an awesome addition to my super bowl menu!!  the only changes i made were to double the recipe, use a delux mixed nut blend, use a tad less sugar and added some lime juice!  chili lime nuts!!  yum!!  everyone really loved these.  thanks for posting, will make again and again for parties where drinking is involved!!! ;)

I wasn't sure whether to use raw or roasted cashews, so I used raw. They turned out really well. They don't really crunch up until they have cooled. I thought I had done something wrong. I made them for a birthday gift for my dad.

Wow. I was skeptical about the amount of cumin, and while it was baking, I was doubtful. Just ate one and CANNOT BELIEVE how delicious they are!!!! I added lemon juice to the egg white. Thanks for the great recipe!

These are really unusual and tasty! I used tilapia for the fish, sriracha for the hot sauce, and I didn't include the optional coconut meat. These were really quick to prepare.  I only got 6 tortillas out of this rather than 8, but I may have overfilled them. Thanks for posting!

Thank you so much for posting this recipe!  I love taco meat but I don't eat onions, so I can't use those McCormick's flavor packets.  This is just great.  I of course left out the onion and onion powder and added more garlic and chili powder.  I haven't even put it in a tortilla yet -- just ate some out of the pan.  Thanks again.

So happy to have found this recipe.  The taste of the meat is great without being overwhelmed with spices. I used 1/2 c. tomato sauce, omitted the turmeric (didn't have any on hand), and added an extra 1/2 c. water because the mixture got quite thick. (Recipe doesn't say to cover it, so I didn't).  Ate it in a hamburger bun and enjoyed every bite.  TY for sharing, Amy!
Great! Easy. We did not use the flour in the mix or the tomatoes at the end.

We did like this to use for burritos.However adding the flour mixture gave it a slightly odd pastey texture.I was out of onion powder, but since I already had plenty of sauteed onion in there, it seemed moot to add more.I had doubled the recipe, but found I needed to add more of the water and tomato sauce because it was too thick and sticking to the pan.Your seasonings are very good in it though. Thank you!

This has become a staple recipe at my house. It is so easy to prepare and the flavor is the best! I like to make up packets of the flour and seasoning ahead of time so I can grab n' go on really busy nights. Thanks for posting such a tasty, time-saver recipe!

This has a lovely flavor. I used it to fill enchiladas, it is the perfect texture for this, it stays in place when you roll unlike a looser meat. I didn't feel I had to add cheese to keep the enchialdas together. This earns a stop in the repeats file!

As written, this recipe tasted like plain hamburger!  I had to do a lot of doctoring to give it flavor, such as tripling the chili powder and cumin, doubling the paprika, and adding some cayenne pepper.  Even then it was missing something.
Yummy! I put this in a soft shell taco. Very yummy and husband even enjoyed! Will eat again on a very busy day!
This was so fantastic and full of flavour.  You could make this a meat dish, substitute chicken for mushrooms.  We used tomato tortillas
This was really wonderful.  I substituted the spinach for shredded chicken because my husband needs some meat in his meals. :-) We all loved it and will definitely make again.  Thanks for the recipe!
mmmm!! this was great!! i didn't had any red pepper flakes so i omitted them, and i was out of fresh cilantro so i added fresh basil to the sour cream!
Great enchiladas!  We loved the filling - not too spicy, but just right.  The sauce was very good too, but next time I will reduce the chili powder out of personal preference.  Thanks for posting!

This was very refreshing and tasted great.  Next time I will blend the corn to give it a smoother texture.  I have had corn ice cream at a small shop in Lares, Puerto Rico and they sprinkle cinnamin on the top which I high recommend.  Thanks for posting
I had made exactly the same rice one afternoon for lunch while we were in the US. We loved the flavours of this dish. Very very good recipe!
super easy and delicious. Leftovers were great for lunches.
Bland, bland, bland...Way too much rice and cumin for the recipe. Not what I expected.

This was really easy to put together.  I did use brown rice instead of white, and frozen veggies instead of canned.  All in all a healthy and tasty meal.  Not very much zip, and a little more rice then I wanted.  Next time I'll cut the rice down a smidge and add more salsa.  Thanks!

This was great! The only changes I made was that I fried my rice first the way my SIL taught me to do and I didn't add corn just because I'm out.  I also added a 1/2 can of tomatoes and didn't add green pepper just because we don't like it.  This was so easy and so tasty and will make a great side to my chicken enchilada pie that I made at the same time. Thanks!

I had some leftover rice from the night before so I used that. I cooked the onion for a bit and then added the drained and rinsed black beans. I added the cumin and garlic powerder right after because the spices taste better if you let them cook. I had to add a cup of water so that the spices could cook all the way. When the water had simmered away the beans were done. I put the beans on top of the rice and then added the salsa on the top of that with some sour cream on the side. We had this for lunch with some quesadillas made with cheese, tomato and green onions. I like to mix the black beans, rice, salsa, and sour cream and use this as a dip for my quesadillas. Not exatly healthy but sooo good!

Yum!  This is so tasty and so easy.  I did try to skip the step of dipping the tortillas in the hot oil and instead tried to microwave them to get them soft but that didn't work well.  My fault.  But, even though the rolls broke up, it tasted great!  Reminds me of my Chicken Green Chili casserole.  This is so simple!  Thanks Barb!

I use flour tortillas when making this often-requested recipe, one of my husband's favorites. Method: Just before adding the heated sauce (soup, enchilada sauce, milk, & green chiles) to the browned meat, soften the flour tortillas by dipping each one into the sauce. This eliminates the need for frying in oil. For best results, increase the enchilada sauce to 15 ounces. Note: I make these enchiladas in a 13" electric skillet, not on the stove-top.

This was a very good dish.  My entire family loved it.  I didn't change anything.  Just make sure that you strictly stick to frying the corn tortillas 3 seconds per side.  It does matter!  I use a omelet pan to fry in so I didn't have to dirty another full size skillet.  A recommended dish!

When I saw this in 'New Reviews', I thought it would be an excellent Saturday night supper, and it was.  This was very much enjoyed by my family and I have some leftovers for my lunch on Monday.  I made this exactly as written but I agree with Barb that some beans added to the cheese/olive filling would be nice and I'll try that next time.  Thanks Barb :)

I tried this recipe using my new electric skillet . It was just great ! I added some Ranch Beans to the cheese(did not use the olives)and it was enjoyed by everyone !! I will be making this again soon !

Perhaps it was because I used reduced fat cream of mushroom soup, but I was a little dissapointed in the way these enchiladas turned out at first. BUT, the next day I had a left-over enchilada for lunch. These are like spaghetti; The left-overs taste better than the first time around!
Hate to be harsh, but this was terrible. The "sauce" tasted like Beef Stroganoff because of the cream of mushroom soup. I should have known better. Happy cooking!
Deb's Recipes provided a great suggestion re dipping in sauce instead of oil.

I did this the other night. It was EXCELLENT. I also put:

Sliced black olives
Cilantro
Diced Fresh Tomatoes
Sharp Cheddar AND Jack cheese
Sliced pickled jalapenos
I also used the optional salsa (Pace HOT) and sour cream.
Mmm! great stuff!

Excellent idea to help use up the last of the taco meat since we are out of tortillas.  I only made one potato and added some fresh chopped tomato plus some cheddar cheese.  This made a great lunch for me today; thanks, Chris!
We LOVED these!  Very quick and easy, and budget friendly, too.  I also added chopped tomato on mine.  Delicious!

This is such a great recipe for kids! I gave each one of mine a baked potato and just put all the toppings at the dinner table so they could fill them with whatever they liked. It's so much easier for them to eat than tacos that break apart. My family now calls them "Potacos".

We love Taco Baked Potatoes! Have been making them for years! Here is what I do: Rub a large potato with vegetable oil, mix together salt, pepper, a little ground cumin and chili powder and sprinkle on the outside of the potato before baking. Adds lots of flavor. Follow recipe exactly, I also finish it with diced avocados and crushed tortilla chips!  Very pretty presentation!

This was my first attempt to make salsa. It was very easy. My family liked it when I served it with our Mexican meal.

Thanks Kendra

I've given this 3-stars because, as written, this was VERY spicy and tasted mainly of chilis and water. 

However, I added 1 c. of canned pureed tomatoes to cool it down. With this adaptation, I found it still quite spicy, but much richer and tastier. This would bring it up to 4 or even 5 stars, in my opinion.

I also left out the sour cream, so I could freeze what was left over. I put it on as a garnish instead.

With the addition of the tomato puree, this made enough sauce to pour over about 15 - 20 burritos.

I used the adapted version to make "Hefty-Defty Roly-Poly Weebles Wobbles But They Don't Fall Down Burritos" (#37673) "enchilado" style and it was absolutely restaurant-quality. Yum!

I've been on a low carb diet, so was very excited to find this soup recipe. I made it the first time exactly to recipe and found it to be okay, but bland.  I added some hot sauce and bouillon granules and liked it much better.  This time I made it with chicken broth, 3 large cloves of garlic, and simmered it for 20 minutes before adding the fish.  At this time I also added about 1/2 T of Louisiana hot sauce.  I'm on my second bowl and loving every drop.  This is my favorite low-carb recipe so far.  Thanks, Ginny Sue!

You are my new best friend! I'm used to cooking in a hurry for just two people and am always at a loss for potluck recipes. I just made a triple amount of this recipe for my big church potluck tomorrow and it is DELICIOUS as well as very colorful. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe. At last I can stop making excuses to avoid potlucks. This is a dish I'll be proud to bring.
Great recipe!!!!  I do love this type of salad, so it was right up my ally!!!  Would not change a thing about this recipe.

This is THE BEST salsa! Its so easy and simple to throw together for any get-together. People ask me for this recipe every time I make this. 
It has a great texture (unlike those runny watery salsas). The jalapenos give it a nice little kick without being overly spicy, and the cilantro and lime juice adds a great little tangy flavor. MAKE THIS SALSA its awesome :)

What a great recipe, it has it all, bright colors, fresh taste, wonderful blend of flavors and best of all so easy to make. Served at a Mexican Themed dinner and everyone commented on the how much the liked it, didn't tell a soul how easy it is. Made just as directed and wouldn't change a thing

I wonder if some extra garlic might bring the flavor out more. It would have been nicer with more substance. Thanks for posting!

This was EXCELLENT!!  I did make a few changes.....my kids don't like Kahlua anything..so I used Creme de Cocoa instead. it is verry delightful, creamy and just great i recommended

Instead of caramel in the bottoms, I think raspberry juice(strained from frozen raspberries) and sugar caramelized would be nice. 
Thanks Looney, for a delicious recipe.

Perfectly tasty and easy! My husband loved these! Will be making these again!
These were really easy and very good. It made a lot, so we had plenty of leftovers, which heated up great the next day. Thanks for the easy and yummy recipe! :)

Very quick, easy and good!  I added some garlic to the beef, but otherwise made these as written.  The whole family enjoyed these; thanx!

These were excellent. We really enjoyed them. I had cut the recipe in half since we were only two. I liked this recipe because it was really quick to put together and the flavor was awesome. Thanks for sharing your recipe.

Yum, yum, yum! We love this recipe and make it frequently now! It's so easy and hearty! My Fiance and I really enjoyed this recipe-I had a combo in the freezer of leftover beef and pork roast which I shredded, I used my tomato/serrano chili blend that I canned this year along with homemade refried beans-a Quick and very tasty recipe that I will recommend-Thanks for posting!!

Di

These were superb.  I used browned ground pork instead of tenderloins, and served them with extra jalapenos, guacomole. and sour cream!  Delicious!  My DH is already requesting them again.  Certainly a keeper for my household!
good- I just cooked it on the stove and we filled our tortillas at the table. Good, but I will make 1/2 the amount.

Good burritos without much work. I used leftover pork roast cut in bite-sized pieces.  I left out the beans, but added a little garlic.  I also added some extra cheese on top.  I think it's really more than 4 servings, because they are quite filling.  A nice change from the usual.
This recipe is a great way to make sure of leftover pork roast -- just cut it up to simmer with the tomatoes and take it from there. An instant stand-by for my family's table.

I made this as it seemed to be something that I could put together quickly after work, and I was very pleased with it.  I did add some cilantro and omitted the sour cream (personal preference). Fauve, I so wish there were more stars for this wonderful pizza.  It's been years since I had a taco pizza and this was better then any I've ever had. This recipe was a hit with the whole family, especially my 14-year-old son.  I actually made a few adjustments at his request. This was amazing.  I think I dreamt aobut it for like the next 3 nights.  MMMM
Great recipe, we precooked the meat at home and finished it in a cast iron dutch oven on a camp out. The scouts devoured it.
This was really good but I made a couple of changes.  I used refried beans mixed with some salsa and spread that over the crust before adding the meat.  Thanks!!
Awesome! I douhled the amount of cheese, left out the olives, used salsa instead of tomatoes and added green onions.

This was a very difficult recipe to rate, and I rated it on the outcome alone.  I had some serious problem with the sauce.  I followed your instructions to the tee, not daring to change a thing since I have never made anything like this.  The sauce was my problem.  I followed instruction 2 thru 9 exactly.  But at the end of the last 30 minutes of simmering the sauce, it was still runny.  I continued to simmer for another 20-30 minutes without any change.  So I decided to do something.  I combined  an additional 1 tbl of milk and 2 tsp of cornstarch and added it to the mixture.  I simmered it another 30 minutes and it was a little thicker, but not thick enough to not run off the crape.  So I decided to add an additional combined 1 tbl of milk and 2 tsp of cornstrach and after 30 more minutes or a little more, the sauce was thick as it was suppose to be.  I was able to add it to the crapes and spread as directed and everything else worked out find.  I used your Basic Whole Wheat French Crepe recipe adding the 2 tbls  of sugar and the ground cinnamon and ground cloves.  I wasn't sure I was suppose to add the cinnamon and cloves, but I'm glad I did.  Another problem I had was this did not have a caramel taste to it.  It was more like vanilla.  All in all we really did enjoy the end result, very rich and absolutely delightful.  It just took me all afternoon to accomplish it.

This rice reminded me of Tex-Mex rice which is a Mexican rice I had cooked when in Florida. I loved it just as much as I loved this. I substituted the tomato boullion with 1/2 chopped tomato and the sour cream with plain fat-free yoghurt. This rice tastes good and I'll make it again. Thanks for posting!

How I wish I had tried this sooner!  This sauce is so easy; I threw it together in no time, and the end result was a masterpiece! All of the spices just work together and the fresh lime juice and capers really put it over the top. I could eat this every day and probably will for a while.  Thanks for sharing such a winner!

Easy easy easy! Unfortunately, I only had fat free sour cream on hand and used that. The sauce was a bit more runny than I would have liked- but fat free sour cream is thinner than regular so that was my fault not the recipe. I couldn't resist adding chopped cilantro. Good sauce recipe! I, too, sometimes use frozen fish sticks. I prefer Van de Kamps fish tenders.They are made with fillets not minced fish and the batter is sorta like a tempura.

This is so good! I have been looking for a good sauce for fish taco's and this is it! I did omit the cumin & cayanne and followed the rest to a "T". Wonderful, I will use this one often.
Thanks TigerJo
I was looking for a sauce like the one that is on the fish tacos at Baja Fresh. This is perfect!

This was fantastic on my fish tacos today!  It's fresh and compliments fish tacos perfectly - very similar to the sauce used at Taco del Mar.  I added a few shakes of green tabasco for a little added ole!
Not bad, I would leave out the capers next time, they detracted from the southwest flavor. I think that cilantro would be excellent. I added a smidge of buttermilk to thin it out a little.

This was good.  I used yogurt instead of sour cream to cut down the fat.  I also left out the capers based on a previous review and the fact that I generally don't like capers in things.  The flavor was very good.  I made blackened salmon for the fish and served on flour tortillas with cabbage and picco.  Black refried beans and brown rice on the side.

Yum!  This was easy for spur of the moment fish tacos.  I didn't have any fresh cilantro, so most other sauces were not in the cards, but this tasted wonderful!  Will definitely be making this again, thanks for posting.
What a great sauce.  I made it with blackened Mahi, Cabbage, and Colby cheese in a Flour tortilla.  Delicious.  Thank you.
We enjoyed this!  Thanks for posting.
Perfect compliment to spicy fish.  Loved it - thanks!

This sauce was excellent! I actually used about 2 oz olive oil mayo to 7 oz fat free greek yogurt. I was making fish tacos and I'm used to having a slaw instead of sauce so I tossed this sauce with a whole bag of sliced cabbage from Trader Joe's and a half a package of broccoli slaw until it was the right consistency. I also threw in a few tablespoons of chopped cilantro because I had some lying around. Absolutely amazing! I'm never making fish tacos (or breakfast tacos) without this slaw again! Thanks for the recipe!
This was great! I left out the capers (personal preference) and had to use ranch dip as I was out of sour cream but it turned out to be a perfect sauce for my spicy fish tacos!
Excellent sauce....made w homemade mayonaise....simply superb!
Great sauce as written, but to knock it up a notch, I added fresh cilantro and jalopeno.
Great basic sauce recipe. I have an egg/dairy allergy and so I substituted Veganaise for mayo and sour cream and it was still quite good.
I've been using this with baked tilapia for fish tacos, but with a bunch of leftover cabbage and some carrots I decided to make coleslaw - this sauce makes an excellent coleslaw dressing too!

I've been making a recipe almost exactly like this for 20 years now. It's supposedly Rick Rubio's original recipe (he introduced fish tacos to the U.S.). The only difference is the recipe uses 1 teaspoon of capers which is more than enough, and there's one to two finely diced habanero peppers which turns this sauce into the best stuff on the planet. Definitely use plain yogurt (not Greek) and not sour cream. I love sour cream but it has no place in this recipe.

I prepared this exactly by the recipe.  I wanted to test it on DH and myself because I was considering giving it as gifts. It is very good.  The spice packets will be included as gifts for Christmas to several of my friends and co-workers.  Thanks GrandmaG!

Just perfect in my book! I made it this morning and put it in two glass jars to use as I need it. There is plenty for two enchilada recipes. I love the combination of flavors and spices. I let it simmer for about 20 minutes to let it reduce in volume some. Thanks, Carole in Orlando

Fast, easy cheap.  It couldn't have cost more than about 30 cents to make enough for two recipes.  I had the time so I simmered it longer, also added a bit of chili powder.  Great money saving recipe that makes the kitchen smell great!
This is a very good sauce. I made it for company and the enchiladas I made with some leftover grilled pork were the first thing gone. It was just the right amount for 2 large pans of enchiladas.

I made enchilada's tonight and used this sauce recipe and it was great. I like that it wasn't spicy. I was sceptical, after it simmered it smelled spicy but tasted great. A wonderful enchilada sauce. Will be makeing again.
Thanks for posting Julesong!

This sauce was excellent. I did not add the butter or sherry as I didn't have any on hand. Also added a chilpotle pepper and a sprinkle of sugar. Poured the left over sauce into a freezer bag and froze flat so I can break off what is needed. Thanks for the recipe!
This turned out pretty well for a quick fix. I didn't have any cider vinegar or dry sherry this time but I think I'll get some for next time.

Cheese enchiladas are quite possibly my favorite food, so for me to say that these were uite possibly the best I have tasted is high praise. I was going to try to just stick to one, but they were so delicious, I had to hold myself back from eating a third.
This was excellent.  I've made it twice now and had it with veggies once and tortilla chips once.  They both go well with it.
My brother has made this several times for family get togethers.   He makes it just like the recipe calls for and all I can say is AWESOME.

This salsa is outstanding!  It took 4 juicey limes to make the 7 TBS and 2 bunches of green onions to fill 1 1/2 cups. I used about 1 1/2 TBS of dried cilantro, which worked perfectly.  I would say this recipe makes closer to 3 1/2 cups of salsa.  Everyone enjoyed it so much!  Thanks for posting, andypandy!
A refreshing change!  My family and friends loved this dip. Great on fajitas or tacos too.  Don't make any changes to this recipe, it's excellent as is. Andypandy, Thanks for sharing this recipe.

Beans, beans, the magical fruit... This made a great side dish to go along with chicken soft tacos. I just used a packet of taco seasoning mix which lended a nice spiced flavor. Yum! I made these as directed and they were a perfect addition to your mexi chicken. I used my own taco seasoning recipe#4292. Thanks for sharing this low carb sidedish :)
Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.  I used your no sugar taco seasoning to make this and served it with your Mexicali Chicken recipe.  So, so very good!!!!!
Did not really care for these...they were kind of bland.  Maybe you just have to REALLY like kidney beans to like this one.  Thanks for sharing, others seem to like.

Thank goodness DH and I REALLY like Kidney beans. These were great as a side dish for your Low Carb Mexi Baked Chicken (recipe #103966). Both of them are keepers in my 5 Star cookbook. I will make this again and again and again.
These were delicious. My entire family loved them. I even substituted an imitation cheddar cheese; my family had no idea :)
When I first started SB this was my lunch for almost a week straight.  It's tasty and the cheese on top makes it feel indulgent!

This dish is delicious and may be my new favorite SB friendly dish.  I also used the homemade taco seasoning recipe. It's nice, and something different to add as a side.  Thanks for the recipe!
Hearty and filling, and quite tasty.  A nice treat on the South Beach Diet, though it would not be recommended for Phase 1, as you are supposed to avoid beans until Phase 2.

Easy and quick!  I skipped the olive oil and just sprayed a non-stick pan with Pam and sauteed my vegetables.  I used chili powder, but next time I think I'll try the taco seasoning.  I love that this is easy to make, low-fat, high-protein and high-fiber, so I will definitely make again!

Very yummy, especially when served with the Low Carb Mexi Bake! Hubby and I really enjoyed it and it will be made again! Thanks!
Very flavorful & Yummy Beans!  Fixed this while on South Beach but whole family loved them.  Had to fix another pot for me to take for leftovers in lunch!  Thank you!

way better than expected. i made the mexi baked chicken to go with it.

This is very good - lots of flavor. It's so heavy and moist, it's almost like a casserole.  It does not lend itself to slicing and toasting.  It's best enjoyed warm.  Thanks for a tasty and satisfying recipe!
