Wonderful! I used my own enchilada sauce, zucchini for the mushrooms & fresh spinach. So easy & healthy; thanks for sharing!

This recipe looked soooooo good!  I was dying to try it and cooked it exactly as written.  However neither DH or I cared for it at all.  We threw away a ton of leftovers.  I'm sorry!  There was wayyyyy too much spinach.  I would cut it in half at least, next time and instead of 1 can beans, I'd add 2.  We used pinto and really liked that part.  There also wasn't enough sauce, and I used a 10oz can.  It came out kind of dry.

this recipe was surprisingly pretty good. i did add a pound of x-lean ground beef with a 6 oz. package of mushrooms and a 16 oz. pack of spinach. insteda of making the sauce i used a large can of roarita enchilada sauce and then just layered the tortillas instead of rolling them. i always try to find the easiest way to make my meals. :) also i used reg extra sharp cheddar. i feel that with it being so good for you the whole fat cheese doesnt hurt too much. also, you can taste the spinach but it wasnt too over powering for us. thank you, we will be making this again.
I love this - you have to be careful to make enough tomato sauce to cover the dish but it turns out splendidly and even my anti-veggie male family members love it.
Great! Only change I made was to use fresh baby spinach rather than frozen, and regular tomato sauce rather than reduced sodium. Very yummy! Thanks for sharing the recipe!
very good.  next time i'm doubling the beans (spinach was just a little too overwhelming), but, it is definitely a keeper.  thanks for posting

These were good tasting but I could not get them as thin as I would like. Maybe the baking powder? I rolled them even thinner than stated and had to peel them from the wax paper I rolled them on but they thickened in the pan. Nice browning and easy rolling. Will try again with less bp to see if I can get them thinner. 

Thanks for a great recipe!

These tortilla's were great fun to make! I wanted to make tortilla's with a tomato sort of flavour...I couldn't find any dried pasta mix so I used 1 tablespoon of tomato paste and 1 tablespoon of italian herbs, added with the flour etc.  I used a scant 1 teaspoon of baking powder.  I'm pretty hopeless with rolling stuff into a circle so I rolled the pieces of dough out as thin as possible and then used a side plate to cut out circles...lol.  I'm so happy with these tortillas...they look fabulous, taste great and really take very little effort.I'm always on the lookout for recipes that don't use artificial colours or flavours..this recipe will be used a lot here.

My first try at making tortillas was a huge success. Thanks, Cheryl. I served these using Knorr Red Bell Pepper Pesto and look forward to trying the other flavors. I served these with Aztec Guacamole recipe #123915 for Dugan's poker party where five hungry men became five angry men after they inhaled them and had none left and I made a double batch. I only used 1 tsp of baking powder because I prefer a very thin tortilla and will use even less next time.
Two words.  Just Divine!

Oh thanks much, I have made tortillas but didn't know how to get the flavorings, this will be terrific & I will also take the advice of Fairy Nuff & add a bit of tomato paste & herbs! Your basic recipe is very similar to one I use with the exception of using canola or olive oil for the fat. Works surprisingly well. Thanks again!

This comes together in a flash & is super easy.  I diluted it a bit w/water because it was a bit zippy for the kids.  I used 'medium' salsa.  I didn't puree in the beginning; I used my immersion blender at the end.  Voila!!  Thanks, Sistah!

This was a very flavorful soup - tangy with a stiff bite.  At first I thought the cumin would be too much so I added less but then tasted and decided to add all of it.  I pureed 3/4 of it in the blender and kept the rest of the beans whole.  Instead of chicken I used vegetable broth and accidentally drained the liquid from one of two 15 ounce cans of beans I used but did not compensate with extra broth.  I also used medium salsa and garnished with red onion and fresh cilantro.  Also, this recipe makes more like 4-6 servings, not 8-10 (and I'm not saying that just because I liked it).  Thanks!
This is so easy and full of flavor!  I've made it a few times now and we'll keep having it.  I have to leave out the red pepper and use mild salsa for the kids.  Thanks for sharing this.
Delicious! I used medium salsa and it had just the right amount of kick to it. Thank you.
We ate this with tortilla chips-soooo good! The serrano pepper really adds some bite, just enough for us northerners. Used white wine vinegar, otherwise followed exactly. Delicious; thanks!
Really good.  Used it as a topping to a taco salad.  Thanks for posting.

I liked this a lot.  We served it with grilled flank steak...yum.  I did make a few modifications to personal taste.  I added the red wine vinegar and then a lot more white wine vinegar (I like vinegar), used red instead of green bell pepper (but next time will use yellow or orange pepper just for color).  I also wanted a little more heat so added the serrano and then a jalepeno we had on hand.  Thanks katie for a great recipe.

I made this without the chili.. we don't handle "hot" very well, but for the rest it was a lovely salad. Green peppers are my least favourite of the green, orange, yellow, red choice, I did use them but next time would use red or yellow for a very slightly sweeter taste.
Next time I might even be brave enough to add some chili, until then please see my rating system, a great 4 stars! Thanks :)

5 bright stars for Katie!   This is a great recipe. Instead of bell peppers and a serrano chili I used a poblano pepper (better known as GW's peppers) and added a couple tablespoons of cilantro.   Served with Mysteryshopper's Empanadas and it was perfect!  Thanks for sharing.

This was one of the best chicken salad recipes I have ever made/had.  The only thing I did different was use fresh jalepenos and added one serrano chili.  I love spicy food.  Thank you for submitting it.

Wonderful, and different from the usual chicken salads--a nice, fresh departure from the "same old". Except for halving it, I followed the recipe as written. Loved the addition of jalapenos.:) Thanks for sharing the recipe!

This is SO DELICIOUS!  Rather than eating it alone, I made four wraps.  I just took four burrito-size tortillas, divided the chicken salad among them and added some chopped romaine lettuce to each one before wrapping them up like a burrito.  They were so yummy.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!
We had no problem at all loving this recipe.  Thanks for posting it Velouria.  I served it in pita pockets, topping shredded cabbage & carrots. An easy 1 dish meal!

Had all the ingredients on hand and decided to give this recipe a go. Maybe due to great reviews, had the expectations high, and this did not live up to them, in our case. Not bad at all, but maybe the combo of celery and jalapeno is what didnt quite work for us...I think.

My husband LOVES jalapenos so any way I can incorporate them into a recipe especially for him, I do.  This was delicious and something we both liked.  I did make sure to really finely chop the red onion and celery because he doesn't normally like the crunch of those (raw) and he loved it.  Thanks so much for posting!

This was delicious!  I sent this with DH for lunch one day and he really raved about it... and he normally dislikes chicken.  The only change I made was leaving out the celery.  I'll definitley make this again.  Thanks Velouria!
This is a wonderful dish.  I get tired of the same-o, same-o chicken salad but this opens up an entire new vista.  It's really good right away but oh so much better the next day.
Great variation on chicken salad.  I omitted the cilantro, because I didn't have any but otherwise followed the recipe as written.

Marvellous! Made it for our Melbourne Cup lunch and it was perfect for a crowd. Maybe heard some whispering about the cilantro/coriander but just ignored it, wouldn't be the same without that dimension :) I'm going to make this again to haveon tostadas like you say, can't wait!
I have made this twice and used it to fill small choux pastries for a crowd.The only change I made was adding more xalapeÃ±os.It was delicous and everyone loved it.
Oh, yum! This is really, really good! I had to use green pepper because it was all I had. I loved it on tostada shells. Delicious! Thanks!
This is wonderful change from traditional chicken salad!  I didn't use celery or red pepper due to family tastes and used yellow onion.  This was great!!  Thanks for sharing!

This is outstanding! I make this all the time. I add chopped roasted almonds and green onions to mine, and I do not add any additional salt. I also use a large can of cooked chicken, for the convenience and fast cleanup. Turns out excellent every time! My whole family loves this on gorditas and corn chips.

My DH loves this, so I make it for his lunch on a regular basis.  To me, the lime juice mixed with the mayo is what makes it so tasty, although I have used lemon juice with good results.  Thanks for sharing this great recipe.
This is the best chicken salad recipe I've tasted. Delish!

Yummy!  My new favorite chicken salad!  I made sure to chop the veggies into very small pieces (I used a Pampered Chef food chopper, which I hardly ever use but works so great when you're chopping a bunch of things).  I was surprised that this wasn't spicy at all, which is nice so you can serve it to non-spice lovers, too.  I served this as a filling to grilled sandwiches, adding some extra slices of jalapeno to mine before grilling...mmmmm!!!  This will be one of my go-to chicken salads.  Thanks!!

Wow, nice variation on chicken salad. I knew it would be good when I read it was from Cook's Country. I love that show and Americas's Test Kitchen. I did use just a little bit less of the jalapenos, but other than that followed the recipe. I will use this recipe a lot as I always have extra chicken or turkey. I will even have the red peppers, jalapenos and cilantro this summer in my garden. Thanks for posting a really nice variation on chicken salad.

This is such a nice alternative to regular chicken salad.  The only change I made was to use 1/2 of a jalapeno, and about 1/2 of a pasilla chile, instead of straight jalapenos because my husband can't handle spicy food.  We ate this salad wrapped up in tortillas with a bit of lettuce.  This was a big hit with all four of my kids... no leftovers!  Definitely a keeper.

This was yummy!  I skipped the cilantro because we don't like it and use parsley instead.  Also I left out the celery.  Next time I will add a bit more jalapeno..  This is going to be even better tomorrow!
Awesome chicken salad.  Substituted diced jalapenos for the jalapeno relish.  Otherwise made as listed.  Will be making this on a regular basis.

I decided to try this becasuse it sounded different and fresh. WOW love the kick of the jalapenos.  I used a yellow bell pepper for added color, and to get all the veggies past the kids I pulsed them alittle to make them confetti like in my mini processor & drained on papertowel to absorb excess liquid before adding. I will use this again and again.

This is a great new way to make chicken salad.  Because of the ingredients on hand, I used green peppers, lemon juice, and chopped pepperoncini instead of jalapenos.  I served them on Hawaiian rolls and the sweetness of the rolls complemented all the flavors of the chicken salad very well!
Easy and tasty recipe.  I made half a recipe and served it on a tostada.  I also served Recipe #136923 as an appetizer.  Quick and easy.

Tried this the other night with leftover roast chicken, and it was delicious!  The jalapenos gave it a nice bite, but not too spicy.  My husband said it was "one of the best, most interesting" things I've made.  I don't know whether to be pleased or pissed! :)  Used lemon juice instead of lime, no celery.  Am trying it with tuna today!

My husband loves chicken salad sandwiches, so I decided to try this recipe today.  He was excited about the addition of jalapenos, and states that it is the best chicken salad he's ever tasted.  I will certainly make this again.  Thanks for posting!
This was pretty good! I used 4 fresh jalapenos from our garden instead of pickled jalapenos. I wish an amount of salt to start with had been listed though...

Yum! Used a fresh jalapeno and it added just enough pop! I kinda melded two recipies into one - the other one was a bit more traditional and had grapes. I was a bit hesitant but the red grapes countered the jalapeno pop with a sweet finish. Will make this again!
I fixed the recipe as written, and it was great. It is good in a roll up, with a little lettus, or with corn chips. My wife even said she loved it, and that is a high indorsement.
My family loved this recipe! We used fresh jalapenos also and served on tostadas. We will be making this one more often!

LOVE it...this was my first time making or even eating chicken salad.  I did follow some comments below and used fresh jalapenos. I also used Olive Oil Mayo hoping to help a little more with our calorie intake...It was wonderful, cant wait to have a picnic and make these for everyone again!!!
Loved this recipe!  I didn't use cilantro (not a fan) but substituted about a 1-1/2 tsps parsley flakes.  Otherwise did the recipe to the letter.  A keeper!
Delicious! Fresh and really flavorful. I loved the bright flavor the lime added and the crunch from the veggies. Thanks for sharing the recipe.
Very nice chicken salad. I enjoyed the bite of the jalapeno very much. May add a little more next time. Thank you for sharing this recipe.
A cool twist on a classic. Next time I might reduce the lime juice a bit as it was a little overpowering. Thank you.

WOW! This is wonderful!!  We've made it twice this week! lol<br/><br/>Changes were minor. I used fat free plain yogurt with just a dollop of full fat mayo. And I didn't have fresh cilantro, so I pre-seasoned the chicken with dry cilantro salt and pepper before cooking it in the pan.<br/><br/>What a great meal. I will definitely be taking this to family get together's this summer. <br/><br/>Thanks!

Great fresh, summer recipe !  I did it exactly as written except that, as many others did, I subtituted finely chopped fresh jalapeno. I had just bought some honey oatmeal bread from a local Mennonite bakery and used it to make a sandwich with this incredibly flavorful chicken salad and it was absolutely delicious !  This is definitely a keeper.
Vivan los champig~nones! To die for stuffed in whole wheat flour tortillas! Used a large pinch of dried epazote. CG has to be cautious with bacon so only used 2 slices. Thanks for posting, Katers.

It’s really special recipes like this that frustrate me the most … not the recipe, but ingredient issues here in Iceland that force me to sub for ideal ingredient choices. 1 sub was my fault when I had only red onion on hand vs white. The manchego cheese & epazote were my true challenges & I subbed for them as you & the recipe advised, but only after an exhaustive grocery store search. So frustrated, I asked the last guy “Where can a girl find some epazote when she needs it for something special?” He looked fearful, leaned toward his wife & said a few words. I think “pervert” may have been among them! The mushrooms made all my frustration worthwhile – they were so good! My DH gave them 5 stars w/an extra thumbs-up to tell me they were worthy of more. Thx for posting.

I`m in the middle of remodeling my kitchen so I had to do something I don`t like to! That is use my microwave for cooking! I don`t use it often but it came in handy for this. I nuked the bacon for 2 minutes added the onions jalapenoes, and nuked for 2 minutes, tossed in the shrooms and spices nuked for 2 minutes. At which point they were still firm no release of liquid. I placed the cheese on and nuked for 1 more minute. This kept the mushrooms more al dente! I was going to make 1/2 the recipe and I`m glad I didn`t because for these would be great in an omelet or and egg wrap for breakfast!!!!
Thanks!!

These are wonderful, really enjoyed them.  They are very easy to make.  I made them just as posted.  Only I was not able to find the epazote and since I'm not a friend of cilantro I left it out.  Great recipe thank you.
This is a nice combination of flavors, although I also did not locate the epazote.  It still was a delicious dish with eggs and tortillas.  Thanks for posting.

This was an interesting twist on meatloaf! Visually it is quite impressive with the different layers in the middle, but it just doesn't seem to work all together. I would suggest adding the ingredients to the meat as well so that the meat is flavorful and does not depend on the "filling" for the flavor. I did not peel my peppers and this made them a bit bitter, so make sure you peel them before adding to the loaf. I used pecans, but would suggest pine nuts or even pistachios for this loaf. Thanks for introducing me to this recipe!

Elmotoo said I could alter the recipe, because the first reviewer pointed out some problems in the recipe. We agreed on this before I made the recipe.

I made an OK/good meatloaf by putting the chile and spice flavors right into the ground meat.  I soaked dried Poblanos in boiled water, then blended them with a small onion and pine nuts.  I fried this up (gets the bitter taste out of the chile skins), added the salt and herbs and also ground chile for the paprika.

It was a good meatloaf, very tasty, but didn't have the rich flavor you would expect from the amount of chile I used.  I liked it, though.
This was good. I added more brown sugar than called for but i like sweet stuff!! I was too lazy to go get the piloncillo cones but will next time!!

I have actually made this many times.  It is a wonderful dessert coffee.  I put the grounds in the coffee basket along with ground cinnamon, pour in the water and allow it to brew as I normally would.  If desired, you can garnish with cinnamon sticks as stirrers.  Thanks for posting!

This is great stuff SISTAH!!!  :))
I love the flavors of cinnamon and brown sugar!!  YUMMY!!
Thank you!!
I first gave this 4 stars--but made it again and have since become addicted.  Once I adjusted for the strong brew I like, I was in heaven.  This will be a standard around here.
I really liked the way this added flavor to my regular roast. Like Chef Kate, I will be making this again! Since we drink strong coffee, I doubled the coffee amount after reading the reviews.

Now this is what coffee should taste like!  I just tried this for my morning coffee today.  It was so easy to make, although I halved the recipe to make only 2 cups of coffee.  I used brown sugar instead of piloncillo.  Thanks for this super-yummy recipe!

This was wonderful! The way coffee should taste. I got some great coffee off of ebay, but never was thrilled with the way it tasted in my coffee maker. This made it turn out perfectly. I too added a bit more coffee and I also added about one to two teaspoons of vanilla which I think really improved the flavor. Thanks so much for posting!
Very good.  Even though you said "not Instant", I used instant coffee anyways. Works for me!

I also used a little more coffee, as we like our coffee strong.
It was a delicious change from my regular after dinner coffee, the cinnamon added a great flavour!

This coffe was very easy to prepare. The flavor was very good. I served it with cookies. 

Thanks Elmotoo.

Bullwinkle.
good stuff
I added the cinnamon stick with the coffee grinds in the coffee drip maker. Added the piloncillo and using this method found no reason to strain.

Yummm, I altered the measurements a *tiny* bit buy using a 3" cinnamon stick in a single serving and i tsp of Splenda Brown Sugar. This is so much better than plain ole coffee. It's a lovely almost Valentines treat. I used a paper coffee filter to strain it and then popped the cinnamon stick back into my cup (after rinsing).
I omitted the sugar and poured this over ice and a bit of milk for an iced coffee and loved the results.
Great recipe, I love coffee, this recipe was yummy!~Thanks

5 Stars, made the recipe exactly as stated, and yielded a weak coffee taste with wonderful cinnamon and brown sugar to make it an enjoyable drink, without the addition of cream.  I was surprised that 3 teaspoons would suffice, but I think that older people in particular would appreciate the mild coffee, and children could drink this as well.  Next time I will make this in my coffeemaker, as it was a pain to sieve the coffee even with a coffee filter.  Made for "I Recommend" based on free-free's review.

Yummy! I like my coffee to not be super strong and very sweet. This was perfect. I did have to use brown sugar, but I'd like to try the piloncillo cones in the future. Made and Reviewed for VegNSwap 5. Thanks! :)

I like my coffee strong so I used the equivalent of  4 heaping teaspoons of coffee and added Splenda brown sugar.  This was still a bit too sweet for me but the co-workers loved it. I did love the cinnamon and the richness the brown sugar added.

This was pretty good. I doubled the coffee, and halved the water. :) I think it needs a bit more cinnamon, but that's just me. I also added a bit of half-and-half. But it's still good without it! I can't wait to try this with a little whipped cream on top, and a sprinkle of cinnamon sugar!

I just LOVE Cafe de la Olla and had no idea it was this easy to make!  The first batch  (of two today!) was made exactly as written. Tonight's batch was made a bit stronger to get more of a coffee taste.  I can tell I'll be making this a lot! Even the DH, who doesn't like what he calls "foo foo coffee", loved this one and wants me to make more tomorrow to serve over ice.  Yum!  Thanks for posting!

I made this for my husband as I do not drink coffee, he is still raving about it. He really enjoyed the hint of cinnamon. Being he is a man who loves his coffee blacker than dirt, I was surprised that he liked the sweetness of this coffee. He did comment that it is more of a dessert coffee vs a get you going in the morning type coffee.
Very refreshing! I made using some plunger coffee and the amount directed on the pack and it had a nice hint of cinnamon without being overly sweet.
Not spicy enough for my tastes but they were good and it was a nice light dinner. I loved the avocado sauce!

This makes a great mug of hot chocolate. I switched the ratios of water and milk, because I was using skim milk (I thought it would be too thin otherwise), but I don't think it was necessary to do so. This is so rich and creamy! Thanks for sharing, Valeria.
Very good and easy to make; my boyfriend and I have it with breakfast on the weekends. I do usually add a little vanilla, though. Thanks for the great recipe.

We really enjoyed these "nachos" or what I usually call a 7-layer dip.  I seasoned the meat with garlic salt, black pepper, cumin, and chili powder. Also, I used medium salsa instead of the taco sauce, and Mexican 4-cheese blend instead of the colby-jack.  We had this for lunch and it was a very filling meal.  Thank you for sharing.
Quick and easy...would love to sneak some salsa into these!!!  Thanks LAURIE

Easy, versatile, tasty. My corn muffin mix was 6.5 oz (Martha White), but I followed your directions and also added 1 diced green onion. I got 6 big, hearty muffins, and paired it with Recipe #142547 on a cold fall night. This is so easy and uses items I keep on hand - will make it again! :)

This makes a very tasty dish. I decided not to mix the rice in, but to serve this over rice, as a sort of stew. I used fresh tomatoes and also fresh green peppers rather than canned chilies. And didn't use any cheese. Made no other changes to ingredients or proportions. It's nice to think that I have enough to freeze for future meals. Thank you very much for sharing this recipe with us.

This was excellent!  I fixed this as a meal for my family and everyone loved it (even the 2 and 4 year old)!  I didn't mix the brown rice in either.  For leftovers, I shredded the chicken and wrapped it, the rice, and some refried beans into whole wheat tortilla's and served with salsa - DELICIOUS!  Thanks for a great recipe I will be making again!
Sorry, but this was just ok.  DH actually requested that I not make it again.  It just seemed to be lacking something in flavor.  Perhaps some chili powder and fresh cilantro would help.
Very tasty and easy to prepare.   The flavor was just right.  I am looking forward to the freezer portions. Thanks for the great recipe.

I loved this--and the color is gorgeous!  I ground the achiote very fine and had no trouble adding it to the oil. Used homemade chicken stock.  Skipped the jalepeno as I was pairing this with PanNan's Ground Sirloin in Adobo Sauce--enough heat there, thank you.
The directions on this recipe are wonderful.  I use a anchiote powder and chicken stock.  This would have been beautiful with fresh cilantro but unfortunately I was out.

I feel kind of guilty reviewing this, because I couldn't fund achiote powder of paste, and I used brown rice instead of white.  We're eating healthy these days, and white rice completely off the menu.  I wasn't sure at all that the cooking method listed in step #1 would work, since it takes twice as long to cook brown rice, so I just par-boiled the brown rice.  And since I couldn't find achiote powder (I went to THREE different stores....and I love in Arizona for pete's sake....it's not like we're unfamiliar with Mexican food!!) So I used New Mexico Chili Powder.  Had a nice kick.....but not "pass-the-fire-extinguisher-hot,"  thank goodness.  I really liked the technique of adding the par-boiled rice to the onions and chili powder  and then adding the chicken broth.  It produced a rice that had a great texture (not SMUSHY) and had a great flavor.  My father (a fussy cook and an eaven fussier eater) hovered over my shoulder watching, and was quite intrigued and pronounced the finished product, "better than restaurant quality".....quite a compliment, Cookgirl!
Great side! Nice wonderful flavor from the onion, garlic and annato. I added about a teaspoon of salt to this. Thanks for a great recipe cookie!

Oh my *this* is good rice! I happened upon achiote powder while browsing one day and have now found a way to use it! DH usually won't touch rice in any shape, form or fashion and he ate half of this - _mmmmmming_ all the while. I made a helluva mess in my kitchen but it's worth having a few red wooden spoons! The only boo-boo I made was to add the jalapeno in with the onion and garlic and even that was a pretty good move. This will defintely be reappearing on my menu! Thanks for posting!
This is a really good, quick rice recipe.  I made it for Cinco de Mayo with the recipezaar Picadillo recipe and it was delish.  Very tasty and easy.

I LOVED making this today!<br/>For Cinco de Mayo, it provided a bit of Ole!<br/>I used homemade chicken stock, added chili and lime zest too!<br/>It was the perfect compliment to Pil Pibil...Thank you! WHOO HOO!
Used to eat this in Jr. High and loved it!!  One of the things I miss about eating meat.  We used Doritos or Fritos.  Both are good.
We used to make these at summer camp, but we called them Walking Tacos, hehe.
amazing

I took these on a camping trip with my son's cub scout pack.  All the adults and kids LOVED them.  Instead of using Doritos, I bought a few large bags of tortilla chips and divided them into quart size ziploc bags.  I precooked the meat before we left so all I had to do was reheat it for about 10 minutes and lunch was ready!  I was asked to keep this as a staple on the camping menus.

I am not a fan of Velveeta, so substituted grated cheddar for the Velveeta. This was very good, the chili powder making this a nice twist on macaroni-and-cheese with chicken added. Good, easy one-dish supper.

The directions on this kept making me nervous... I thought the chicken would stick due to the lack of oil. It did, but when I added the chicken broth I was able to deglaze all the important stuff. I also wasn't sure that the noodles would cook well enough in the time stated, but they turned out just fine. I wasn't sure whether to slice the veggies (like fajitas) or chop them, so I sliced the peppers and chopped the onions for my onion-complainers. Overall, this turned out pretty well.

I was making chicken fajitas and didn't have tortillas, so I quick checked recipezaar and found this recipe.  I had cooked the chicken with fajita seasoning,one sliced green pepper and dry onion so I just threw in the noodles, broth and a package of shredded sharp cheddar, simmered and it was great!  My kids loved it too!

Good quick fix that everyone ate and enjoyed. Was better not served right away, allowed it to thicken up. Was in a hurry so used frozen chopped onions and two cups of frozen chopped bell peppers which worked well. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

This made a nice lunch that took five minutes to assemble.  I used green salsa verde for a change.I like how the tortillas get crispy edges but the middle is still soft. 

Roxygirl

this is  nice for a fast lunch  used pace salsa  still turned out good    and put some shredded lettace on top aftrer coming out of oven  go to her site it  is wonderful  she has alot of cookbooks   thanks for posting dee

This is so good. My only problem was that it was hard to eat - it was so messy - everything kept falling off.  But in my book, messy is always great! I didn't have enough cheddar for this, so I halved the tortilla, and used cheddar on one half and made it as directed. The other half I used monterey jack.  Both were so good.  Maybe next time I'll add a little diced tomato and a dollop of sour cream.  Great recipe echo, thanks for sharing.

These are so easy to put together and takes no time at all to have a great meal! I used pinto beans instead of black beans and left off the green chilies for DH. The tortillas get a little crispy while in the oven and the flavor of these little pizza's is wonderful! I will use finely shredded cheese next time as the thicker shredded cheese does not melt as nicely. This will be made again soon!
This is so easy.  I took the ingredients to work and just made zapped it in the microwave instead of in the oven - works very nicely.  Thanks!
Easy, quick, delicious -> a winner! Thanks for sharing!

Quick and tasty, which is just what I needed on a busy Thursday night when DH worked late.I used some leftover fat-free refried beans, spread on a spinach tortilla, then salsa, then a Mexi-blend cheese. I topped with a dollop of sour cream and a bit of hot sauce.

Yum.  An easy lunch for me this past weekend. I used two small low carb tortillas but the same amount of topping.  I used refried beans and a little less 2% cheese.  Plus some good salsa we get at Sam's Club.  A healthy and quick lunch!

I made this exactly as written and it was very yummy!  The hubby added jalapenos to his and he was a big fan also!  We had these alongside a bowl of tortilla soup and it was a wonderful combination.  I loved the way the edges of the pizza got crisp but the center stayed soft.  You can bet your boots that we'll have these again, thanks so much for posting your recipe :)
I made this with beef and the meat was very flavorful and easy to make.  I'll be making this again but doubling it so there will be some left over to freeze.

Very tasty and this was perfect for soft tacos as well as enchiladas.

Will definitely use this recipe again.

When making Chime Changas, for a Tex-Mex flavor, I also add about 1 cup ( two 4-oz cans) of Hatch green chiles to the mixture before cooking the liquid down. After liquid has reduces, add a few cups of cooked pinto, or black, beans to meat mixture, stiring to mix ingredients, reheat.

Then, AFTER Chimes are stuffed and rolled as written above, I put a small amount of water into a bowl. You can also use an 'egg wash' by placing an egg into a small bowl. Add a couple of tablespoons of milk, beating mixture with fork, or wisk, until well beaten.

Using a pastry brush, brush the entire end of the tortilla liberally with the liquid, including any folded over side edges. This method SEALS the end of the Chimi, removing the possibility of the burrito opening up during the frying process. 

Place the burrito on a long platter, seam-side DOWN, and let rest. Repeat these steps until all burritos are made. 

Pour oil into large skillet until it is about 1-1/2 to 2-inches deep. Heat oil on medium-high heat. Test frying readiness by dipping fingers into a bowl of water and 'flicking' fingers over oil. If oil sizzles and pops, then oil is ready for frying. Do NOT let oil heat to the 'smoking'stage as this is TOO hot for frying the burritos.

Starting with the first sealed burrito, gently place it into the oil, seam-side down. Place more burriros into oil leaving space between each burrito for turning over. Fry until bottom side is golden brown. With metal tongs gently flip the burrito over and fry the other side until golden brown. Take fried burritos out of oil and place each of them onto a cookie sheet that has a metal cooling rack in it. If you do not have a cooling rack, drain Chimis on paper towels.

Top the Chimis with desired toppings. Serve with refried beans and Mexican rice.

~munchkin Mama.  You probably didnt turn the stove to simmer the rice.  When cooking rice you bring it to a hard boil, then reduce to simmer and cover. I omitted both sun-dried tomato and cilantro and it's still pretty good! Instead of grilling and pre-cooking the bacon I baked the thing in the oven at 450F for 10-15 mins. I left few seeds in the Jalapeno and man it was HOT! (my Jalapeno peppers are small to medium sizes) So next time I make this dish I probably will clean the seed out completely. I made a small trial batch using 4 ounces cream cheese and that filled up 7 Jalapeno peppers so I definitely needed a lot less cream cheese filling than the recipe called for. I also used only half a strip of bacon to wrap each and it turned out fine.
love these!!!  soooo yummers!

These are fabulous!  I cheated and used a mixture of herb and garlic and sun dried tomatoe cream cheese for the filling.  I also added some green onion.  I grilled these on the bbq and they went so fast I didn't even get one so of course I had to make them again the next night and I had to fight everyone off just to get one!  Thank you soooo much.  I will be making these again and again!
great recipe! had them at a football bbq, everyone loved them!
I agree, wear gloves, but also use an apple corer or strawberry corer depending on the size of your peppers to reove the stem and aloot of the seeds. These are great for crowd pleasers.

These spread like wildfire! They are always requested at special events now. They taste amazing, we have done them in the oven, on the bbq, used flavored cream cheese, or just plain. You just can't go wrong! Thanks for a great recipe!

Wow...these are good.  I made 20 of them, and my hubby and I almost ate them all, and I ate another one cold for a snack this afternoon and it was just as good cold!  I used the preparation as given, and although it took a little practice, it wasn't that hard, and so worth it.  I have made these cut in half and it is so much better with whole jalapenos.  If you don't like hot make sure you get all of the seeds out!  I didn't have all of the ingredients on hand, so I used the cream cheese and added 3 t. of cajun seasoning, which was great.  I will try the as posted recipe next time.  Thanks Tasmith!

What I liked with this one was the addition of sun-dried tomatoes.  I used the dry kind so I soaked them in hot-water before chopping into cheese mixture. Originally I found this recipe c/o 444031.  They are almost the same recipe with exception of the garlic powder vs garlic cloves & the addition of salt (which I find is not necessary anyhow due to the sun-dried tomatoes).  For the bacon, I recommend precooking the slices as mentioned.  I used ? slice (sliced lengthwise) per pepper half.  Great recipe, thanks for sharing.
these were great, added the cheddar cheese to them and cut out some cream cheese, they were all gone in a few minutes

These were great!  I also cut the cream cheese with some grated just because family does not like heavy cream cheese flavor.  Actually now I have a question....I froze my jalapenos from our garden.  They are whole and I now want to use some for this recipe.  Is it likely to work?  I don't want to waste our peppers.
Nice mix of ingredients. I cored and stuffed mine then smoked them at 225F for 2 hours.
Last evening, Sister #2 missed out.  I called her and asked if she wanted to stop by for hors d'oeuvres and a cocktail.  She hemmed and hawed so long, I suggested emailing it to her.

I did 1/4 recipe using just ground turkey which I made into a 6 muffin tin.  Putting a sprinkle of moz cheese in the middle while filling the tin.  Plate licking good!  Omitted green chile using red bell pepper, chopped onion and a pinch of red pepper flakes.  Spooning the salsa on top the last 5 minutes of baking at 350 for 50 minutes.  So good!
Quick & easy lunch that hit the spot!  We always have tortillas on hand, so will remember this one!  Thank you, sweet girl!

i love the "border" chili cheese burritos and often do these, with leftover homemade chili or a caned one.....and always put sour cream

it is nice to see a recipe out here for it
I loved these at the "border" restaurant, but ours quit serving them years ago. I made my own recipe for this with homemade chili.  I love it.  I am glad you posted a recipe for this.

My husband and I love this dish!  We would give it 10 stars if possible.  I made two small changes - instead of 2 types of cheeses I just used a mexican blend and instead of 2% milk I used skim.  It tastes awesome you you would have no idea its a "light" recipe.  The cilantro/tomatillo sauce thickens up to the perfect consistency and the inside of each enchilada is moist and delicious. At first I was a little concerned as i mixed up the tomatillo sauce since I've never made enchiladas with a green sauce but I am very glad i tried it!

Love this recipe!  The chicken for the filling comes out so yummy.  I've made this recipe many times.  I actually chop the onion from the cooking process in the filling.  Adds to the moistness of the filling.  Thanks for a great recipe!

This really was quick and easy.  I added one minced serrano chile to the sliced peppers to give it some more heat.  My soup mix packet was 1 oz, so I wasn't sure I was using the right ingredient.  These were very tasty with the bonus that they're healthy, and did I say FAST and EASY?

While it was very easy, it was quite cloying with the cheese and then yogurt on top.  Husband and daughter did not enjoy it, I'm afraid.  I do like the easy yogurt sauce and can re-used that simple idea in other recipies.
I really liked this recipe. Made it for a Colts televised game and it was a hit. The cilantro/yogurt added a nice bite to the dish. Watch the oven time, do not overbake.

Very tasty recipe. I only used a yellow pepper and an onion. For the chicken I used leftovers from a store made rotisserie chicken and added BBQ to it. I spread the ranch/bbq mixture on half and then used the remainder for dipping. Great easy recipe to use up some leftovers!
Have tried this and it turned out well.

Had these last night.  I did it a little different.  I put 4 large chicken breasts and 1 jar of salsa in the crock-pot and let it cook all day while at work. I did not add water.  I shredded the chicken w/2 forks that night and we had chicken taco's.  Really easy.  Added shredded cheese, lettuce, sour cream and hot peppers on soft wrap.  Turned out great.

What an awesome idea to use up leftovers. I often have leftover chicken meat and almost always an open jar of salsa that needs to be used up. Thank you so much for sharing this tasty recipe with us. Thank you.

Easy, yes indeed.  Had leftover thighs and legs from a rotisserie chicken and was looking for a recipe to use them up!  I used a medium salsa and still thought it was a bit bland when cooked, so I would add a tsp of taco seasoning next time.  Thanks for posting this recipe!  UPDATE:  We had some leftovers so I used it for taco salads, serving the meat atop a bed of lettuce, corn, and black olives, topped with a little more salsa and sour cream.  The taco meat worked well for this purpose!
I have been making this chicken for years now. I usually shredded a Costco rotisserie chicken and add a small can of Hernandez salsa. It is so good! The next day it is even better.

I knew DH and I would absolutely love this recipe and I was correct.  It is so easy to prepare.  I made 1/2 of the recipe, using sour cream and did not use the guacamole.  This was a delicious simple dinner for us tonight!  DH commented several times on how much he liked these!  Thanks Karen!

These were fabulous! The only reason for the absent 5th star is that here was no time given for how long to broil the poblano peppers for.  They were reallt flavorful and definitely worth the time! Thanks!!

These were quite tasty.   Instead of using raw pork, I cubed leftover pork loin roast and slow cooked it in this sauce for 4 hours until it began to fall apart.  I used Recipe #42094 for the enchilada sauce.  In addition to being a great recipe on it's own, it is also definitely a great way to use up left over pork.

Great recipe Teresa! My girlfriend loved it and so did I. The store I went to didn't have fresh poblano chilies, so I used the diced green fire roasted chilies in the can and it worked really well. I will make this one again. The sour cream and cilantro is a MUST finishing touch.

Wonderful for leftovers, I had previously made a Boston butt roast using a combination recipe of Kittencal's "Dry Rub for ribs, pork shoulder, and boston butt" and her "Fall-apart Tender slow Roast pork butt" recipes, then froze the leftover pulled pork. This recipe fit the bill for use, although I did make a couple changes. I added 1 4.5 oz can of chopped green chiles, 1 fresh diced jalapeno, substituted tomato sauce for fresh tomato, and added enchilada sauce to the filling mixture as well as the top. Had a very nice flavor, I'm not sure DH even knew he was eating pork! Thank you!

Wow!  This recipe is definately a keeper.  Well worth the extra effort and I am so looking forward to having the leftoevers today.  Me and my family all loved it.  I made a few small changes . . . used the medium verdi (green) enchilada sauce, the large green chilis because the store did not have poblano chiles and a yellow onion because that is what I had.  I can not wait to use this for a dinner party.  It is definately worth the 5 Stars.  Thanks
interesting good hot or cold

DELISH!!  OMG....This was so wonderful!  Had this for my Sunday coffee -- mixed with some milk -- buy OH MY!  The flavors were wonderful and it was so easy to make!  It's a new favorite for me -- that's for sure!  And the orange juice?  Added a subtle dimension that really, really complimented the coffee.  Thanks Lee!

Wonderful flavored coffee! Just the right balance of spices with a hint of orange. Easy, low calorie and made from ingredients always on hand. Added some vailla soy milk which was perfect. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

This reminds me of one of those International coffees :))
It is delicious!!  Thank you!!  Now I want to try it cold!
Just loved this!
Well, Dh gobbled this up while I just found it strange.  Must be my taste buds lately so I'm not rating it.  I made no changes.

Wow, fusion cuisine at its best as far as I'm concerned.  BF and I both rated 5 stars at least.  I'm putting this into my keepers cookbook.  I used soy sauce, asafetida, salsa, whole wheat tortillas and less oil on a non-stick skillet.  Truly fantastic.  Definitely Indian, Italian and Mexican components here.  Not strange at all to me, just good!  Thanks Sharon!
I thought this was very good!  I don't eat red meat so I used ground turkey instead.  Thanks for the recipe! :-)

This was really good, and a big hit with my family! I left out the beans because we don't like them and was worried that the pie wouldn't be substantial enough, but we didn't miss them! This dish was plenty filling and tasty, though I think next time I'll use taco sauce instead of salsa because my family (everyone's so picky!) didn't like the chunks of peppers and such. Thanks for another great, easy recipe!

My kids love this recipe as a movie snack, but instead of refried bean I cook beef mince with grated onion, carrots and brocolli stem,(removing the tough outer skin before grating). They have no idea that there junk food is so good for them.
This was a lot milder than I'd expected.  Next time I'll use real garlic instead of garlic powder.  Also it would be a good idea to poke holes in the chicken so the marinade really gets in there.
We added cilantro to the marinade.  This chicken turned out nice and juicy.  I would have liked a little more zest.  so next time I will add garlic.
Loved it just as is. Used chicken thighs and a very hot pan. The marinade is just enough liquid to make a little camrelization during the last minute or so of cooking. Kids loved it too. Thanks!

This worked really well for my family. The only thing I did different was I used a couple cloves of pressed garlic instead of the garlic powder. I cooked the chicken on the grill and it came out nice and juicy. The kids REALLY liked it. Very simple and inexpensive. Thanks Charmie!

Very nice! I needed some chicken for tacos, and this worked great. I forgot to start the chicken early enough to marinade, so instead I poached the chicken in the marinade in the microwave. It came out moist and flavorful and was a delicious addition to black bean tacos! Thanks, Charmie777!

I LOVE this chicken!!!I used it for filling your taquitos recipe but also put it in tortillas and made burritos with it. It is OMG good! Everyone raved over it! Wonderful flavors! Excellent on the grill! This is one of our favorites on Zaar!

Just the right amount of spices and citrus.  I grilled the chicken and paired it with mexican rice and beans.  We really enjoyed this because it was so flavorful but yet not so spicy my son would frown upon the kitchen.  The chicken was also incredibly moist.  I am planning on using this chicken in soup and tacos in the future.
This was OK.  I think next time I'll add beer and tequila to make it a little more tender.

oh im excited now.  I made just a small amount over the weekend, halving the recipe -well the chicken, i left the marinade the same - and will be picking up a couple of pounds to cook and then freeze so i always have it available

This is easy and tastes fantastic!  My chicken quarters came out with a nice crispy, tasty skin cooked in the rotisserie.  I've already made this several times in the last two weeks and am making it again today.  My sister loved it too and demanded I send her the recipe!  Thanks!

As suggested by other reviewers, I also used garlic cloves for this and loved the flavor.  My son kept asking for more and he's usually not much of a meat eater.  The only change I'll make for next time is maybe to decrease the salt--my feet were swollen last night!  Thanks for a keeper.

This was so wondeful!  I used 4 chicken breast cut into 3rds and pounded.  I added 1 tsp of cumin, because it's just not Mexican without lots of cumin.  I used fresh garlic and it marinated for 2 hours.  We grilled it and had it as a salad.  We LOVED it and will be making it again!  Thanks!

I made this four our Mexican Themed Father's Day BBQ and it was delicious! I used bone in/skin on thighs and put the in the marinade the day before. Either the fat from the chicken or the oil, or both made the grill flame like crazy and the skin was pretty dark, but it was SOOO good like that. We will have this again for sure!
Great marinade.  Skipped the oil.
i didn't get a chance to marinade the full 2 hours, but it came out pretty good anyway. not too spicy, even my picky 4yr old liked it.
This is wonderful plain! I served along with a salad and loved the chili lime combination.
Delicious!  The marinade really gets into the meat.  I added cumin as well.  Definitely will use this recipe again!

This passed the test of my picky 8 year old who insists she does not like chicken - she had seconds! This was very tasty. I did add a little cumin, as others had done. We'll definitely be making this again! I think I'll try it as a fajita marinade!
Fantastic flavor, and the kids gobbled it down like there was no tomorrow.

Another 5 star from me!  I added cumin as well and also a handful of cilantro.  Found out last minute we were out of lighter fluid for the grill so I ended up doing my chicken tenders under the broiler.  They were delicious and so easy.  The only thing was because of all the lime juice, I only let it marinate for 45 minutes because the citrus started cooking the chicken and I'm not sure if that is safe or not?  Anyways it was a great recipe.  Oh I added some black pepper to the mix as well.  Served over my own cilantro lime mexican rice and topped after cooking with homemade pico de gallo.  Tasty and easy.
This was really good, and not at all too spicy (my hubby is a bit delicate with spices, lol).  The tang was a nice change from the usual, and we both enjoyed it.  Thanks for sharing!
This makes very good chicken.  I used it to marinate some chicken tenders that I am using to eat along a tossed salad.  Wonderful seasoning............makes the salad seem special!!

The best kind of recipe ~ easy and delicious. I've made this three times now and it was great each time. For me, the best part of this is that the meat doesn't have to marinate forever to taste great. Each time, I marinated for between one and three hours and the meat was juicy and flavorful each time. This is my go-to recipe for chicken. Thanks for posting!

Incredibly simple, tender and the perfect flavor! We didn't use pieces. We doubled the recipe and butterflied a whole chicken. Will definitely be making this again. It's on our "must-make-this-again" list. Thanks much to the original poster :)

In-credible. Very simple and very tasty. I cut the back out of a roaster and used a double recipe. Had to get a little creative with foil to keep the wings from burning, but it was worth the effort. This is going in the use often section. Thanks for sharing.
I'm surprised I haven't rated this yet!  We've been using this marinade for at least a year now, and we LOVE it!  Great on the grill, great in the oven - it's our go-to marinade for chicken.
Awesome! So simple and taste is addictive!!!!!
This was really, really yummy, although I do wish I'd cut the chilli back a little hahhaaha.
So, so, so good! Chicken was so tender and flavorful. Great served with cilantro-lime rice!
Very good! We cut into strips and made into tacos and everybody loved them. Thanks!
These turned out soooo good, they were moist and such good flavor done on the Kamado Joe.  Loved them with our Mexican kale salad.
So wonderful! Made this with 2 chicken breasts and halved the recipe. Marinated for just over 2 hours and it tasted so good. I think next time I will cut it up and eat as a taco/burrito.

Ok, this is so far the best marinated grilled chicken I've ever made! I only got about 3 hours marinating time and my chicken just sucked up so much flavor! It was tangy and delicious. Will be using this marinade for a long time :)
Really enjoyed this and so easy to prepare.
This marinade was so easy. We marinated large bone-in chicken breasts for two hours and then grilled on low heat for 40 minutes. Just delicious! Thank you for a wonderful and easy recipe.
This was so good and flavorful and I didn’t have time to marinate. Still was yummy next time I will marinate ??
Nice variety of flavors so enjoyed this marinated meat.

My hubby said give it a 4 or 4 1/2, so I'm giving this a 5, since I deviated from the original recipe and made it a main dish instead of an appetizer!  In honor of the 1st of May I decided to make this to get ready for Cinco de Mayo, but only had boneless skinless chicken breasts.  Because of this, I'm sure it was not nearly as good as using wings and took longer to make.  Adding the lemon-lime soda was the thing that made this a step above other spicy wings.  I'd go easier on the sprinkled red pepper flakes next time (I didn't measure!) and would add the green onion halfway through the browning phase, so they wouldn't crisp up.  As a main course, we really liked putting some leftover sauce on the rice I made using chicken broth.  On Cinco de Mayo I'm going to use what I was supposed to use (chicken wings) and will bring to a party as an appetizer which I'm sure people will find differemnt and tasty...

I did not have the Old El Paso Brand items, but if the flavors were different, these were still very good. As the other reviewer said, I thought the addition of 7-Up was the key to making this different from other chicken wing appetizers. I'm glad I doubled the recipe so I could freeze the remaining wings to pass around on Cinco de Mayo!

Awesome potatoes!  I knew when I read this recipe that it would be perfect for me.  I put a little shredded cheese on top, too.  I think these would be good with or without the crumbled bacon.  Thanx for a great baked potato!  I'll make these again.

A very good and quick weeknight meal. I like to add a little hot sauce and lime to my guacamole, so did that here too, and it was great that way. You could definitely do this up and add more things as well (cheese, tomatoes, cilantro, etc.), though we didn't.

Absolutely delicious!  I would give this more stars if I could because of how easy and the fact that I always have these ingredients on hand.  I used pre-cooked chicken and Old El Paso grren enchilada sauce.  A great quick weeknight meal that is much better than going out to a mexican restaurant!  Thanks Amy!

We have two nopal plants in the backyard and after serving them grilled w/ salt, cooked in salsas, and fried with eggs, I was out of ideas. I tried this recipe and as-is, my husband loved them. I made mine without ham, and they were great too! Thank you for a recipe that made me look extra creative!
Easy and delicious! I made these to go with coffee this morning and they were devoured! Thank you!
These were so easy and so good! In my hometown, the fast-food mexican restaurant called these "crustos"...but no matter what you call them, they are delicious!! Thanks for posting this recipe!
This is really easy and good. I will be making this again. Thank you for a Great recipe.
This was easy to make and sooo tasty. I will definitely make it again. I just ate it plain without sauce. It would be great with leftover spaghetti or marinara sauce.

Dear Daughter (11 y.o.) made these for our lunch today, and I must say, we made pigs of ourselves!  Ymmm!  She heated the sauce in the microwave--which went very slick.  

I think next time, we'll use some pre-cooked sausage crumbles for a different taste!  

Definitely a KEEPER-recipe!

This is a winner!  I added these to my appetizer buffet and should have tripled the recipe.  Everyone kept asking "Where are those little pizza sandwich thingys?"  when they were gone.  Excellent!  They were a tiny bit hard to turn in the pan (without losing the stuffing), so if you add just a touch of mozz over the oregano the melted cheese helps the top tortilla stick when you flip it.

Very delicious.   Instead of dipping into tomato sauce, we just spread it right IN the quesadilla.

We think this should be for four servings---unless it's a main dish.

Also great as an afternoon snack (using the leftovers from lunch!).  

This is a KEEPER!
I love these! I use whole wheat carb balance tortillas and turkey pepperoni with lots of veggies. Yummy!

I could eat this soup every day.Very delicious but light to eat.
And a very balanced meal.
such an easy soup such a great flavor. It is truely a great soup because u can add different toppings to make it ur own. LOVE it.

I made the recipe with the amounts and ingredients as posted.  I only changed the prep method.  I browned the beef, onion and garlic until done.  Then I added all the other ingredients and put it in my 12 quart Nesco (I doubled the batch) and let it cook for 4 hours.  The double batch made at least 10 quarts of soup.  It was SOOOOOO GOOD.  I will definately make this one again.  Thank you for sharing your recipe.  I also submitted 2 photo's.
This is a great soup.  wow

I had leftover grilled flat iron steak, so I used this recipe as a base for my soup. Here's what I did. My meat was already cooked, so I browned the pepper (I used Green & red) & onion. I added the garlic (used granuales) I then added the tomatoes, chili powder, & cumin. I left out the fajita seasoning because my meat was already grilled with a smokey grill spice. I added beef broth and I used a frozen corn & black bean fiesta mix. I left out the pintos, spinach, and jalapenos. Everyone loved it.
This was very good! I made my own taco seasoning using Taco Seasoning. Also used 8 oz light Velveeta so it was a little more cheesy (yum!) Very simple and fast recipe. Thanks ladypit!
loved this, so simple, so quick, so tasty... for a lunch I added tuna.. fantastic!
This was so easy to make. I made up a double batch and it disappeared fast. We really enjoyed this low-fat dish and will make it again. Nick's Mom

Awesome mac and cheese! I used corkscrew pasta for this dish and it turned out very nice. Lots of flavor with the taco seasoning and  homemade salsa. Very easy to make and fast as well. I used 8 ounces of light velveeta cheese. Made for "low in" or "Free of" challenge in the photo forum. Thanks Ladypit for another fantasic recipe.
Quick and easy and very tasty. Thanks for sharing. Another keeper...
This was very quick and easy and the taste of the salsa and seasoning was a nice addition, but we next time I may try adding in a few handfuls of shredded cheese just to get a cheesier texture.

We made as directed except I only added salsa and taco seasoning to half. I added the full amounts though, and it was a bit too spicy for me. I did use medium salsa and free handed taco seasoning spices, so that's probably on me. Also, we served as a main dish, so I got four servings. I made ours with whole wheat rotini and 5 oz of light Velveeta.  The nutrional information does not include the cheese, so I figured the calorie info on fitday.com. According to that site, the recipe has 442 calories per serving, 5.3 grams of fat, 82.3 grams of Carbs, and 22.7 grams of protein. (2 cups whole wheat pasta, 1/4 cup salsa, and 1.25 oz light Velveeta). We will definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing!

Lovely cake; I used a smaller can of evaporated milk (all I had) and it was plenty.
For the topping I mixed 8oz of whipped topping with 1 box of vanilla pudding mixed with 3/4 cup milk. Will certainly make this regularly. Thank you for posting.
This was wonderful. It seems like you have to much liquid when pouring it over the cake, but suprisingly, it all does get absorbed. I toped the cake with berries and a spoonful of whip cream.

This was really tasty!  However, I did have some problems.  I followed the cake recipe to a T.  At 34 minutes, the cake was an inch taller than my pan and still liquid in the middle.  I cooked it an additional 15 minutes before the center was done.  As the cake cooled, it shrunk to the height of my 9x13 pan, but the edges were slightly overdone.  I'm wondering if this is due to all the cake mixes alreading having pudding in them...maybe it's too much pudding with the addition of the mix.  I followed recipezaar's substitution of  3/4 cup milk mixed with 1/3 cup of butter for the heavy cream.  I don't think I'll ever do that again.  It left tiny dots of butter everywhere, spend the money and get the heavy cream.  I also couldn't get all the liquid absorbed...it solidified, but didn't all absorb in to the cake.  That said, it did taste excellent and I will definitely make it again.

I decided to make two of theses cakes for Thanksgiving dessert, just to have another option besides all of the pies. I used a french vanilla cake mix in place of the yellow. I used 2% milk instead of whole milk.  I also made one of the cakes with banana creme pudding flavor and the other with vanilla. Everybody loved both, but the banana was gone much faster. Everybody thought it tasted like nilla wafer banana tres leches cake... My sister has also made this recipe the way that it is shown, and with yellow cake mix it had  a thicker (almost egg like) taste. The french vanilla cake mix was lighter in color and also i thought i could taste more of the milks (which was creamier, not heavier) I also used coconut extract in place of the vanilla! wonderful...I would definetly make this again and i think it would be fun to try with different types of pudding just for something different. I did agree with the previous comment about the time. I cooked the cakes individually and cooked them for 45 min before they were done all the way through. All liquid absorbed into the cake just fine. I used only cool whip for topping...

This is my favorite tres leches cake I have tried! I love the shortcut of using the cake mix, and no one can ever tell! I used french vanilla cake mix as was suggested by another user and preferred that to white or yellow cake (I've made it all 3 ways). I used a teaspoon of rum extract in the filling and it is much better with it than without. Used a large tub of cool whip on top on which I put caramel sauce in lines across the cake and pulled a knife through to create a feathered pattern. I make this cake to celebrate a coworkers birthday, All of the men (even ones that don't like sweets) LOVE this cake, it seems to be a guy thing lol!

I don't know what happened here, but I suspect this queso needs a stronger cheese. I used sharp cheddar and everything else exactly as indicated, but the flavor was almost completely absent. Perhaps EXTRA-sharp cheddar would help. Got this recipe from the Food Network and made it with Emeril's chili.
This queso was a hit at our Mexican feast. I used extra-sharp cheddar and colby. Smooth and creamy. I added a few chopped jalapenos. Yummy!
Forgot to rate this!  I made this in my last oamc plan. Very tasty fajitas and work great to freeze in the marinade ahead of time.  This has been added to my regular rotation.  Yum!
Delicious!  And so easy - I used the jalapenos, but skipped the onions.  Like JillAZ, I also used as an OAMC recipe.  I'm going to be making this often.
The beef was so tuff and unflavored and bland how can you add hot spices and still have a bland dish? My kids refused to eat it.

This is sooo good, and I am not sure why I didnt rate this before today!  We had this weeks ago, and it was perfect.  I had my chicken a little frozen as it suggested, and it helped immensely to cut it.  I was a little worried about the chunks of chicken being too big, but it turned out great!  Thanks for a great recipe Dee!  I hope all is well with you!

This dish was wonderful.  My family loved it.  Next time I make it though I will have to grease the pan because for some reason the chips stuck to the pan, but oh well, we just added more.  I can't wait for our next potluck because I will take this dish for sure. Oh and sour cream goes really well with it.  Thanks for posting!!

This was really good.  I was really unsure of how this combination of ingredients would turn out but was pleasantly surprised.  It went very well together.  I followed the recipe to the letter except left out the seasoning salt.  Thanks twissis.
Very popular with our lunch guests. Took only moments to buzz it up in the food processor. Used the salt, lime juice and medium-strength salsa, and served with raw vegetables and cooked prawns.

I wasn't sure how well I would like this with the shrimp in it but was very pleased with the taste and texture.  I even had some ask for the recipe after trying it.  Congrats on the 2010 Conference title football win!
Excellent! Extremely easy to make as well. Thoroughly enjoyed it, and will defintely be making it again. Thanks for posting the recipe.

This was very easy. I made a few minor variations.  I only had canned mushrooms, so didn't use fresh.  I cut back on the salsa, for personal preference. And at the end, I didn't stir in the cheese....I sprinkled it on top.  I really liked how quick and easy it was to prepare. Thanks SuperSpike

Totally awesome; I made it tonight and it came out absolutely perfect.  I couldn't find any yellow rice, so I used Rice-a-Roni's Mexican Rice and I couldn't find button mushrooms, so I used regular.  I like following recipes to the letter, but I am beginning to understand it's not always possible.  The cheese made it taste even better.  I didn't use the cayenne, as I used Pace Hot Salsa.

This was really good! I think next time I will leave out the chicken stock because I added a little and the consistency was pretty runny. I'm pretty sure I didn't need to use the chicken stock. But thanks for a great recipe that I'm sure I'll be using again!
Did everything the way I was supposed to.  Wasn't too hard to make and came out tasting great!  Thanks for the recipe, I will be making it again in the future.
Love it!  So simple, so filling, so tasty!  I leave out the mushrooms cause i dont like them but sometimes add in some sweetcorn for some crunch.
Wow...my hubby loved this one! Easy and tasty! Thank you!
Loved this!  So easy to make!  I used brown rice, only needed about 1/2 cup of chicken stock.  Hubby loved it too!  Thanks for a super recipe!
My husband loved it. I used short grain brown rice, and all of the stock, it took longer but the end results were great!!

I was apprehensive about trying this for some reason but it turned out quite good.  I used a mild, thick chunky salsa from a local business and basmati rice.  I only needed to add one cup of chicken stock.  I did double the garlic and probably added about 1/2 teaspoon extra of cumin and cayenne.  I would like to try this with brown rice next time and perhaps with some chopped green pepper.  Thanks for posting!

No stars because of the substitutions (turkey for chicken, additional bell pepper, Rotel for the salsa, omission of cayenne) but this recipe was VERY nice and easily made.  We had no trouble with soupiness.  A terrific way to use up some of our Thanksgiving leftovers.  We'll be making this one again!

really wonderful! i did tweak it a bit tho...i used a pound and a half of chicken and 3 cups of rice (we love leftovers here). the one thing i would HIGHLY recommend is (if you are able to) go to a local Mexican restaurant and get FRESH salsa to use instead of Pace (you can really taste the preservatives in it).  what i did was brown the chicken with the onion and garlic (we don't like mushrooms so i didn't use them at all), then added about a cup of broth and a cup of salsa, let it simmer in that mixture for about a half hour. i then made a "roux" out of flour/water/chicken bouillon and added that to give the sauce a thicker consistency.  i then added the rice and let that simmer, stirring frequently, for about another 10 minutes...then last but not least added the cheese, i found this step REALLY made the dish wonderful and creamy. this will definitely stay in the rotation!  thanks so much!

This was a great last minute meal I threw together after a long day at work. I loved how simple it was to prepare. I realized half way through, though that I was out of salsa so I subbed 2 cups of diced tomatoes and spiced it up with some shredded pepper jack cheese. Thanks for sharing.

This was super easy compared to making traditional Mexican Rice.  You can really do anything to this recipe, which is great.  The only complaint is that I felt the rice mixture got too mushy by adding the chicken stock in the end.  I put in about a cup total just to dilute the spiciness of the salsa.  I will definitely make this again when in a time crunch!

Thanks, Spike! I threw this together for lunch to use up leftover salsa (my own), and rice. I did not need the broth at all. It was very good and I will make it again! However, next time I will brown/cook the chicken (bite sized, not strips) then remove and start with onions, etc. I used pepper Jack (all I had) and I will do that on purpose next time. For our preferences I will skip the 'shrooms and use corn and black beans instead. I can't wait!! Hope you're well, Spike...:) /Tia

Very easy & quite good! I had leftover chicken & rice so it was really quick. Only change I will make next time is to add more of the vegetables. Wish I had this recipe when all my kids were little because of the ease & fabulous taste.

OMG - Followed the recipe exactly and preparation was easy & dish seasoned perfectly.  My first bite did't include chicken and I thought I was in heaven. . .added a bite of chicken and yes it was heaven.  I'm trying to cut back on meat in the diet - this would be a delicious meal w/o the chicken (just use 1 lb mushrooms), but then we'd have to rename it.  Thanks so much for sharing!
Very good and super easy! Thank you I will make this again.

Loved it!!  Made subtle substitutions (pepper jack for regular, chili powder, which is cumin and cayenne, plus a few others) and added an 8oz can of tomato sauce because my salsa was on the watery/fresh side.  SUPER EASY, super tasty....can't wait to make it again.  THANKS!
Delicious! I have made this a few times now and the recipe never fails. I only use about one cup of chicken broth and like to add black beans. Quick clean up too which is always a plus! :)
I followed this recipe pretty loosely, but it turned out great.  Thanks for the post!

This turned out so good! We really enjoyed everything about it. I used homemade salsa that I wanted to finish up and taco sauce, baby bella mushrooms, pepper jack cheese, a 1/4 cup of chopped cilantro only needed about a cup of broth and added about a 1/4 cup of sour cream at the end just because I'm cleaning out the fridge and wanted to use it up.I loved the mushrooms in this recipe, I would never have thought to added them to a dish like this. I think I'll try making it with this again using double the mushroom and no chicken just to see if it would work as a meatless meal. I found this recipe because I wanted to use up some leftover cooked rice and ended finding a real keeper recipe. Thanks for sharing.

Excellent one-pot meal the whole family enjoyed. I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs because we prefer them over breasts. I used Adobo Seasoning with Cumin and eliminated the salt and cumin. Added ground black pepper to taste I didn't use the cayenne pepper either because my salsa had just the right amount of heat without adding to it. We made this into a full meal by serving with pinto beans and tortillas. This made for a delicious dinner and was so quick and easy to prepare and cleanup was a breeze. My kinda meal. Thanks for sharing. It'll be made again because it received all thumbs up around our table.

YUMMY!!!  I had some leftover chicken that I didnt know what to do with, so I browsed and had everything this called for. It was soo good and my kids even had seconds! This was perfect for this 20 degree temperature.

This was delicious and perfect for a 14 degree cold night. It was too cold to go to the grocery so since I did not have a jalapeno pepper I substituted 1/8 tsp. red ground cayenne pepper. I did not add any salt and only about 1/2 tsp. black pepper. Also no garnishes so I ate it with Breton whole wheat crackers. It hit the spot.  DELICIOUS!!

A whole meal in a bowl. This is so easy and so tasty. This is going into the regular rotation at our house. I didn't have any jalapeno pepper, so I just used a regular yellow pepper, which still added some spice. I added some carrots to bring some extra nutrition and they fit in well with the flavors. Thanks for sharing!
This was great!!  I agree, the fajita marinated chicken made all the difference.  We will make this over and over again!!

5 Stars...Easy to make and bursting with flavor. Friends loved it.  As chicken finished cooking, removed from pan and tented with aluminun foil. This was pretty darn good! I wasn't sure why we had to marinate the onions but not the bell peppers but I followed the directions. Not bad, *RACH*!

Very easy to make and nicely flavored. I did reduce the ranch dressing and up the sour cream which made it a bit thicker.  I did completely deseed the jalapenos.  We used this as a dip and also on fajitas.  Thank you Kerrie for sharing your recipe!
Very close to the dip served at Chuy's.  Easy to make.  It is better after it is chilled overnight.

Outstanding. I simmered the pulled pork in bottled verde (tomatillo) salsa. Then I wrapped it in burrito sized flour tortillas with Mexican rice, cheese, home made guacamole and sour cream. I had left overs and look forward to having this again in a few days. Thanks for sharing.
Exceedingly refreshing...fruity with a bit of tang! Yummy!!!
tased fantastic. My children loved it. I vl b repeating this recipe on next sunday as some guests are expected

Deeeelicious! The perfect side to any Mexican dish.  And easy too.

This was good! I made it almost exactly as the recipe stated, but I left out the cilantro  and butter, and then just sprinkled the corn with cayenne pepper just before serving. I loved the flavor and the firmness the kernals retained from cooking them this way!

I like to eat mine with chili pepper, real mayo and lemon pepper (don't knock it till you try it!!  MUY BUENO!!
Great side for a barbeque, family loved it.  I used a jalapeno pepper and we ate this plain with no toppings, just fresh limes.

Delicious! Normally I just coat my corn on the cob with butter, but I thought I'd give this a try since lime, chili and cilantro are some of my favorite flavors. This was sooooooooo good. I laid the ears of corn separately in pieces of foil and squeezed lime directly on the corn, sprinkled the spices and then sprayed with I can't believe its not butter and sealed the foil around the ear and grilled until hot. It was wonderful!

I do however think this recipe sounds really good and will definitely try it.

The cornmeal/bread crumb combination gives a lovely crunchy crust  and  the chili /garlic powder  a nice kick to the chicken.  the Jalapeno Cilantro Cream is just right. Oh yes! This is a great recipe!  I bought the chicken prepared (butterflied)and ready to go..nice and quick dish on a week night!  We loved the flavors in the sauce! Served it with rice (won't mention because of contest) what a wonderful meal.

We really enjoyed this SUPER easy and tasty dish! I had everything on hand which made it so much easier. I added some onion powder and really that was the only thing I did different! Thanks Susie!

I LOVED this! I do think the batter for the chicken could use a little more spiciness but that is just a preference. The crispiness and moistness of the chicken were wonderful and the sauce is absolutely amazing. I will be making this again.Thanks for the recipe
This is great, I have made it several times.  Lately, I have been baking it in a 9 x13.  Put olive oil in the bottom and flip it half way thru.  I do 400 degrees for about 35 minutes.

So before I made this recipe, I made the jalapeno cilantro cream sauce twice. The first sauce I made as directed and served it with tacos and burritos in place of ordinary sour cream. I let the sauce sit in the fridge for 3 hours to let the flavors blend. While I thought it was good, it wasn't quite hot enough for our tastes. In fairness we do like VERY spicy food. The second time I made the sauce to top baked potatoes, I made it as directed but left half of the jalapeno's seeds in hoping for more hot. It was much better but still not hot enough. The third time was when I made the fiesta chicken. This time I made as directed but used 1 jalapeno, 1 habanero, and one half of a hatch green chili (no seeds from any). It was the best sauce so far. For the chicken I made as directed except I just used store bought breadcrumbs. I also used 1/2 tablespoon New Mexico Red chili powder and 1/2 tablespoon McCormick chili powder. The chicken came out awesome and paired so well with the cream sauce. Since this is such a good recipe, I must check out other recipes posted by Susie. Thanks.
Turned out great, served with  baked sweet potatoes and Mexican Kale salad.

Oh my goodness, this is a sensational recipe for chicken. I had to make a couple of little changes. I didn't have garlic powder on hand, so used a garlic–ginger paste to cover both ingredients. Because my pieces were quite thick, I fried them for 12 minutes (6 a side) and then finished them in the oven. A truly wonderful recipe that will be repeated often.

We loved, loved, loved this chicken. We all enjoyed the crispiness and flavor of the chicken coating. Three out of four of us used the jalapeno cilantro cream to top the chicken. It was delicious - a wonderful combination of flavors. Made in loving memory of SusieD.
This is a great chicken entree which I will be adding to my recipe go-to list. Loved the flavors and the cream sauce really compliments this chicken so well.
We enjoyed the flavor of this dish.  I didn't cook it quite as long as the recipe called for because the sides started to burn.  I would definitely try this again as an oven casserole.
Very nice served with lettuce, tomato, carrot, Cheese etc salad. Similar to a lasagne. Will cook again

We used the hot enchilada sauce and I cut the montery cheese down to half to decrease the cals. Also used low fat soup. Great recipe, plan on making this one often! These were really good.  We served them with spanish rise.  I think in the end we all agreed that we'd rather have enchiladas but these were a nice change.

Just realized I hadn't reviewed these yet.  My family loves these!  Nothing like my favorite two things together...Mexican and Pasta.  These freeze great also, so I usually do extra and put those in the freezer.  Great taste!  Easy to put together!  Thanks so much!

looneytunesfan, this is terrific! Thanks for posting this recipe, which included all the ingredients I had. This recipe was delicious! A nice change from regular rice. I used my food processor to prepare the ingredients instead of a blender. I also sauteed a green pepper on the side and added it in at the last minute before serving. This will be a regular on our menu.

I liked the speedy process! This was indeed a simple and easy to make recipe and I appreciated having something so quick and hearty for dinner on a very cold night! DH was able to explain that this was in fact ok and edible! LOL! Lots of hot salsa and sour cream on the side went very nicely; thanks for posting and I'm looking forward to eating the leftovers!

Delicious and easy recipe. DH said it was one of the best Mexican dishes he has ever had.  I used refried beans with green chilis mixed in them and did add some salsa with the picante sauce, other than that did not change a thing! Thank you for posting!
This was so easy and fast to prepare.  Very good!  The whole family enjoyed this.  Thanks.
So delicious, and so perfect for the nights when you just feel like throwing everything in a pan.  :)

Seven beer guzzling poker players give seven hairy thumbs up to this delicious and nutritious finger food.
